Initial salary offer corrections: admins can correct annual salary while the employee is onboarding and repeat the classification review against the proposed amount. Active employees and approved/finalized payroll remain protected from undated salary replacement. Changes to salary, role or overtime classification reopen the wage notice and mark its document for reverification; the complete prior acknowledgment is preserved in the audit record before the working response is cleared. Unchanged terms preserve the current acknowledgment. The wage-notice UI now displays current role, compensation, overtime classification, hire date, location and pay-schedule text using the same terms helper that records the signed response. The portal sends the displayed terms with submission and rejects a mismatch if an admin changed them while the page was open. Existing API clients that omit displayed terms continue to acknowledge the current server terms. Real API tests verify amount correction, prior-response preservation, re-signing revised terms and active-employee protection. All 107 backend tests passed before the final displayed-terms check; all four focused review tests passed afterward. The browser correction/employee display test passed; final signature submission is also covered in its extended workflow. Dated post-onboarding compensation changes and automatic pay-schedule text in hiring terms remain active work.

46. Initial offer corrections require a fresh employee wage acknowledgment when salary, title or overtime classification changes. The previous signed response is retained in audit history. This correction path applies only to salary amounts during onboarding; subsequent pay changes require dated compensation history and notice delivery. Existing signed documents remain retained, but the working wage-notice task must be reverified for the new terms.

Hiring notices now follow schedule history: onboarding packets and signed wage terms derive their pay-schedule description from the employer's actual configured schedule. Existing hires use the current employer-local date; future hires use their hire date when selecting a scheduled version. Cancelled versions are excluded. Weekly/biweekly notices identify period length, anchor and payment lag; semimonthly notices identify nominal payday numbers; all identify the preceding-bank-business-day rule. The signed response preserves a structured schedule snapshot alongside the displayed description. Stale portal terms are rejected after a schedule change while prior signed terms remain retained. The obsolete freeform pay-schedule description input was removed from Employer setup; previously saved text is retained in stored policy but no longer overrides the schedule in new hiring notices. Tests cover frequency descriptions, current versus future-hire selection, cancellation, stored signed snapshots and stale submission rejection. All 110 backend tests passed. The browser hiring flow configured weekly payroll, corrected salary, displayed the actual weekly notice and signed it successfully. TypeScript, scoped lint and whitespace checks passed. Dated salary changes and broader requirements remain unfinished.

47. Hiring terms use the schedule applicable on the later of today's employer-local date and the hire date. Published future schedule versions therefore apply to hires starting after the transition. This describes the configured schedule and does not replace separate advance-notice delivery and schedule-change receipt workflows. The pay-calendar configuration is authoritative over legacy manually typed schedule descriptions.

Dated salary changes: Pay setup & leave now schedules a future salary agreement with its classification review, written-notice delivery date/reference and reason. The first change preserves an opening record from the hiring salary. Records append chronologically; the effective date must be the beginning of an open generated payroll period, and any change involving nonexempt classification must also begin a workweek. Decreases use the existing conservative frequency-based notice intervals. Approved/finalized future payroll blocks changes. Payroll selects the salary review at period start, current admin/employee displays select today's version, and onboarding terms use the current salary record. An interior salary change caused by a later calendar edit blocks calculation rather than blending agreements. Generic profile responses retain current salary presentation; initial review cannot overwrite an established salary history. API tests verify scope, date boundaries, opening-history preservation, earlier versus later payroll amounts, duplicate rejection and calendar conflicts. All 111 backend tests passed. Browser tests scheduled an exempt raise, reloaded history, and retained the nonexempt payroll-review flow; TypeScript, scoped lint and whitespace checks passed. Cancellation of future salary changes and employee receipt acknowledgment are not implemented yet and remain active work, along with the broader requirement audit.

48. Dated salary agreements begin on complete pay periods; nonexempt changes also begin a workweek so one workweek never mixes salary agreements. The future calendar must be generated before scheduling a change. Decreases require a conservative 7/14/16/31-day advance written-notice interval for weekly/biweekly/semimonthly/monthly schedules, matching the existing hourly change policy. Mid-period salary changes, retroactive changes and alternative prorating methods require additional correction functionality.

Future salary-change cancellation: admin salary history now offers cancellation only for the latest future active change. Cancellation preserves the record and stores actor, time, reason, written-notice date and reference. It restores the preceding salary agreement; opening/effective agreements and changes used by approved/finalized payroll cannot be cancelled. Restoring a lower salary or removing nonexempt overtime eligibility requires the conservative schedule-based notice interval. Cancellation notices cannot predate the original delivery. The transaction includes the audit record; a synthetic audit failure proves rollback. Scope, invalid confirmation, payroll locks, duplicate cancellation, restored payroll amounts and replacement scheduling on the same date are covered by real API tests. The browser schedules, cancels and reloads history. All 111 backend tests passed, as did both salary browser workflows, TypeScript, scoped lint and whitespace checks. Employee salary-change and cancellation receipt acknowledgment remains active work.

49. Cancelling a future salary change restores its immediate predecessor rather than deleting history. Cancellation uses the schedule effective on the originally planned change date for advance-notice requirements. A cancellation that restores a lower amount, or restores exempt status in place of planned nonexempt status, receives the same conservative notice interval as a decrease. This is a protective implementation assumption; special contractual obligations and retroactive corrections need separate handling.

Employee salary notice receipts: the Pay statements portal now lists salary changes and cancellations, with separate receipt acknowledgments. Employee responses contain only the public agreement terms and delivery dates; internal duties assessments, references and reasons remain private to admins. Receipt snapshots and timestamps are preserved independently for the change and cancellation. Retries return the original receipt without adding audit events, and salary cancellation/acknowledgment share the employer lock. Cancelled changes cannot receive new original-change acknowledgments; former employees may acknowledge records. Admin salary history displays both receipt statuses. Tests verify employee scoping, private-field filtering, confirmation, duplicate retries, cancellation state, former-employee access and rollback when audit insertion fails. All 112 backend tests passed. The browser scheduled a change, redeemed an employee invitation, acknowledged the change, cancelled it as admin, acknowledged the cancellation as employee, and verified both admin receipt statuses. Both salary browser workflows passed; mobile receipt layout was inspected. TypeScript, scoped lint and whitespace checks passed. These receipts record delivery acknowledgment without waiving wage rights. The full payroll goal remains unfinished, including bonus regular-rate allocation, broader compensation policies, corrections, year-end outputs and production integration verification.

50. Salary notice acknowledgments record receipt, not consent to waive wage rights. Change and cancellation receipts remain distinct, including when the employee has left employment. The preserved receipt shows the notice as received, while current notice listings show cancellation state. Actual delivery dates and internal delivery evidence remain admin inputs; no real messages were sent by these tests.

Reviewed annual bonuses: Pay setup & leave now records a single annual lump-sum bonus against an explicit open pay period, with discretionary/nondiscretionary classification and evidence. Discretionary review requires retained discretion over payment and amount plus no prior promise or employee expectation. Bonuses created through this path do not recur in later periods. The UI supplies a request reference; retries with the same details return the original record, while different details conflict. Payroll review shows the bonus classification. Native withholding combines concurrent regular wages and bonus for federal tax, and calculates Maryland regular-pay withholding plus the annual lump-sum rate for the supported 3.20% local jurisdiction. Statement items preserve public classification metadata while excluding internal review evidence. Earned/promised or unclassified bonuses for nonexempt employees now explicitly require workweek allocation, including legacy hourly bonuses that previously relied only on the withholding blocker. All 114 backend tests passed before the final retry refinement; focused bonus tax/finalization/retry tests passed afterward. The browser creation/preview flow passed, mobile review was inspected, and TypeScript, scoped lint and whitespace checks passed. Earned-bonus overtime allocation, other supplemental wage types, off-cycle payment and broader goal requirements remain unfinished.

51. A discretionary bonus requires all three factual conditions in the Department of Labor's guidance: discretion over payment, discretion over amount until near the end of the period, and no prior promise or expectation. Its name alone is insufficient. Source: https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fact-sheets/56c-bonuses. Earned or promised bonuses stay blocked for nonexempt payroll until their additional regular-rate overtime is allocated.

52. The implemented automatic bonus method is for an annual lump-sum bonus paid concurrently with regular wages. Federal withholding uses aggregate wages, following https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15. Maryland's 2026 guide specifies 6.50% state plus the applicable highest local rate for annual lump-sum bonuses; the currently supported 3.20% local configuration therefore uses 9.70% on the bonus: https://www.marylandcomptroller.gov/content/dam/mdcomp/tax/instructions/withholding/2026/withholding-guide.pdf. Maryland-exempt elections, bonus-only payments, pretax deductions, other supplemental types, and cumulative total wages above $1 million require additional handling. Using total wages for the $1 million gate is deliberately conservative until separate supplemental-wage YTD tracking exists.

Earned-bonus allocation preview: Pay setup & leave now calculates a reviewed proportional-hours allocation for an earned annual bonus. The calculator includes approved time from the complete workweeks around the earning dates and counts only the earning dates in the allocation numerator. Additional overtime uses the exact allocated fraction, full weekly worked hours, and half the bonus regular-rate increment for hours above 40, rounded once per week. Displayed bonus allocations use largest remainders so cents reconcile to the bonus total. Evidence retains each time-entry slice. Closed-week, scoped employee, unresolved time, overnight break, invalid classification and salary-review checks prevent an unsupported preview. A still-open entry beginning before the earning range remains visible to those checks. The mobile UI displays each weekly allocation and resets when dates, amount, employee or method confirmation change. This checkpoint is calculation-only: it does not yet persist the allocation as a reviewed bonus agreement, reconcile historical payroll coverage, or add bonus overtime to a payable run. Existing nonexempt bonus approval blockers remain until that integration is complete.

53. Proportional earned hours are one supported earned-bonus allocation method, not a default interpretation of every bonus agreement. The admin must verify that the agreement supports this allocation; production, equal-week, percentage-of-total-earnings and other methods still need their own implementation. Full weekly hours, including hours outside a partial earning period, form the additional-overtime denominator. Only statutory overtime hours receive the additional half-rate premium. This follows the workweek allocation framework in 29 CFR 778.209 and the DOL interpretation at https://www.dol.gov/sites/dolgov/files/WHD/legacy/files/2020_01_07_01_FLSA.pdf. Historical time must be complete and approved; this preview alone is not proof that original wages or earlier bonus premiums were paid.

Validation for the earned-bonus preview checkpoint: all 116 payroll backend tests passed; the final weekly-boundary and reviewed-exemption tightening passed the two focused allocator/API tests afterward. Both annual-bonus browser scenarios passed and the 390px allocation card was visually inspected. TypeScript, scoped React lint, whitespace checks and production build passed. No external payment, tax filing, deployment or QuickBooks posting was executed. The hire-to-pay goal remains active, with earned-bonus payout integration and the broader scope gaps above still outstanding.

Earned-bonus saved review: recording an earned annual bonus now requires valid earning dates, explicit proportional-hours agreement verification, and the fingerprint from the internal allocation preview. Under the employer/employee transaction locks, the server recalculates the allocation and rejects stale time or classification inputs before saving. The earning period cannot end after the selected pay period. The saved adjustment and its transactional audit retain the full allocation and supporting time slices. Identical request retries return the original record; changed earning details reject that request key, and audit failure rolls back the adjustment. The browser submits only its current preview, removes it when inputs change, and clears final confirmation when the allocation is changed or recalculated. This supersedes the previous checkpoint's missing persistence; historical wage coverage and actual additional-overtime payment integration remain outstanding.

54. An admin's allocation review applies to the exact earning dates and time records shown at review. Changed records require a new calculation and confirmation before saving; the system must not silently reinterpret the agreement or substitute newer hours under the old approval. The saved evidence is a review record, not a historical-payment reconciliation.

Saved-review validation: all 117 payroll backend tests passed, including stale-time rejection, unchanged retry, changed retry, saved allocation evidence, retained approval blocker, and audit rollback. Both annual-bonus browser scenarios passed; the earned-bonus scenario now saves through the UI and inspects the database record. TypeScript, scoped React lint and whitespace checks passed. No production payment, filing, deployment or external posting occurred. The full goal remains active.

Earned-bonus payment integration: payroll now recalculates each saved proportional-hours bonus, checks its saved input fingerprint, and reconciles every historical time slice to exactly one finalized payroll calculation. Historical snapshot hours must reconcile to the wage row, and snapshot gross must equal stored regular, overtime and other taxable wages. Historical payments must precede the current period and have a payment date no later than the current payment date. Current-period work is paid by the current run; future-period work, missing/duplicate historical coverage, imported history without time reconciliation, and changed allocation inputs block approval. Successful reconciliation adds a separate BONUS_OVERTIME taxable earning without changing worked hours, leave accrual, or the original base-overtime record. The draft/approval fingerprint includes normalized allocation and payment coverage fields, avoiding JSONB object-order differences. Finalized statements preserve the allocation and current/historical payment evidence and print additional bonus overtime as a separate earning. Admin payroll review displays the earning dates and additional amount. This supersedes earlier calculation-only and saved-review-only limitations for the supported annual earned-bonus path.

55. Each earned bonus is a distinct award with its own additional overtime, allocated to complete workweeks. Original wages must be in the current payroll or internally finalized with matching time records; imported payment totals alone do not establish that coverage. Bonus-only off-cycle payments, other allocation methods and imported workweek reconciliation remain required extensions. Changed reviewed time requires pausing the outdated bonus and recording a newly reviewed replacement; paid bonuses are not silently rewritten.

56. Additional bonus overtime is recorded as taxable overtime wages alongside the regular payment. Federal withholding aggregates all current taxable earnings; Maryland's regular percentage calculation includes this overtime, while the annual bonus principal receives the separately supported 9.70% lump-sum rate. Treating the overtime correction as wages is the implementation interpretation of the Maryland guide's inclusion of back pay and retroactive increases; the guide does not give a separate example specifically for overtime attributable to a bonus. See https://www.marylandcomptroller.gov/content/dam/mdcomp/tax/instructions/withholding/2026/withholding-guide.pdf (taxable wages, percentage formulas, annual bonus). Existing year, locality, pretax, concurrent regular-wage and high-income restrictions still apply.

Earned-bonus payment validation: all 121 payroll backend tests passed. Added cases cover current hourly, historical hourly and historical nonexempt salary bonus payment through real approval/finalization, saved payment coverage, statement earning lines, federal/Maryland withholding values, stale records, and missing/duplicate/inconsistent historical evidence. Both bonus browser scenarios passed, including the saved earned bonus appearing in payroll review with its payable overtime and earning dates; the 390px payment review was visually inspected. TypeScript, scoped React lint, whitespace checks and production build passed. No real payment, filing, deployment or QuickBooks posting was performed.


Shorter exempt workweeks: salary classification review now records seven daily leave-basis minute amounts, Sunday through Saturday. The reviewed week must total more than zero and at most 40 hours. Initial and dated reviews preserve these terms; a dated review without new schedule inputs inherits the latest active agreement. Salary calculations use each date's reviewed hours within employment, retain the full scheduled salary, preserve actual recorded work separately, and freeze the workweek in the statement and approval fingerprint. Hiring wage terms include the schedule, a changed initial schedule reopens the acknowledgment, and employee salary-change notices and receipts include the announced daily hours. The admin form supports shorter and weekend workweeks and shows the weekly total. Existing reviews without schedule data retain the legacy eight-hour Monday–Friday basis.

57. Maryland exempt leave accrual assumes 40 hours per workweek unless the normal workweek is shorter; the shorter week then applies. The implementation records a recurring seven-day distribution to allocate that weekly basis across payroll boundaries and initial/final employment dates. For normal weeks above 40 hours, admins distribute the statutory 40-hour basis across normal workdays. Holidays and paid leave preserve this assumed basis. Salary and exemption salary thresholds are not reduced when the leave basis is shorter. Rotating multiweek schedules and shorter nonexempt salary agreements remain separate work. Source: https://mgaleg.maryland.gov/mgawebsite/Laws/StatuteText?article=gle&section=3-1304&enactments=false, subsection (e).


Shorter-workweek validation: all 124 payroll backend tests passed. Salary payment tests cover standard weekly/biweekly schedules, a 30-hour week including Sunday, a 12-hour first week with no accrual, and following-week eligibility once combined assumed hours reach 24. Salary remains unchanged, and finalized snapshots preserve the reviewed leave basis. Hiring notice tests verify schedule changes reopen acknowledgment. Both salary browser scenarios passed, including the exact daily schedule in employee notices; a further exempt-salary run captured and verified the seven-day form at 390px. The form, payroll review and employee notice were visually inspected. TypeScript, scoped React lint, whitespace checks and production build passed. The full goal remains active, with no external payment, filing, posting or deployment performed.

Shorter nonexempt salary agreements: classification review now accepts a fixed weekly salary agreement from 0.25 through 40 hours in quarter-hour increments. Legacy fixed-40 confirmations retain their meaning; they cannot authorize a shorter agreement. The minimum-wage gate uses the agreed annual hours. Salary payroll pays the unchanged scheduled base plus straight-time wages for actual hours above the agreement through 40, then time-and-a-half for actual hours above 40. Carried prior-period workweek hours reduce the remaining threshold once. Additional straight-time earnings flow through taxable gross, withholding, saved snapshots and statement lines with hours and rate basis. Actual work minutes remain unchanged for time reporting and leave. Hiring terms and employee salary-change notices disclose covered weekly hours; initial agreement changes reopen the hiring acknowledgment. Dated changes and cancellations also check whether the regular hourly rate decreases, including when salary is unchanged but covered hours increase.

58. Nonexempt salary agreements cover a fixed number of weekly hours, never a variable/fluctuating workweek. The regular hourly rate is annual salary divided by 52 and by agreed weekly hours; actual hours beyond that agreement receive additional straight-time pay through 40 and 1.5 times the regular rate thereafter. No salary deductions are made for weeks below the agreed hours or initial/final partial periods. Additional pay retains fractional precision until final cent rounding. The same advance-notice interval already used for salary decreases applies when increasing contracted hours reduces the regular hourly rate. Sources: 29 CFR 778.113, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2019-title29-vol3/pdf/CFR-2019-title29-vol3-sec778-111.pdf, and the DOL explanation at https://www.dol.gov/sites/dolgov/files/WHD/fww/FR-FWW.pdf. Rotating workweeks and agreements covering more than 40 hours remain separate methods.


Short fixed-salary validation: all 129 payroll backend tests passed. Added cases cover weekly/biweekly 30-hour agreements through approval and finalization, extra straight-time and overtime earnings, unchanged actual-hour leave accrual, crossed-period thresholds, invalid agreement hours, and advance notice when contracted hours reduce the regular rate. Both salary browser scenarios passed, including entering a 30-hour agreement and reviewing $500 additional straight-time plus $600 overtime on 48 worked hours; the mobile review was visually inspected. Final statement-detail refinements passed all four nonexempt salary payment/PDF tests afterward. TypeScript, scoped React lint, whitespace checks and production build passed. No actual payment, filing, deployment or QuickBooks posting was performed; the broad goal remains active.


Final-period payroll tracking: former employees now have an internal review card showing the stored employment end date, corresponding regular payday, payroll run state, payment timing, and unresolved time/requests. The card opens the exact payroll period. Missing or ambiguous calendar coverage remains unverified rather than generating an unsupported deadline. The automation refreshes a deduplicated warning when payment confirmation is due within seven days or overdue, configuration/evidence needs review, or unresolved requests remain; complete recorded payroll dismisses the warning, and a later request reopens it. A finalized run without a net amount or payment confirmation remains flagged. The existing termination status update now records the employer-local date instead of the database's default calendar date. Returning-worker identity continuity still requires its own workflow; this checkpoint does not implement rehiring.

59. For the currently supported Maryland deadline, wages for the last employment period remain due on the regular payday that would have applied without termination. The tracker uses the existing payroll calendar and separately identifies actual recorded payment after that date. An overdue confirmation means the internal record is missing, not proof that an external payment was never made. Finalized regular payroll is not a certificate that all separation obligations are settled: earned bonuses, expenses, later corrections, and any vacation payout required by the communicated employment policy require review. Missing calendar coverage, other states and zero-wage closure need explicit resolution. Source: https://labor.maryland.gov/labor/wagepay/wppayonterm.shtml.

Final-pay tracking validation: all 130 payroll backend tests passed. Focused tests cover facility scoping, missing calendar, overdue confirmation, unresolved time, alert idempotence, late recorded payment, dismissal/reopening and missing payment evidence. The final-pay browser workflow passed, including exact-period navigation; revised confirmation wording was rerun and the mobile card visually inspected. TypeScript, scoped React lint, whitespace checks and production build passed. No real payment or external filing/posting was performed. The full goal remains active.

Unused vacation/PTO payout preview: the separation page now accepts exact payout minutes, an explicitly reviewed hourly rate, and confirmation of the communicated policy and unused-vacation treatment. It calculates cents using integer arithmetic, rejects negative/insufficient balances and unsupported leave types, and retains scoped ledger evidence with a fingerprint for subsequent payment review. Available minutes include posted credits through the employer-local current date and all recorded future deductions; future positive credits are excluded. The preview resets when inputs change and leaves the leave ledger and payroll unchanged. Reservation, cancellation, native tax/payment integration and the matching final ledger reduction remain unfinished; this is not yet a payable cashout.

60. The initial leave-cashout method is for unused vacation recorded as PTO, with the applicable payout rate and communicated policy reviewed by an admin. The rate is not inferred from salary or exemption leave-basis hours. Future grants are not available for immediate payout, and existing future leave deductions remain committed pending review. The ledger must reconcile before calculation. Statutory sick leave and attendance incentives require their own policy/treatment path. Sources: Maryland termination-pay guidance at https://labor.maryland.gov/labor/wagepay/wppayonterm.shtml and DOL guidance distinguishing unused paid leave from regular-rate earnings at https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fact-sheets/56a-regular-rate. No tax calculation or payment is produced by this preview checkpoint.


PTO payout preview validation: all 132 payroll backend tests passed. Added tests cover cent rounding, invalid amounts/rates, insufficient balance, policy confirmation, scoped ledger access, future credit/debit treatment, changed-evidence fingerprints and absence of payroll mutations. The separation browser scenario passed with exact-minute input, $191.63 for 450 minutes at $25.55/hour, calculation reset after editing, and unchanged leave balance; the mobile card was visually inspected. TypeScript, scoped React lint, whitespace checks and production build passed. Reservation and payment posting remain active work, along with the broader goal requirements.


PTO reservation and payment settlement: administrators can reserve reviewed PTO against an open employment-period payroll, see reservation history, and cancel with a reason before payroll approval. Idempotency keys and employer-level serialization prevent duplicate or competing reservations. Available leave excludes reserved minutes; database constraints prevent ledger changes from spending them. Payroll preview and saved snapshots show payout minutes, rate and cents. Finalization inserts the corresponding PTO debits and marks reservations paid in the same audited transaction. Failed audit/settlement rolls back both; paid payouts and their ledger entries are immutable. Statement snapshots retain the payout identity and reviewed rate without internal policy notes. The final-pay alert remains open while unpaid reservations exist.

61. A PTO reservation commits already available leave without immediately debiting the ledger. Cancellation releases the commitment; only confirmed payroll finalization creates the debit. Each request rounds its own payout to cents, so splitting a payout can differ by a cent from a single combined request. Payout terms cannot be edited after reservation: cancel and replace before approval. The payment date cannot precede the date the reservation was recorded. Later payments after an already finalized final period still require the unfinished off-cycle workflow.

62. Reviewed unused PTO cashout is taxable compensation with no worked-hour, overtime-hour or sick-leave accrual credit. The first native withholding path aggregates cashout with concurrent regular wages under the existing verified 2026 Maryland-resident/3.20%-local elections. Federal supplemental-wage handling follows the aggregate method; cumulative total wages above $1 million conservatively require separately verified treatment. Standalone cashout also requires separately verified withholding until off-cycle methods are implemented. Maryland vacation cashout is treated as wages under the ordinary tables; applying the annual-bonus flat rate to vacation cashout is not assumed. Sources: IRS Publication 15, section 7 and vacation pay, https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15; Maryland 2026 Employer Withholding Guide, taxable wages including vacation allowances, https://www.marylandcomptroller.gov/content/dam/mdcomp/tax/instructions/withholding/2026/withholding-guide.pdf. The Maryland cashout/table application is an implementation interpretation of the wages guidance.

PTO settlement validation: all 135 backend regression tests passed before adding two extra scenarios; all seven focused payout tests then passed, including concurrent requests and both hourly and nonexempt salary finalization. Tests cover scope, rounding, retries, insufficient balance, reservation cancellation, immutable terms and paid ledger, blocked changes after approval, multi-payout settlement, audit rollback, unchanged worked/accrual hours, aggregate withholding and frozen statements. The browser flow passed on mobile with reservation/cancellation and payroll calculation review. TypeScript, scoped React lint, whitespace checks and production build passed. The itemized payout statement was rendered and visually checked. No real money, tax filing or QuickBooks posting occurred. The full goal remains active.


Off-cycle expense reimbursement: Payroll runs now offers a separate payment for an approved, tax-reviewed employee expense, including after employment ends. The draft reserves the existing expense adjustment so regular payroll excludes it. Voiding the draft releases that assignment and permits a replacement. Approval/finalization recheck the approved amount, receipt/review evidence, employee, processing period and payment date. Competing off-cycle runs and already committed regular reimbursement evidence block another payment; legacy aggregate reimbursement records without sufficient item detail require reconciliation. Expense-only payroll carries zero wages, taxes, deductions and leave accrual, cannot accept withholding overrides, and does not lock regular timesheets or mark the regular pay period paid. The employee statement identifies an expense reimbursement and its processing period. Final-pay tracking retains an alert for approved expenses until payment is recorded. The QuickBooks journal debits reimbursement expense and credits payroll clearing.

63. The first off-cycle path covers approved, substantiated, non-taxable employee expense reimbursement under the tax treatment already verified by the hiring/payroll admin. It does not treat undocumented allowances, advances, bonuses, cashout or wage corrections as reimbursement. The payment date cannot precede the expense approval date. The existing assigned payroll window serves as the processing period; no wages for that period are paid again. Actual payment still uses the existing confirmation workflow. IRS accountable-plan guidance is the basis for treating a qualifying reimbursement as non-wage compensation: [Publication 15, employee business expense reimbursements](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15).

Off-cycle reimbursement validation: 138 backend regression tests passed before the last focused refinements. Five focused tests then passed, covering expense settlement, zero accrual, former-employee eligibility, duplicate prevention, void/replacement, changed review evidence, scope, incorrect tax overrides, legacy payment evidence, coexistence with regular payroll/time, final-pay expense tracking, itemized statements and balanced QuickBooks journal generation. The browser scenario completed preview, draft, review, approval and payment confirmation; the mobile form and reimbursement PDF were visually inspected. TypeScript (production build), scoped React lint, whitespace checks and build passed. No real payment or QuickBooks posting occurred. Taxable off-cycle wages, PTO cashout after a finalized period, retroactive time/pay corrections and the remaining full-goal requirements are still active work.

Implementation note for further off-cycle work: `payroll_run.run_kind` currently distinguishes REGULAR from OFF_CYCLE_REIMBURSEMENT. The latter deliberately has no workweek, wage, tax or leave-history effect. Adding taxable correction kinds must revisit the regular-only time/compensation, prior-workweek and leave-history predicates instead of copying the reimbursement exclusions. Every earning needs source identity, prior-payment reconciliation and year-to-date treatment before it can be paid through that path.

Legacy reimbursement coverage refinement: the off-cycle duplicate-payment guard now requires the entire regular reimbursement total to reconcile to uniquely identified expense items in exactly one employee snapshot. A single identified item no longer hides an unidentified remainder. Missing amounts, malformed amounts, duplicate expense identities, partial totals and duplicate employee snapshots block the new payment; a fully reconciled payment for different requests permits it. The expanded off-cycle integration test passed, including the existing approval/finalization flow and these legacy variants; whitespace checks passed. This strengthens payment evidence without completing taxable off-cycle payroll, which remains active work.

Standalone supplemental federal withholding foundation: added a 2026 calculator for eligible flat 22%, aggregate withholding after subtracting regular and earlier supplemental tax once, and the mandatory 37% portion above $1 million of supplemental wages. Integer-cent arithmetic handles flat-rate rounding. A separate payment-history reconciler classifies BONUS and LEAVE_PAYOUT as supplemental, treats the supported overtime/straight-time/paid-leave items as ordinary wages, reconciles taxable item totals to finalized employee records, and identifies qualifying current/prior-year regular federal withholding. Imported payment totals require allocation rather than being silently treated as regular wages. Reconciliation proves consistency of stored records; employer/common-control history completeness still requires an explicit review before the calculator may be used for payment.

64. Standalone supplemental wages will use an eligible federal flat method or a documented aggregate payroll basis. The portion above the statutory supplemental-wage threshold uses the mandatory rate without regard to W-4 exemption; ordinary aggregate wages honor a valid exemption. Prior-year regular withholding may establish flat-rate eligibility, while only the payment year's supplemental wages count toward its annual threshold. Regular payroll and prior supplemental withholding are subtracted once under aggregate treatment; excess prior withholding produces zero additional withholding, not an automatic refund. Source: [IRS Publication 15 (2026), section 7](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15). The calculation and evidence modules are not yet connected to the taxable off-cycle payment API/UI, Maryland standalone treatment, or FICA/employer-tax settlement.

Supplemental foundation validation: all seven new tests passed with the isolated PostgreSQL database enabled. Coverage includes 22% eligibility, threshold splits, mandatory excess despite exemption, repeated aggregate payments, rounding, invalid amounts/history, wage-class reconciliation, calendar-year filtering, employer scope and imported totals. Whitespace checks passed. This is foundation work; no taxable off-cycle payment was created or represented as complete.


Standalone discretionary annual bonus: administrators can record a new, separately reviewed annual lump-sum bonus for an active or former employee against an existing processing period, including a paid period. The run contains only that bonus. Its request reference prevents duplicate creation and rejects changed/replacement details under an already used reference. Audit failure rolls the whole creation back. Approval and finalization recheck payment history and tax inputs. Native federal treatment uses eligible flat 22% plus the mandatory excess rate, and Maryland uses the separately verified annual-bonus rate of 9.70% for the supported residence. FICA, Additional Medicare, FUTA and Maryland UI consume actual year-to-date wages. A paid bonus in the same processing period is included when subsequent regular payroll calculates wage caps. No regular wages, work hours or leave accrual are repeated. Pending standalone bonuses remain visible in final-pay tracking. The statement identifies a bonus payment and freezes the supplemental tax breakdown; private review/history notes stay out of employee statements.

65. The first taxable standalone payment path is an annual lump-sum discretionary bonus, requiring explicit confirmation of employer discretion over amount and payment, no prior promise/expectation, complete employer/related-employer payment history, and the applicable Maryland annual-bonus rate. The 9.70% rate requires review of the highest applicable local rate for the residence, not simply assuming the ordinary paycheck rate always applies. The processing period is a reference for the statement; the actual payment date controls tax history and reporting. This path does not reclassify earned bonuses, vacation cashout or wage corrections as discretionary pay. Native aggregate standalone withholding and earned off-cycle workweek settlement remain unfinished; other income-tax cases use the existing verified-calculation review where all other blockers are resolved. Sources: [IRS Publication 15, supplemental wages](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) and [Maryland 2026 Employer Withholding Guide, annual bonus instructions and 3.20% local table](https://www.marylandcomptroller.gov/content/dam/mdcomp/tax/instructions/withholding/2026/withholding-guide.pdf).

Standalone bonus validation: 146 backend regression tests passed before the final refinements; four focused tests then passed, including three bonus scenarios plus final-pay tracking. Coverage includes hourly/former and salary employees, Social Security and Additional Medicare threshold crossings, subsequent supplemental history, regular payroll in the same processing period, no duplicate wages/accrual, request replay, changed request rejection, audit rollback, payment confirmation and frozen statements. The browser workflow passed through finalization with the state-rate attestation, and its mobile form and bonus statement PDF were visually inspected. TypeScript/production build, scoped React lint and whitespace checks passed. No real funds, filing or QuickBooks posting occurred. The full goal remains active.


Standalone earned annual bonus: the admin selects earned/promised classification, enters earning dates, reviews proportional-hours allocation and calculated additional overtime, then previews and saves a standalone payment. Every underlying time segment must reconcile to exactly one finalized regular wage payment, even when the selected processing period overlaps the earning dates. Duplicate employee snapshots, missing wage coverage and changed allocation inputs block settlement. The payment adds bonus principal and any additional overtime without repeating worked wages, hours or leave accrual. Both earnings count toward standalone federal supplemental history. Approval/finalization retain payment-order, year-to-date, audit and evidence checks. The frozen statement includes allocation and finalized wage coverage.

66. Earned standalone annual bonuses use the reviewed proportional-earned-hours method, with each full workweek closed and its underlying wages finalized before payment. Processing-period overlap does not establish wage payment. With no additional overtime, eligible federal supplemental and reviewed Maryland annual-bonus withholding calculate natively. With additional overtime, federal supplemental withholding includes both amounts, but the Maryland combination requires a separately verified calculation entered through the existing admin withholding review. This deliberately leaves native Maryland treatment of the combined payment unfinished instead of extending the annual-bonus rate to overtime without an established basis. The browser fixture's $11.00 Maryland withholding is synthetic test data, not a tax-table expectation. The full assumptions list remains subject to employer review.

Earned standalone validation: 149 backend tests passed before the final no-overtime fixture; six focused tests then passed, covering current/historical regular bonuses and standalone earned bonuses with/without overtime. Coverage includes matching-period payment proof, missing/duplicate snapshots, former employees, professional withholding approval gating, frozen evidence, supplemental history and no repeated accrual. Both standalone browser workflows passed through payment confirmation, with no page errors. Mobile visual inspection, TypeScript, scoped lint, production build and whitespace checks passed. No real payment, filing, deployment or accounting posting occurred. The full goal remains active.


Standalone PTO settlement: reservations now carry an immutable REGULAR or STANDALONE payment mode. Standalone reservations can reference a paid processing period and remain excluded from regular payroll calculations. An active or former employee can have unused vacation reserved under the reviewed policy, then a separate PTO payroll created from that exact reservation. Creation serializes under the employer lock, permits replay of identical details, rejects conflicting active payment details, and allows replacement after voiding the old run. Native eligible federal supplemental withholding, FICA and employer taxes consume reconciled payment-date history; state income tax currently requires the admin verified-calculation workflow. Approval rechecks the reservation and payment history. Finalization atomically posts its exact PTO debit, marks the reservation PAID, freezes the statement and records payment/audit history. Cancellation is blocked after its own payroll approval; an unrelated finalized regular run does not prevent cancellation of an unapproved standalone reservation.

67. Standalone vacation cashout uses an explicitly reviewed unused-vacation policy and payout rate; it is not paid time off taken during a workweek and adds no worked hours or sick accrual. Its processing period is a reference, while the actual payment date controls taxation and reporting and cannot precede reservation. The existing 2026 federal supplemental method applies where payment history establishes eligibility. Native state treatment for a standalone vacation payout remains unfinished, so a verified state calculation is required before approval rather than reusing the annual-bonus rate. Synthetic $8 state withholding in the test is a workflow fixture, not a tax expectation. Source: [IRS Publication 15, vacation pay and supplemental wages](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15).

Standalone PTO validation: 151 payroll backend tests passed; the enhanced focused settlement test then verified void/replacement, immutable payment mode, audit rollback, identical request replay, changed-request rejection, approval/cancellation gates, one leave debit, zero repeated hours/accrual, frozen source identity and subsequent supplemental history. The browser workflow passed from reservation through confirmed payment with no page errors; mobile form inspection passed. No real funds, filings, deployment or QuickBooks posting occurred. The full goal remains active.

Standalone compliance refinement: standalone PTO and bonus previews now initialize and enforce the same unresolved critical compliance tasks as regular payroll. Verified withholding does not remove those blockers. Six focused backend tests passed after this change, including explicit missing-review rejection and subsequent completion. The prior full regression result remains 151 tests. The existing regular PTO browser workflow also passed after the new payment-mode selector was added.

Approval refresh validation: the admin approval button now submits for authoritative server revalidation instead of remaining disabled by stale saved blockers. The PTO browser test proves an unresolved employer review still rejects approval after withholding is verified; completing those reviews permits approval of the same draft and final settlement. That test passed, as did both standalone bonus browser flows with compliance enforcement. TypeScript and scoped lint passed after the UI change.


Federal aggregate PTO withholding: admins can select the aggregate method when creating a standalone vacation payroll. Payment history now carries the source run kind, payroll period, frequency and boundaries in its fingerprint. The aggregate reconciler selects finalized regular wages from the current or immediately preceding complete period, collects earlier supplemental payments made during the current period, and subtracts actual federal withholding once. Missing, duplicate, mixed, cross-year or unreconciled evidence requires a separately reviewed calculation. The calculation and its source run are frozen into the payment snapshot and shown in the admin payout review. Changes to source evidence invalidate draft approval. The existing mandatory supplemental excess calculation can proceed without an ordinary aggregate basis once the annual threshold is already exceeded.

68. The initial native aggregate standalone path uses an existing, unambiguous payroll period containing the actual payment date, with a finalized current or immediately preceding regular payroll at the same frequency. It supports complete weekly, biweekly, semimonthly and monthly periods. The source regular calculation must have separable regular wages and withholding; combined regular/supplemental source payroll, multiple regular payments during the current period, cross-year sources, schedule-transition fragments and imported totals require further reconciliation. Earlier supplemental payments are selected by actual payment date in the current payroll period, not by the processing-period label on an off-cycle statement. This implements the supported current/preceding-period method without inventing wage history for a former employee whose last regular payment is older. Maryland standalone vacation withholding remains separately verified. Sources: [IRS Publication 15, section 7 and vacation pay](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) and [Maryland 2026 withholding guide](https://www.marylandcomptroller.gov/content/dam/mdcomp/tax/instructions/withholding/2026/withholding-guide.pdf).

Aggregate validation: 154 backend regression tests passed. Four focused tests then passed, including actual repeated standalone PTO settlements with zero prior regular withholding, a case ineligible for the flat method. Independent weekly expectations verify federal withholding of $0, $9.04 and then $10.00 on successive additional $100 payouts after the first, including prior tax subtraction. Both browser flows passed with native federal values visible, state withholding review, unresolved compliance rejection, subsequent review completion and final payment. Mobile form inspection, TypeScript, scoped lint, production build and whitespace checks passed. No real payment, filing, deployment or accounting posting occurred. The full goal remains active.


Federal aggregate standalone bonuses: the same verified current/preceding-period basis is now available for discretionary and earned annual bonuses. Administrators select flat or aggregate federal treatment before preview; changing the method invalidates the reviewed preview. Earned bonuses continue to require finalized underlying wage coverage and include their additional overtime in supplemental wages. The payment context and calculation fingerprint retain the selected method and aggregate basis, and idempotent creation rejects a changed method under an existing request reference. A shared review panel shows the native federal amount, source regular payroll, earlier supplemental wages and actual withholding subtracted for both PTO and bonuses.

69. Aggregate federal treatment changes the withholding calculation, not the bonus classification or its entitlement. Discretionary bonuses still require the documented employer-discretion facts, and earned bonuses retain their reviewed allocation and paid-workweek evidence. For supported Maryland annual bonuses without extra overtime, existing reviewed native state treatment remains available. When extra overtime is present, state withholding still requires a verified calculation. The supported aggregate period, source history and cross-year restrictions in assumption 68 also apply to bonuses. Source: [IRS Publication 15, section 7](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15).

Aggregate bonus focused validation: five backend cases passed, including repeated discretionary payments with no qualifying regular federal withholding and earned bonuses with and without overtime under both methods. Repeated $100 bonuses verify federal amounts of $0, $0, $9.04 and $10.00 after subtracting actual prior tax. All four discretionary/earned × flat/aggregate browser workflows passed through final payment; both aggregate mobile forms were visually inspected. TypeScript, scoped lint and whitespace checks passed. No real funds, filings, deployment or QuickBooks posting occurred. The full goal remains active.

Aggregate bonus final verification: the full 157-test backend suite and production build passed. Both PTO browser regressions passed with the shared supplemental review panel. A focused earned-aggregate browser test passed again after shortening its classification label for mobile display, and the resulting form was visually inspected. No required work outside this checkpoint is represented as complete.


Employment-period foundation for rehires: payroll now keeps employment date ranges separately from the current employee profile. Existing valid ranges are backfilled, employee creation opens a range, and separation-date updates synchronize its end. Nonoverlapping later ranges can preserve the same employee identity and earlier period; direct model tests exercise this without enabling a user-facing rehire. The database rejects overlapping ranges, cross-employer identity, rewritten start dates and deletion of employment history. Admins can read the ranges in People & onboarding. Clock-in, shift creation/edit availability, manual time creation/approval and employee-requested corrections require their time range to fit a single recorded employment period in the employer timezone. Midnight at the end of the separation day is treated as an exclusive interval end. Shift-series failures roll back the entire series.

70. Employment periods preserve hire/separation boundaries, including gaps, under one employee identity. Existing valid profile dates seed the first known period; invalid legacy date ranges require reconciliation instead of inventing dates. A work interval must fit one period, and the separation date is inclusive by employer-local calendar day. This is preparatory rehire work: reopening onboarding, retaining prior task/document versions, compensation changes, leave-policy reinstatement and activation across employment periods still need implementation and verification. The existing API continues to reject direct status-based reactivation of a former employee.

Employment-period validation: the corrected full backend suite passed all 158 tests. The new test covers retained old/new periods, employer scope, before-hire/gap/cross-gap time rejection, local-midnight boundaries, all-or-nothing recurring shifts, overlap/start/deletion guards and future-hire clock prevention. TypeScript, scoped lint and whitespace checks passed. No production migration or external action occurred; the full goal remains active.

Employment-history UI verification: the admin browser test passed twice, including the recorded range and existing final-pay/PTO workflow. The new card was captured at 390px viewport width and visually inspected without overflow. The production build passed. Rehire activation remains deliberately unavailable until onboarding/document continuity and the remaining employment-period integrations are implemented.


Onboarding record versions: task creation, changes and document uploads now capture immutable revisions with the task response, review state and associated document identities. Documents are immutable and attached to a specific onboarding cycle. Opening a later cycle requires advancing exactly once and clearing submissions/approval; the current packet and signed-form submission checks only use that cycle's documents. Older encrypted files remain available through the same scoped, audited download route. Admins can inspect saved history inside each checklist step and download the documents saved with a revision. This is usable record preservation before a rehire transition is enabled.

71. A new onboarding cycle must obtain a fresh submission or a newly recorded secure-provider receipt rather than silently treating an older cycle's file as current. Prior signed records are retained unchanged. Existing tasks receive an initial snapshot of the state actually present at migration; earlier revisions that were never captured are not invented. This is a product review policy, not a claim that every government form must legally be replaced on every rehire. The eventual rehire workflow must apply the appropriate form-review requirements and reset employee-level readiness, compensation and access in the same transition.

Onboarding-history validation: all 159 backend tests passed. Coverage includes encrypted prior-document retrieval, current-cycle filtering, rejection of stale-file-only submissions, successful new-cycle submission, immutable snapshots/files, cycle rollback rejection, and employer/employee scope. The browser verifies prior completed evidence alongside a new OPEN cycle, with current approval unavailable until submission. Mobile inspection, TypeScript, scoped lint, production build and whitespace checks passed. No production migration, external message, payment or filing occurred. The full goal remains active.

Rehire preparation: People & onboarding now includes a read-only review for former employees. A proposed start date loads a consistent database snapshot of recorded employment periods, final-period payroll, pending saved runs, applicable dated pay, later scheduled pay changes, current leave balances, reservations and retained onboarding steps. It flags missing/inconsistent separation history, dates overlapping prior employment, backdated starts and outstanding payroll items. Changing the proposed date or refreshing workforce data clears the displayed review; responses for superseded dates are ignored. Authentication and employer scope apply to the review endpoint. The review does not reopen tasks, change identity or status, or certify that every prior wage has been settled.

72. Rehires should use the same employee identity to retain payroll, tax-year, document and leave history. Preparation uses the proposed start date for compensation and the employer-local current date for recorded leave balances; future leave credits are excluded. The displayed balances are ledger evidence, not a decision about reinstatement or payout policy. Backdated rehires need reconciliation, and a clean result from these limited checks is not an approval to rehire. The actual transition remains unfinished: payroll selection still depends on current profile dates in several paths, salary/compensation and leave treatment need integration, and reset/access/activation must occur transactionally before submission can be enabled.

Rehire-preparation validation: all 161 backend tests passed. New coverage verifies authentication/employer scope, invalid dates, historical-date warnings, hourly and salary terms at the proposed date, future scheduled terms, pending/finalized payroll evidence, future leave-credit exclusion, and unchanged employee/tasks/revision count after review. The browser verifies the review, changed-date invalidation and final-pay/PTO reservation/cancellation behavior. Its initial full-card viewport assertion was corrected to accommodate the tall existing PTO form; the complete browser flow then passed. The 390px rehire card was visually inspected. TypeScript, scoped lint, production build and whitespace checks passed. No production migration or external action occurred; the goal remains active.

Payroll across employment periods: regular payroll now selects the employee's recorded periods that overlap the payroll dates, rather than using the latest profile hire/separation dates. A former closed period remains eligible while a later period is in onboarding; the current onboarding period requires activation. The selected historical dates are passed to salary calculation, and salary leave accrual counts only days within the selected employment intervals. Multiple intervals in one pay period produce one employee calculation and one scheduled salary. Time and paid leave outside eligible intervals generate a blocking reconciliation warning rather than disappearing silently from a payable run. Workday rate history continues to determine hourly wages.

73. Rehiring preserves the same employee identity and the prior employment period's payroll eligibility. Reopening onboarding does not retroactively make the employee's earlier employment unactivated. The existing full-period salary policy remains in force for initial/final partial periods and multiple employment intervals in one pay period: one scheduled salary, with no new absence deductions. Exempt sick-leave accrual uses the reviewed normal workweek only on employed days, excluding gaps. A pending new period cannot silently contribute time or leave to an earlier eligible period; those records require activation/date reconciliation before payroll approval. This does not yet implement changes of pay type, new rehire salary agreements, retroactive corrections, or the actual rehire transition.

Employment-period payroll validation: all 163 backend tests passed. New API cases verify retained old hourly wages at $25/hour while rehire onboarding is pending, no employee calculation in a gap, a blocking warning for pending-period work, and $30/hour after activation while the earlier rate stays unchanged. The salary case verifies one $1,000 weekly salary before/after activation and a leave-accrual basis increasing from 1,440 to 1,920 employed minutes while excluding the gap. Pending-period time is excluded with a blocker until activation. Scoped lint and whitespace checks passed. No UI files or production configuration changed in this checkpoint; no real payment, filing or deployment occurred. The full goal remains active.

Same-role rehire action: admins can now review a proposed start in People & onboarding, confirm the displayed terms and retained leave balances, record prior-obligation evidence, and reopen onboarding under the same employee ID. The server repeats the review under employer/employee locks and rejects changed evidence, outstanding review issues or conflicting active adjustments/shifts. It retains prior employment, pay, statements and signed records; archives prior document metadata and tax elections in the rehire audit; clears current form/payment/tax readiness; resets all 13 tasks with fresh due dates; and revokes existing employee sessions and unused invitations. The employee's password remains usable for a fresh login. Identical request retries return the original result without creating another employment period or cycle; altered retries fail. Audit failure rolls back the entire transition.

Hourly rehire opens a dated rate for the new hire date. Admins may edit that opening rate before current-period work or dependent payroll exists, without altering rates from prior employment. Salaried rehires retain the existing reviewed role/agreement and preserve an opening salary-history record if none existed. Both types must submit and review the new checklist before activation. The admin checklist reloads when the hire date changes. Submissions, uploads and reviews in later cycles require a matching cycle identifier, preventing stale prior forms from being applied to the new cycle.

74. The initial rehire action carries forward the reviewed role and pay basis; hourly opening pay may then be adjusted during onboarding. It retains all recorded leave balances subject to the admin's documented review, with no automatic forfeiture or new restoration credit. This is a configurable product policy, not a statement of minimum legal reinstatement requirements. Prior final-period payroll must be finalized, outstanding requests/payroll/payouts resolved, and scheduled adjustments/shifts reconciled before this transition. Rehire without payable prior wages, changed salary duties or pay basis, backdated starts, older off-cycle payment dates and full historical leave-policy integration still need further work. Current verified tax elections are archived and cleared so the new signed-form review controls subsequent automatic withholding. Prior finalized payment snapshots and year-to-date identity remain unchanged.

Rehire-action validation: the full 165-test backend suite passed. New hourly/salary API flows cover stale-review rejection, an injected audit failure with complete rollback, idempotent replay, changed-request rejection, preserved password/leave/payroll evidence, session/invitation revocation, current tax-election clearing, distinct employment periods, fresh cycles and full employee submission/admin review/activation. Browser tests passed for the action, disabled activation before new submissions, correctly reloaded progress, current-cycle review, retained history and prior final-pay/PTO behavior. The mobile action form was visually inspected. TypeScript, scoped lint, production build and whitespace checks passed. No production migration, external invitation, payment, filing or QuickBooks posting occurred. The full goal remains active.

Historical payment and leave dates after rehire: standalone bonus and PTO payment validation now uses the first recorded employment date instead of the latest hire date. It still rejects payments before employment, missing employment history and invalid dates; a legitimate supplemental payment may occur during a recorded separation gap. Annual leave opening includes anyone whose recorded employment began by January 1, and applies the configured opening policy according to whether an employment period covers that date. Employees separated on January 1 retain their recorded balance without a new grant. A later rehire no longer removes a person from a historical opening or incorrectly frontloads leave during a separation gap. The preview explains the January 1 basis.

75. Supplemental payment dates describe when wages were paid, so the latest rehire date must not replace the person's first employment date as their lower bound. Other payment-history, reservation, tax, approval and finalization checks remain required. Annual leave opening uses recorded employment on January 1 rather than the employee's status today. A separated interval retains the prior balance under the existing policy; the new-hire/reinstatement policy still requires its own review. Effective-dated changes to the leave policy itself remain unfinished; historical openings currently use the configured policy reviewed by the admin.

Historical-date validation: all 166 backend tests passed. Bonus and PTO settlement regressions now include a later recorded rehire while settling an earlier supplemental payment, retaining tax history and finalization behavior. The new annual-opening test verifies historical employment inclusion, separation-gap balance retention without a grant, later first-hire exclusion, invalid payment dates and employer scope. An initial bonus fixture still expected regular wages during the separation gap; its later regular payroll was moved into the actual rehire period, preserving the FICA-history assertion. The annual leave browser flow passed with a later hire date. TypeScript, scoped lint and whitespace checks passed. No production migration, external message, payment, filing or deployment occurred. The full goal remains active.

Salary and role review during rehire: the salary classification form now accepts a revised annual amount, title, exempt/nonexempt classification and reviewed workweek during rehire onboarding. Each saved agreement is dated to the new hire date. Further onboarding edits retain the superseded agreement as cancelled history, while the earlier employment agreement remains active for historical dates. Ordinary salary-change cancellation cannot cancel an opening rehire agreement; administrators revise it through the hiring review. Changes reopen pay review and, when the displayed terms change, employee wage acknowledgment. New-period work or dependent payroll prevents editing the opening agreement. A matching hire date is required, rejecting stale forms from earlier employment.

Future-hire packets and dashboards select the agreement effective for that hire date, including after early activation. Regular payroll selects terms for the later of its period start and the employee's selected employment start; thus a mid-period rehire uses the new agreement. A salary change during continuous employment still requires the existing period-boundary reconciliation. Earlier employment payroll keeps the prior salary/classification.

76. A rehire may renegotiate salary, title and overtime classification through the existing documented salary review before new-period work or dependent payroll exists. The new agreement is effective on the new hire date and requires a current employee wage acknowledgment; previous employment agreements are retained. The existing full-period salary policy still applies to a partial first period. This does not change the pay basis between hourly and salary, implement retroactive corrections, or establish effective-dated state/benefit/leave-policy changes; those remain outstanding.

Rehire salary validation: all 166 backend tests passed. Focused tests verify two successive rehire offer reviews retain the $52,000 prior exempt agreement, supersede the $62,400 draft without deletion, and use the final $65,000 nonexempt agreement in the new packet and first partial payroll period. Prior payroll keeps its original salary/classification. Recorded new-period work, stale hire dates and cancellation of the opening agreement are rejected. Fresh submissions and admin reviews still complete activation. Both rehire browser variants passed; the salary variant initially stalled at a populated textarea because of its exact label selector, then passed using its accessible textbox name. No production migration, payment, filing or deployment occurred. The full goal remains active.

Final rehire-salary production build, TypeScript, scoped lint and whitespace checks passed.

Employee-session isolation during hiring transitions: employee writes now revalidate the session inside their transaction after acquiring employer and employee locks. This covers profile edits, clock actions, time attestations, password changes, workforce requests, onboarding submissions/uploads and pay/salary/schedule acknowledgments. The check uses the current employment status and actual session expiry/revocation, rather than relying only on middleware state captured before a lock wait. Former employees retain permitted record/contact/sign-in actions. Login and invitation redemption serialize with hiring transitions; invitation redemption locks the employer and employee before creating a session so a concurrent rehire cannot miss revoking it.

77. A hiring transition, logout or password reset must invalidate pending writes whose session authorization is no longer current. The write transaction is the authorization boundary. An operation that holds the relevant locks and completes before revocation may finish; a competing operation that reaches the boundary after revocation fails and requires fresh sign-in. Separation is rechecked there as well. Existing permitted former-employee payroll contact and record-access behavior is retained.

Session-isolation validation: the 167-test regression suite passed. Final focused tests pause requests after middleware authentication, then revoke or expire their session before allowing the write to continue; profile, clock, attestation, password, request, onboarding/upload and pay-notice writes return 401 without their intended mutations.
