Workweek boundary validation: the final full suite passed all 193 tests. Five focused regressions cover both adjacent pay-period edges for hourly/salary, salary/hourly and salary/salary cases, employer scope, unrelated later weeks, Sunday workweek starts, changed-salary boundary blocking and preserved one-salary rehire-gap behavior. An attempted broader salary split conflicted with the established salary-gap policy; it was removed before the final passing run. The opening-agreement exception was narrowed instead. Scoped lint and whitespace checks passed. No frontend change, production migration, external message, real payment, filing or deployment occurred. The full goal remains active.

Hiring workweek evidence review: live payroll previews and saved drafts now include the complete boundary week’s dated agreements, time segments, approved minutes, open/unapproved time issues and overlapping approved/finalized regular payroll records. Time instants are normalized before snapshot comparison, and weighted-preview rebuilding preserves this context. Admin payroll displays the same evidence with explicit whole-period labels for prior payroll amounts. The review does not yet apply additional overtime.

103. Whole-period paid earnings must not be treated as an allocation to the overlapping workweek. The review shows those amounts as context alongside retained workweek payment records; regular-rate allocation and settlement remain required. Approved hours include recorded work throughout the week, while incomplete clocks and non-approved time are separately flagged.

Hiring workweek review validation: all 193 backend tests passed. Updated adjacent-period regressions verify both time segments, stable clock timestamps, approved minutes and open/unapproved time issues from either side of the boundary. The browser verifies evidence beyond the selected period, the salary amount, saved draft persistence and mobile display without page errors. The mobile layout was inspected. TypeScript, scoped lint, production build and whitespace checks passed. No production migration, external message, real payment, filing or deployment occurred. The full goal remains active.

Allocated-earnings overtime arithmetic: a shared calculator accepts reviewed straight-time earnings as rational cent amounts and preserves exact fractions through the regular-rate and premium calculation. The hourly calculator now uses this arithmetic while preserving its existing snapshot representation. A shared settlement path handles finalized premium history, payable overtime through a period, closed-week requirements and overpayment review for either hourly-rate inputs or reviewed earnings allocations. The salary workweek allocation/approval workflow is not yet connected.

104. The arithmetic receives already-reviewed, nonexempt straight-time earnings and their associated worked minutes. It does not decide salary allocation, earnings exclusions, exemption status or payment authorization. All applicable straight-time earnings must be included, with premiums supplied separately as verified payment history. A negative settlement difference remains a review issue and never creates an automatic deduction.

Allocated earnings validation: all 196 backend regressions passed. Fifteen focused checks cover exact fractional earnings, segment-order/splitting invariance, rounding only at payment, empty/no-overtime weeks, invalid fractions and unsafe totals, closed/history gates, duplicate prior-run rejection, partial-period settlement and overpayment review. Existing weighted payroll allocation, frozen statement and native tax regressions passed through the shared arithmetic. Scoped lint and whitespace checks passed. No frontend change, production migration, external message, real payment, filing or deployment occurred. The full goal remains active.

Scoped workweek allocation preview: a new admin endpoint loads the employee’s current hiring-boundary evidence within a repeatable-read transaction, derives all worked minutes and hourly straight-time earnings from recorded time and dated agreements, and accepts a documented salary earnings allocation for each nonexempt agreement. It rejects missing/duplicate agreements, incomplete or unapproved time, unsupported exemption cases, inadequate evidence and salary allocations below the reviewed minimum wage. It returns exact combined-rate arithmetic and an evidence fingerprint as a draft, without saving an allocation or authorizing payment. Admin form, retained approval and settlement integration remain unfinished.

105. An admin must document which straight-time salary earnings belong to the workweek; the system does not infer this amount from a whole-period payment. Employee hours and hourly earnings are server-derived, and supplied overrides cannot replace them. A preview computes the full-week premium before any separately verified prior-premium settlement, and remains a draft until allocation completeness, closure and payment history are reviewed.

Allocation preview validation: all 197 backend regressions passed. The new API fixture verifies 50 derived hours, $1,800 straight-time earnings, a $180 full-week premium, stable/revised fingerprints, ignored client hour/rate overrides, employer scope, invalid/missing/duplicate allocations, minimum-wage/evidence/overflow rejection and unapproved-time blocking. Audit, payroll-run and leave-ledger counts remain unchanged. Serialized database period IDs were normalized consistently before the passing run. Scoped lint and whitespace checks passed. No frontend change, production migration, external message, real payment, filing or deployment occurred. The full goal remains active.

Admin salary allocation form: hiring-boundary workweek reviews now include inputs for each salary hiring agreement’s straight-time earnings and evidence. Live and newly saved previews retain their payroll-period ID so the form can request a scoped calculation. Results show derived hours, straight-time earnings, rounded regular rate and full-week premium with explicit draft/no-payment wording. Editing inputs clears an old result; a response for a changed form is ignored. Saved approval and payment integration remain unfinished.

106. Preview amounts are temporary calculations. They are not saved allocations, payment approvals or net premium settlements. Every calculation reloads the current recorded workweek; changing an input requires recalculation, and previously paid premiums require their separate verified settlement review.

Admin allocation form validation: the extended browser test verifies open-time rejection, successful recalculation after correcting/approving the time, derived 2.00 hours and $75.00 straight-time pay, result clearing on input change, minimum-wage rejection and successful recovery. The actual form screenshot was inspected at mobile width. Six backend allocation/boundary/settlement regressions, TypeScript, scoped lint, production build and whitespace checks passed. Automatic permission review initially timed out before a combined edit/test command ran; the test edits were then written separately and the extended test passed. The full backend suite was not repeated for the additive period identifier; the preceding full run passed 197 tests. No production migration, external message, real payment, filing or deployment occurred. The full goal remains active.

Retained workweek allocation review: a new scoped save action serializes on employer/employee locks, requires a closed employer workweek, recomputes the allocation from fresh evidence and checks the preview fingerprint. It retains an immutable audit record containing normalized inputs, the reviewed evidence, calculation and reason. Matching request references replay the same record; changed inputs cannot overwrite it. Scoped history returns retained reviews. This action does not release a payroll blocker or apply a payment; the admin save controls and settlement integration remain unfinished.

107. A saved allocation is historical review evidence, not a permanent assertion that the workweek has not changed. Current evidence and paid straight-time/premium history must be revalidated before settlement. Reviews require a completed employer-local workweek and explicit admin confirmation; concurrent unchanged retries must produce one record.

Retained allocation validation: all 198 backend regressions passed. Coverage verifies stale preview rejection after time changes, explicit confirmation, employer scope, audit-write failure rollback, three concurrent saves producing one record, exact replay, rejection of changed retry inputs, scoped history and no payroll/leave payment mutation. A future-week fixture cannot save a review before closure. Scoped lint and whitespace checks passed. No frontend change, production migration, external message, real payment, filing or deployment occurred. The full goal remains active.

Allocation save controls: the admin workweek form now collects a review reason and explicit confirmation after preview, retains the immutable review through the save API and lists retained reviews for that employee/week. Unchanged retries reuse a request reference. Allocation inputs are disabled during saving. History loading merges with a newly saved record so a slower initial fetch cannot erase the displayed save result.

108. Saving retains the reviewed evidence and rationale; it does not finalize payroll. A request reference is kept for unchanged retries while the form is mounted, and retained history is the source of truth after reload. Editing the review reason requires renewed confirmation. Prior review history remains available even when a new draft allocation has not yet been entered.

Allocation controls validation: the browser calculates and reviews an allocation, loses the first save response after the server succeeds, retries, verifies one audit record and reloads the retained reason and $75.00 straight-time/$0.00 premium values. The mobile history display was inspected. TypeScript, scoped lint, production build and whitespace checks passed. Backend code was unchanged; the preceding full run passed 198 tests. No production migration, external message, real payment, filing or deployment occurred. The full goal remains active.

Allocation freshness in live payroll: each hiring-boundary review now locates the latest retained allocation for that employee/workweek and recomputes it against current earnings evidence. The admin screen reports missing, current or stale review status; changed time/agreement evidence requires a new review. The status and referenced review are retained in payroll preview/fingerprint context. This does not yet clear settlement blockers or authorize payment.

109. Allocation fingerprint version 2 covers earned-wage evidence and normalized allocation inputs separately from payment history. Approving a payroll record cannot invalidate unchanged earnings solely by adding a payment-history entry; paid earnings and premium reconciliation must have its own current verification. Version-1 retained allocations remain historical evidence and require recalculation/review before use with the new contract.


Allocation payment reconciliation: live hiring-boundary reviews now collect finalized/approved payroll snapshot versions and whole-period hours alongside workweek allocations, plus scoped overlapping imported payments. A separate fingerprint covers current allocation identity and payment evidence. The reconciler validates each finalized run's full workweek hours/pay totals before crediting only the selected week's straight earnings and premiums. Approved commitments, unsupported taxable earnings, incomplete imported records, malformed or duplicate evidence, and overpayments require review. The admin screen displays finalized totals and unsettled differences. No settlement is applied by this review.

110. A reconciled stored ledger does not establish that all historical payments have been entered. History completeness must be confirmed separately. Only finalized payments with fully reconciled versioned workweek evidence are credited automatically; approved commitments require resolution. Other taxable earnings need their own allocation review. Negative differences remain explicit review items and never create automatic wage deductions.

Payment reconciliation validation: all 202 backend regressions passed, plus the added imported-payment employer-scope check. Focused checks cover exact selected-week credit, malformed and duplicate evidence, payment fingerprints, stale allocations, commitments, imported history, unsupported earnings, and overpayments. The extended mobile browser flow verifies the $75.00 unsettled straight-time difference and stale-evidence feedback; the screenshot was inspected. TypeScript, scoped lint, build and whitespace checks passed. No production migration, external message, real payment, filing or deployment occurred. The full goal remains active.


Workweek settlement authorization: a scoped audited action retains the admin's complete-history confirmation, settlement confirmation and reason against a fresh reconciliation fingerprint. Employer/employee locks serialize requests; unchanged references replay the original record and changed inputs cannot reuse a reference. The complete employer-local workweek must be closed, the retained earnings allocation must match current evidence, and payment evidence must reconcile. Preview revalidates the latest authorization and displays current/stale status, retaining the historical reason. The admin form uses stable retry references, separate confirmations, disabled saving controls and explicit saved-receipt feedback. The authorization itself neither clears payroll blockers nor applies funds; payroll incorporation remains required.

111. Complete-history confirmation is an admin assertion against specific retained earnings/payment evidence. It is not reusable after those inputs change. A replay returns the original historical receipt; a fresh payroll preview determines whether authorization is still current. Authorization does not itself pay wages, approve the payroll run, accrue leave, or bypass tax and statement checks.

Settlement authorization validation: all 202 backend regressions passed. The extended API fixture covers missing confirmations, employer scope, stale fingerprints, audit-write rollback, three concurrent requests producing one authorization, matching replay, changed-reference rejection, time changes and new approved payroll commitments invalidating authorization. The extended mobile browser test loses the first save response, retries with one audit record, reloads current authorization and then displays stale authorization after a time change. The mobile authorization screenshot was inspected. TypeScript, scoped lint, production build and whitespace checks passed. No production migration, external message, real payment, filing or deployment occurred. The full goal remains active.


Authorized workweek payroll integration: current authorizations covering every complete, previously unpaid workweek of a payroll period now replace the ordinary salary/hourly earnings calculation before taxes and deductions. The engine matches approved clocks, dates and worked minutes to retained evidence, validates whole-period coverage, separates straight earnings from the additional overtime premium and retains one reconciled workweek payment record. Current application releases the matching hiring-boundary blocker. Finalization freshness excludes only the specific scoped run being validated, avoiding invalidation from its own approved commitment while retaining other payment evidence. Finalized statements preserve authorization/allocation references and matching earnings; employee/admin displays identify straight-time earnings and the combined workweek premium. The payment collector also surfaces overlapping supplemental runs and bonus-allocation workweeks outside their processing period for review.

112. The implemented automatic replacement applies to complete workweeks covering the selected period with no previously paid portions. All nonexempt worked hours fund the existing actual-work leave-accrual policy once. Partial-period coverage, previously paid earnings/hours, paid leave and extra taxable earnings require additional allocation/coverage support; they do not silently use this replacement. Reimbursements and deductions still run through the existing calculation once.

113. For an allocated workweek, the straight-time amount covers all worked hours, including overtime hours; the overtime amount is the additional premium. Statements and the employee portal must label this explicitly. The payroll being checked may be excluded from its own approved-payment context only through the internal scoped run-validation path; other commitments and finalized payments remain evidence. Once finalized, the paid workweek no longer has an unpaid difference and its original authorization becomes stale for reuse.

Authorized settlement validation: all 206 backend regressions passed. Two new engine tests verify combined withholding/FICA, matching payment/statement/net totals and refusal of changed time, partial coverage, duplicate entries, previously paid portions or unsupported additional earnings. Two new database flows cover both hiring directions, approval, finalization audit rollback, repeat-finalization rejection, single leave accrual and authenticated frozen statement download. The mobile admin flow displays applied hours, straight earnings, premium and the combined rate. The generated one-page statement was rendered and inspected. TypeScript, scoped lint, production build and whitespace checks passed. No production migration, external message, real payment, filing or deployment occurred. The full goal remains active.


Dated allocation coverage and partial-period settlement: allocation version 3 retains a deterministic dated share for every reviewed time segment. Salary is distributed within each hiring agreement by worked minutes, hourly fractions reconcile to the workweek's rounded hourly amount, and the additional premium is distributed by chronological overtime minutes. Largest fractional remainders receive residual cents, with chronological ties. Admin previews show dated shares and explain the method. A selected period now uses its covered dates, requires all earlier worked portions to match finalized coverage, and refuses overlapping, changed, unrecorded or legacy paid portions. Payment records retain the selected segment coverage; subsequent authorization references fresh payment evidence. Statements and employee/admin displays use the covered period dates and the combined full-week rate.

114. This is an internal allocation of already reviewed full-workweek straight-time earnings, not a replacement for the salary agreement or a new legal classification. Salary shares follow that agreement's actual worked minutes; overtime premium shares follow overtime minutes. Cents are conserved across payroll periods. Version-1/2 allocation reviews remain historical evidence and require recalculation under version 3 before the new coverage method is used. The full-workweek regular-rate basis follows [DOL Fact Sheet 56A](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fact-sheets/56a-regular-rate); the deterministic dated cent-sharing method is an implementation assumption, not a claim that DOL prescribes this method.

115. Prior allocated payments can be credited automatically only when their saved dated clocks, minutes and earnings still match current coverage and reconcile to their run totals. Earlier worked portions must be settled first, and a paid segment cannot be reused. Each current period contributes only its own hours to the existing leave eligibility/accrual policy: the semimonthly fixture's first 24-hour portion is below the existing threshold, while its 26-hour second portion accrues 52 minutes. Legacy/imported records without dated coverage, ordinary unallocated weeks and additional taxable/leave earnings still require further implementation.

Partial settlement validation: all 211 backend regressions passed. Five added tests cover chronological cent remainders, overtime share conservation, engine split-period coverage and both database hiring-direction flows. The database flows approve and finalize two periods, preserve the full-week earnings total, finish at zero unpaid earnings/premium and avoid duplicate leave basis. Changed paid evidence is rejected. The extended browser test verifies dated salary/hourly shares and the partial-period earnings display; screenshots were inspected. The generated partial-period statement was rendered and inspected. TypeScript, scoped lint, production build and whitespace checks passed; added legacy-version and statement checks also passed. No production migration, external message, real payment, filing or deployment occurred. The full goal remains active.


Ordinary weeks in affected payroll periods: when an employee has a salary hiring boundary in the selected period, workweek review now includes every week touched by that period for that employee. Ordinary weeks expose the same dated agreement/time evidence and scoped allocation/authorization controls. A biweekly run can therefore combine its hiring-boundary week and following ordinary salary week in one authorized calculation, rather than stopping because the ordinary week had no review path. The UI describes the complete-period reconciliation requirement. Employees without a hiring boundary retain their existing payroll path.

116. All touched workweeks for an affected employee require complete current evidence before the allocated period replaces ordinary payroll calculation. Repeated boundaries do not duplicate a week's review, and workweek identity still follows the employer's configured start day. Ordinary hourly earnings are derived from recorded time/rates; salary allocations continue to require a documented admin review. This expansion does not itself change compensation or authorize an unreviewed week.


Ordinary-week validation: all 213 tests in the full backend run passed. The new scope check verifies unique affected employees, full-period week coverage, Sunday-start boundaries and unchanged empty scope for unaffected periods. The biweekly database flow verifies ordinary salary alongside the boundary week through approval, audit rollback, finalization, one leave accrual and employee statement download. A subsequent expanded focused run passed both salary-to-hourly and hourly-to-salary cases, preserving the reviewed scheduled salary and deriving the ordinary hourly week without salary inputs. The mobile flow exposes the ordinary week's time and pending allocation; its screenshot was inspected. TypeScript, scoped lint, production build and whitespace checks passed. No production migration, external message, real payment, filing or deployment occurred. The full goal remains active.


Native historical payment coverage: workweek payment evidence now loads the scoped employee calculation retained in each native run. For an older finalized hourly record without dated coverage, recovery requires matching frozen regular/overtime hours and pay totals, complete approved unique dated segments, matching current clocks/hours, and exact selected-workweek straight-time/premium totals. The derived coverage is used by the existing prior-payment matcher and identified in the admin view. The frozen native record is not rewritten; its calculation is part of the current reconciliation fingerprint. Missing or different records require review.

117. Only matched native hourly payroll can be reconstructed automatically from retained calculations. Today's time records alone are insufficient evidence of what was paid. The original run/statement stays immutable; derived coverage follows the currently reviewed allocation method only when its hours and amounts exactly agree with the retained payment. Imported records, salary records without reconciled workweek payments, and historical premiums that differ from current allocation shares need separate reconciliation support.

Native coverage validation: all 217 backend regressions passed. Two pure tests verify unchanged source data and rejection of absent, changed, duplicate or unreconciled calculations. A database flow pays native hourly wages first, opens the next hiring cycle, reviews the full workweek, authorizes and finalizes the remaining salary earnings, and verifies matching statement totals without modifying the earlier statement. The new mobile flow runs this sequence and displays recovered native coverage with zero remaining wages/premiums; its screenshot was inspected. The initial fixture was corrected to represent the rehire onboarding cycle rather than bypassing the salary-review guard. TypeScript, scoped lint, production build and whitespace checks passed. No production migration, external message, real payment, filing or deployment occurred. The full goal remains active.


Historical wage entry: the previously read-only history panel now includes an audited employee-specific entry form. It collects work dates, actual payment date, method/reference, gross wages, withheld taxes, net paid and source evidence. Separate confirmations identify the payment as wage-only and already paid/not duplicated. Server validation requires valid past dates and balanced amounts; employer/employee locks serialize imports. Matching requests replay the original audit receipt, conflicting references/work periods are rejected, and audit failure rolls the inserted record back. Later approved/finalized taxable payroll in the same year, or overlapping regular payroll, requires reconciliation before the import can change its wage history. The history table identifies the employee and exposes the retained evidence, withheld tax and net amount.

118. This entry path supports a prior wage-only payment whose gross is taxable wages before annual caps and whose net equals gross minus withheld taxes. Reimbursements, other deductions, partial payments of an already recorded work period and more complex tax bases need a separate supported breakdown. Creating the record is not approval of its workweek allocation or completion of tax reconciliation. Source evidence and the original audit receipt remain retained; no money moves from this action.

Historical entry validation: all 218 backend regressions passed. New coverage verifies arithmetic/date/confirmation validation, employer scope, future-payment rejection, audit rollback, concurrent same-request submission producing one record, changed retry rejection, duplicate work/reference detection and protection of later approved payroll history. The browser rejects mismatched net pay, loses a successful save response, retries without duplicating the payment/audit, and opens retained source evidence. The select locator failure was resolved with explicit accessible labels; the final mobile flow passed and its screenshot was inspected. TypeScript, scoped lint, build and whitespace checks passed. No production migration, external message, real payment, filing or deployment occurred. The full goal remains active.


Imported workweek allocation preview: each historical wage record now offers a scoped preview using a payroll review period covering its complete work dates. The API requires current retained allocations for all touched, closed workweeks, selects only the imported work dates and checks their straight earnings plus premiums against recorded gross. Gross/tax/net must reconcile, and overlapping native or other imported payment evidence requires resolution. The fingerprint includes source payment fields and retained allocation identities/dated coverage. The preview does not modify historical payment records or payroll payments. The dashboard presents period mismatch feedback and matching workweek totals.

119. Matching imported gross to reviewed dated earnings creates a proposed allocation, not proof of source-payment contents. A wage-only source confirmation and retained allocation are still required before the record can supply paid coverage. The selected review period must encompass the entire imported work period; every touched workweek is included, and changes to source evidence or any retained week's fingerprint invalidate the proposed mapping.

Imported preview validation: all 220 tests in the full backend run passed. Three focused checks, including the subsequently added multiweek case, verify date selection, exact gross conservation, source/earnings fingerprints, missing or stale coverage and overlapping payment rejection. The scoped database fixture verifies 24 hours/$600 of imported coverage, employer isolation, invalid period handling and no preview audit/payment mutation. The mobile test rejects an incomplete review period, displays the matching $600 allocation and confirms that no payroll run was created; its screenshot was inspected. TypeScript, scoped lint, production build and whitespace checks passed. No production migration, external message, real payment, filing or deployment occurred. The full goal remains active.


Imported allocation retention: the historical-payment controls now save an immutable review containing the source payment, all dated workweek coverage, the administrator's reason and wage-only confirmation. Saving locks employer settings, employee and payment in order, recalculates current evidence and rejects a changed fingerprint. Exact retries return the retained receipt, including after source evidence changes; changing inputs under the same request reference is rejected. Scoped history exposes retained records without asserting current validity. This does not change historical payment amounts, create payroll, accrue leave or yet credit imported coverage in settlement.

120. Retaining imported payment evidence confirms an administrator's reviewed wage-only mapping; the record must be revalidated against current source and workweek evidence before reducing an unpaid balance. Retained history is an immutable receipt, not a permanent reconciliation status. Native run identifiers and imported payment identifiers must retain separate provenance when paid coverage is connected to settlement.

Imported retention validation: all 221 backend regressions passed. The extended database fixture verifies confirmation validation, employer scope, stale fingerprints, audit rollback, three concurrent submissions creating one review, changed-request rejection, scoped history, stale-source rejection and exact receipt replay after source changes. Payment amounts, payroll run counts and leave remain unchanged by retention. The mobile flow saves a review, reloads its history and verifies one audit record; its screenshot was inspected. TypeScript, scoped lint, production build and whitespace checks passed. No production migration, external message, real payment, filing or deployment occurred. The full goal remains active.


Imported settlement coverage: payroll preview revalidates each retained imported allocation against its source payment and the complete original review period. This includes workweeks outside the current payroll period. An internal evidence-only preview avoids recursive historical coverage loading while retaining current agreement, time, allocation and duplicate-payment checks. Missing confirmations, changed source/week fingerprints, unavailable review periods or imported payment dates later than the selected payroll date require renewed review. Current imported coverage enters payment reconciliation with separate historical-payment/review identifiers and dated hours, wages and premiums. Authorized settlement retains imported provenance separately from native run IDs and pays only remaining current-period coverage. The admin reconciliation displays the retained imported source.

121. Imported wages reduce unpaid earnings only while their complete original allocation remains current and their actual payment date is no later than the selected payroll payment date. A source change or any affected workweek change invalidates the entire imported mapping, including portions outside the selected payroll period. Imported records remain unchanged; subsequent native payroll retains the source identifiers and applies tax/leave calculations only to its own current earnings/hours. Historical wage imports do not invent prior leave credits.

Imported settlement validation: all 223 backend regressions passed, followed by two focused checks after adding payment-date chronology validation. The database flow records $600 of prior wages, retains the allocation, rejects changed source evidence, authorizes and finalizes only the remaining $1,380, verifies the frozen statement sums to net pay, preserves the original import and reconciles the final unpaid balance to zero. A multiple-week test changes a week outside the current payroll period and verifies invalidation of the entire mapping. Mobile verification saves source evidence, loads retained history and displays the $600 prior paid coverage with $1,200 straight earnings and $180 premium remaining; its screenshot was inspected. TypeScript, scoped lint, production build and whitespace checks passed. No production migration, external message, real payment, filing or deployment occurred. The full goal remains active: extra taxable/leave earnings in allocated settlements, broader compensation/policy/tax methods, retroactive corrections, year-end filings and production execution remain outstanding.


Dated leave allocation evidence: full-workweek reviews now load each non-cancelled paid-leave row with its scoped source request, date, minutes, recorded rate, leave type and salary-inclusion flag. Unapproved source requests and leave outside retained employment agreements require resolution. Allocation version 4 retains this evidence in its fingerprint and response; earlier versions require a fresh review. Changing approved leave invalidates retained allocations and downstream settlement/import coverage. The mobile allocation preview displays leave separately from worked hours and explicitly identifies unresolved payment treatment. Combining paid leave with authorized settlement remains the next implementation step.

122. Approved leave must be visible in the same workweek review as worked earnings, even when the leave lies outside the currently selected partial payroll period. Recorded salary inclusion is source evidence, not automatic permission to add another payment. Leave additions, amendments and cancellations must invalidate any allocation whose retained leave evidence no longer matches. Leave hours do not become worked overtime hours. This follows the federal distinction described in [DOL's hours-worked advisor](https://webapps.dol.gov/elaws/whd/flsa/hoursworked/screenEr14.asp) and [regular-rate overview](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fact-sheets/56a-regular-rate); salary inclusion and applicable state payment rules still require correct implementation before combined payment is enabled.

Leave-evidence verification notes: the initial full run passed 222 of 224 tests; the only failures were the two partial-settlement fixtures expecting allocation version 3. Their expected version was updated to 4, and the full suite was rerun. The browser retained imported coverage, opened payroll review, added approved salaried leave and displayed its dated evidence in the allocation preview. TypeScript, scoped lint, build and whitespace checks passed. The screenshot was inspected. This checkpoint intentionally does not claim that combined allocated leave payment is enabled; salary-included leave must be separated from worked earnings without duplicate salary payment before removing that gate.

Final leave-evidence regression run: all 224 tests passed, including both updated partial-period settlement fixtures. The full goal remains active; no production migration, external message, real payment, filing or deployment occurred.


Allocated leave earnings: allocation version 5 values approved leave using the compensation agreement effective on each date. Hourly leave uses the dated hourly rate. Nonexempt salaried leave uses annual salary divided by 52 and the verified fixed weekly hours, with exact fractional arithmetic and whole-cent rounding per leave row. Salary leave is separated from the entered total salary allocation before worked earnings and overtime are calculated; hourly leave is additional. Dated leave records retain amount, rate fraction, request and employment references. Duplicate records, ambiguous/missing agreements, unverified salary terms, more than 24 combined work/leave hours in a day, unsafe cents and salary allocations insufficient for leave or worked minimum wages are rejected. A leave-only salary allocation can produce leave pay with zero worked earnings and overtime. The mobile preview exposes included salary leave and additional hourly leave totals. Payment incorporation remains unfinished; existing settlement gates remain until dated leave payment coverage is implemented.

123. The administrator's entered salary allocation includes paid leave belonging to that salary agreement. The system separates its normal-rate leave value and distributes only the remaining salary among worked time. Hourly leave is added separately. Normal salary leave rate uses the retained fixed-hours agreement, not a hard-coded 40-hour week or an old hourly approval rate. Fractional rates stay exact until each dated leave amount is rounded to whole cents. This is the initial supported leave valuation policy; alternate contractual leave rates will require an explicit dated policy. A salary allocation must cover both the leave component and applicable worked minimum wages.

Allocated leave validation: all 227 tests in the full backend run passed, followed by four focused tests including the added 37.5-hour salary agreement case. The tests prove salary conservation, separate hourly leave, overtime based only on worked earnings/hours, zero-work leave-only allocation, exact rate handling, stale approval-rate avoidance and rejection of invalid leave/agreements/totals. Existing retained imports and both partial-period hiring-direction settlements pass with allocation version 5. Mobile verification displays the $30 salary leave component; its screenshot was inspected. TypeScript, scoped lint, production build and whitespace checks passed. No production migration, external message, real payment, filing or deployment occurred. The full goal remains active.


Allocated paid-leave settlement: authorized payroll now matches each dated leave adjustment to the retained leave ID, source request, date, minutes and reviewed amount. It substitutes the reviewed amount before ordinary withholding and deductions, keeping leave separate from worked earnings and worked leave-accrual basis. Each workweek payment retains versioned dated leave coverage, and the frozen pay item retains the leave's normal-rate and salary/hourly provenance. Statements display the leave date, hours and salary-component/hourly-leave description. Payment reconciliation verifies whole-run leave cents/minutes against additional taxable earnings, checks current dated evidence and rejects duplicate leave claims across runs. Subsequent periods require earlier leave to be settled, reject current-period overlap and cannot pay the same leave twice. Other unsupported additional taxable earnings remain gated.

124. Reviewed salary leave is paid as its own statement component after it has been separated from the total salary allocation; it is not a second salary payment. Current leave rows must match retained request/date/minute evidence. Paid leave remains taxable under the existing ordinary withholding rules but does not increase worked hours or worked-hour leave accrual. Prior paid leave requires exact dated coverage and whole-payment reconciliation; a missing, changed or duplicate source cannot be silently credited or repaid. Historical wage-only imports still do not supply leave coverage.

Allocated paid-leave validation: all 232 backend regressions passed, followed by five focused checks after adding cross-run duplicate leave detection. Both hourly-to-salary and salary-to-hourly database fixtures finalize adjacent periods, pay one leave hour in each period, preserve 50 worked hours and the existing 52-minute accrual outcome, verify combined gross totals ($2,002 and $2,205 respectively), reconcile statements to net and retain two unique leave records. Coverage tests reject altered cents/minutes, unsupported versions, duplicate rows, wrong workweeks, mismatched current evidence and duplicate claims across runs. Both mobile flows display finalized dated leave amounts and zero remaining worked-earnings differences. The generated one-page statement shows $1,170 worked wages, $177 overtime premium and $30 salary leave with matching gross/net; it and the mobile screenshot were inspected. TypeScript, scoped lint, production build and whitespace checks passed. No production migration, external message, real payment, filing or deployment occurred. The full goal remains active: additional bonus/earnings methods, retroactive corrections, broader policy/tax support, year-end filings and production execution remain outstanding.


Allocated discretionary bonuses: allocated payroll accepts reviewed discretionary annual lump-sum bonuses through the existing bonus-entry and withholding path. Eligibility requires positive safe cents, the original adjustment and payment period, verified tax treatment, the recorded classification, all three discretion/no-prior-promise confirmations and source evidence. The frozen pay item retains a versioned copy of that review with its adjustment/period identifiers and amount. Prior payment reconciliation verifies the bonus against its recorded payroll period and additional taxable earnings, rejects changed or duplicate evidence, and keeps bonus records separate from worked-earnings and leave coverage. The admin reconciliation displays retained annual bonus payments. Nondiscretionary bonuses still require earned-workweek regular-rate integration; they cannot bypass that gate by using this path.

125. Only bonuses with the existing documented discretionary classification and annual lump-sum payment treatment use this allocated-settlement exclusion path. The classification requires actual discretion over payment and amount and no prior promise, consistent with [DOL Fact Sheet 56C](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fact-sheets/56c-bonuses). The bonus is taxable through the existing supported withholding calculation but does not alter worked hours or the reviewed worked-earnings overtime rate. Retained classification evidence and original payment-period identity are mandatory; a bonus label alone is insufficient. Broader payment types and nondiscretionary bonus allocation remain separate outstanding work.

Allocated bonus validation: all 237 backend regressions passed. Both hiring-direction database fixtures finalize adjacent periods with one $100 annual bonus and one hour of paid leave per period, preserve worked hours/accrual/overtime, reconcile combined gross totals ($2,202 and $2,405), retain two distinct bonus references and balance each final statement to net pay. Pure checks reject missing confirmations, nondiscretionary classification, wrong periods, unsafe amounts, altered saved amounts and duplicate references. Both mobile flows display the retained bonus records. TypeScript, scoped lint, production build and whitespace checks passed. No production migration, external message, real payment, filing or deployment occurred. The full goal remains active.


Earned-bonus employment evidence: bonus allocation now resolves the retained compensation agreements across every full earning workweek, rather than applying the employee's current classification to old work. Hourly agreements remain nonexempt; salaried weeks require their dated verified classification. Each time segment must belong to exactly one eligible agreement. Weeks mixing exempt and nonexempt classifications require individual review. The fingerprint now includes canonical dated agreement evidence and explicitly normalized clock timestamps, preserving both clock-change detection and JSONB key-order stability. The admin preview displays dated agreements and each week's overtime treatment. Allocation/payout recalculation rejects changes to retained agreement evidence, including separation-date changes after the original review.

126. Earned-bonus overtime follows the compensation/classification agreement covering the earning workweek. A later exempt salary rehire does not erase overtime from earlier hourly work. Separate weeks may use different verified classifications; a single mixed-classification week remains subject to individual review. Changes to dated employment evidence require a fresh bonus allocation review even when hours and calculated bonus cents happen to remain equal. This extends evidence retention without enabling nondiscretionary bonuses in the allocated-settlement path yet.

Earned-bonus history validation: all 239 backend tests passed in the final run. Four off-cycle tests now explicitly verify stale evidence after separation changes and recalculate before payment; all pass. TypeScript, scoped lint, final production build and whitespace checks passed. No production migration, external message, real payment, filing or deployment occurred. The full goal remains active.


Allocated earned-bonus settlement: nondiscretionary annual bonuses can now use allocated payroll when their proportional-earned-hours agreement, fresh earning-date allocation and underlying wage coverage reconcile. Unmatched, duplicate, missing or altered overtime is blocked. Frozen bonus pay items retain version 2 allocation/payment evidence; overtime items retain the originating bonus adjustment ID. Historical reconciliation includes both bonus and its additional overtime in other-taxable-pay reconciliation, rejects changed prior workweek hours/classification and keeps those payments separate from ordinary workweek premiums and leave. The admin history distinguishes earned and discretionary annual payments and displays earned-bonus additional overtime.

Current and historical bonus/overtime amounts must reconcile together and cannot be split into unrelated adjustments. Imported underlying wage support and broader bonus methods remain outstanding where the existing coverage path does not support them.

Time-correction payroll impact: admin time-correction requests now offer a read-only impact review with proposed hours, original time evidence, affected employer-local workweeks and the employee's approved/finalized payroll or imported wages. The lookup includes off-cycle earned-bonus dependencies from saved statement or approved calculation evidence, even when the payment period is outside the corrected workweek. Request approval uses the same fresh scoped lookup inside its transaction. It no longer relies only on clock-in dates or unrelated employees' payroll. Overnight intervals and adjacent-period workweek effects route to payroll correction review, preserving original time and request state. This is source-impact review, not a completed correction calculation or payment workflow.

128. A correction request must review both the original and proposed employer-local workweeks, including overnight dates and earned-bonus dependencies. Existing employee payment evidence requires a separate correction calculation rather than direct mutation of paid time. Another employee's payroll alone does not establish this employee's paid impact. Imported wages are relevant payment evidence even without a native run. Time-correction impact validation: all 243 backend tests passed in the final run. Retained correction impact reviews: pending paid-time corrections now allow an admin to record a reason and confirmation against the current impact fingerprint. The transactional audit retains the original request, source time, proposed time and matched employee payment evidence. Concurrent exact retries return one receipt, changed-input reuse is rejected, and audit failure rolls back the review. History reload compares the saved version and source fingerprint with current evidence; it never presents a review as approval, payment or request resolution. Fingerprints include the complete matched native payment row and frozen employee calculation, with JSON normalization before canonical sorting so Date objects remain meaningful.

129. An impact review is a retained administrative checkpoint, not authorization to mutate paid time or recover/pay a wage difference. Only pending requests with payment impact can retain a new review. A review must become stale when its source time, proposed time or matched frozen payment evidence changes, even if gross pay does not change. Exact retries return the original immutable receipt after later changes; callers must obtain fresh evidence before further correction actions. Actual correction calculations, their authorization, tax/leave effects and settlement still require implementation.

Retained correction validation: all 243 backend tests passed, including concurrent retries, changed-input rejection, facility scope, synthetic audit failure, unchanged paid clocks and stale frozen statement evidence with unchanged gross. Correction wage calculation: a current retained impact review can now open a wage-difference preview in the request card. No time entry, paid run, leave ledger or request is mutated. The endpoint uses a repeatable-read transaction and rolls it back even on success to discard any setup initialization. Each affected native regular hourly run must reconcile frozen paid totals, dated clocks, minutes, rates and workweeks with the current baseline before its proposed calculation can be shown. Overlapping proposed time, uncovered work dates, imported wages, salary/allocated payroll and dependent earned bonuses require their corresponding correction methods. Impact fingerprints now also retain the complete matched imported payment row.

130. Correction wage previews use existing payroll rules and dated rates, with proposed time treated as approved solely for the hypothetical calculation. The original paid evidence must reconcile first; equal gross alone is insufficient. All original/proposed work dates must have native payment coverage for this first correction method. Positive and negative differences describe wage recalculation, not automatic payment or recovery. Taxes, leave adjustments, correction retention/authorization and settlement remain separate required steps. Salary, allocated wages, imported wages and earned-bonus premium corrections remain required extensions rather than being treated as zero differences.

Correction calculation validation: all 244 backend tests passed. The new fixture finalizes a $1,000 forty-hour week, then previews two additional hours as $75 overtime, a two-hour reduction as -$50 and a missing four-hour shift as $150. Retained correction wage calculations: admins can now retain a confirmed calculation and review reason against its current fingerprint. New saves recalculate within the transaction and discard payroll-reader setup changes before appending the record. Exact retries return the original receipt, including after later evidence changes or request decline; changed-input key reuse is rejected. History independently recalculates current evidence and marks earlier calculations current or stale, while preserving the original amount and reason. The admin UI can reload saved calculations and expand the original/proposed hours and wages.

131. Retaining a wage calculation preserves its evidence and review intent; it does not authorize or execute payment, recovery, time mutation or leave/tax changes. Subsequent settlement must revalidate the complete calculation. An exact retry retrieves the original receipt even if the request was later declined or its evidence changed. Stale historical calculations remain readable and must never be substituted for a current settlement calculation. Setup initialization performed by the shared payroll reader is rolled back during calculation retention and history reads.

Retained calculation validation: all 245 backend tests passed. Correction sick-leave replay: correction calculations now include a versioned leave result across the affected and all subsequent finalized regular payroll. Correction leave validation: all 250 backend tests passed in the final bounded-concurrency run. Correction payment tax preview: a current retained calculation can now prepare a later regular-payroll preview. No run, adjustment, source time, audit record or leave entry is persisted by this preview.

A positive total cannot net a negative run correction into this payment. Prior-period leave credits remain separate and unapplied; settlement must also reconcile their effect on the target payroll's accrual/fraction context. Existing version-two settled calculations continue to support verified bonus-hour coverage; they are not assigned invented workweek monetary evidence. Pending older calculations need a current retained calculation before payment authorization.

Correction workweek evidence implementation: the calculation preview and retained history display original/proposed straight-time wages and overtime premiums, with a clarification that straight-time includes the base portion of overtime hours. Validated settled coverage exposes the retained workweek records for the next monetary reconciliation integration. The original financial records remain unchanged. Corrected monetary credits are not yet consumed by allocated salary/workweek reconciliation; that remains required before this follow-on path is complete.

Workweek evidence validation: all 272 backend tests passed. Five subsequent focused checks passed, including a new in-memory reconstruction of previously settled version-two evidence that preserves bonus-hour coverage without manufacturing workweek cents. Validation tests reject inconsistent minutes, classification totals, dates, weeks, money and deltas, and preserve a retained one-cent rounding allocation. Three mobile flows passed, covering calculation retention/reload and both later bonus finalizations. The workweek display was inspected. TypeScript, scoped lint, production build and whitespace checks passed. No production migration, real payment, external message, filing or deployment occurred. The full goal remains active.

144. A finalized hourly correction can supply later allocation coverage only when its retained workweek cents reconcile to the original frozen payment and its finalized correction settlement. Correction earnings are credited to their original work dates; they are excluded from the processing period’s unrelated taxable earnings during allocation reconciliation. Duplicate or mismatched settlement evidence blocks the credit. Prior financial records remain immutable. Older corrections without dated monetary evidence, changed-rate premium methods and broader unsupported correction cases require further implementation.

145. Subsequent hourly payroll credits finalized corrections against original workweek hours and premiums only after the original frozen wages, retained calculation and correction payment agree. Payroll approval fingerprints include correction settlement identities. Missing dated monetary evidence blocks verified workweek coverage; original payment totals remain unchanged. The processing-period correction earning does not create worked hours or another overtime premium. The admin review displays the included settlement references. This does not add negative recovery, multiple corrections to the same source entry, or salary/allocated-source correction support.

146. New hires may save partial answers for open steps or steps with requested changes, then resume from the server on another visit. Draft saving does not submit the step, permit admin completion, change the employee identity, or capture an acknowledgment. Only task-specific text fields are retained; acknowledgment checkboxes and employer terms are captured through the existing full submission validation. Submitted/completed steps cannot be overwritten by a draft, and drafts from an earlier onboarding cycle are rejected. Saved progress is explicit through the Save progress button.

147. Handbook acknowledgment covers the exact handbook and benefits instructions displayed to the employee. The server compares that displayed text with current employer policy before accepting a signature, and retains both texts with the response. Changed policy blocks admin completion of stale submissions and activation of onboarding employees with stale completed acknowledgments. Existing employee history is retained; a fresh acknowledgment is required for onboarding records that lack a matching benefits snapshot. Revised terms reset the employee acknowledgment checkbox. A separately reviewed not-applicable exception retains its existing behavior.

148. Hiring pay acknowledgment must include the terms actually displayed to the employee; requests without those terms are rejected. Admin review and onboarding activation revalidate the signed role, pay, classification, hire date, location, workweek and pay-schedule snapshot against current hiring terms. JSON property order is immaterial, but values must match. Revised terms reset the acknowledgment checkbox, and the original signed response remains in revision history. Existing onboarding clients must reload before submitting under this requirement.

149. First-shift readiness refers to the earliest scheduled or completed shift on or after the hire date in the employer timezone. Admin completion retains that shift’s identity, time, location, activity and arrival notes. Cancellation, a different earliest shift, or changed details requires a new review before onboarding activation. A completed reviewed shift remains valid; missed and cancelled shifts do not. Workforce automation opens one deduplicated warning for stale completed reviews and dismisses it after re-review or departure from onboarding. A recorded not-applicable exception retains its existing behavior.

150. During onboarding, stale submitted or completed handbook/pay acknowledgments are shown as requiring review. Stale completed acknowledgments do not count toward current completion progress. Employees receive instructions to request reopening when a completed step needs renewal; fresh acceptance and admin review remain separate actions. Workforce automation maintains one renewal alert per onboarding employee, keeps it open while stale changes are requested, and dismisses it after current submission or departure from onboarding. Historical signed records and approved exceptions remain unchanged.

151. Employees can view and download text copies of their own submitted hiring-pay and handbook acknowledgments, including prior onboarding cycles. The view uses retained terms and signature names, pages through older records, and omits internal admin review fields and other employees’ records. A legacy initial capture is labeled as a retained record; missing submission time or benefits text is disclosed rather than invented. Downloads are acknowledgment copies of saved terms, not new submissions or approvals.

152. Completing hiring pay review requires reviewed federal/state forms, verified tax elections supported by the current native calculator, and a reviewed check or active direct-deposit election. Review retains the employee compensation/leave settings, payment evidence and tax-election snapshot; a displayed fingerprint prevents stale review. Changes require renewed review before onboarding activation and produce an automated follow-up alert. The checklist can be refreshed after editing pay settings. This currently uses the existing 2026 native withholding coverage; it does not add later-year or additional-jurisdiction calculations, benefit enrollment, or bank payment execution.

153. Admins may generate a selected pay-calendar month, defaulting to the current month, within the calendar engine’s existing 2000–2200 range. Generation continues to use the configured dated pay schedule and existing duplicate/locked-period safeguards. Calendar generation does not establish support for that year’s tax calculation. The complete hourly hire-to-pay browser journey now runs on a fresh isolated harness and includes verified tax setup before hiring completion; all payment and filing confirmations in the test remain synthetic.

154. Browser integration checks use a fresh local database schema for every test, including the actual admin QuickBooks return, employee clock recovery, expense assignment and date-filtered exports. The admin permission bootstrap is simulated only in the root-application return check; payroll requests still reach the real isolated API. QuickBooks OAuth return routing is distinct from a live Intuit connection or journal transmission. No browser test sends invitations or executes real payments or filings. Historical PTO browser fixtures pin the isolated database `now()` function before creating records; production clocks and ordinary test schemas remain unchanged, and reviewed reservation terms are not rewritten.

155. Every completed hiring pay review requires a structured benefits disposition: no plan offered, not eligible, employee waiver, confirmed enrollment, or a waiting period with a future eligibility date. The admin supplies an employee-facing explanation, separate private evidence reference, effective/eligibility date and explicit confirmation. The current published benefits terms are retained with the review; changes require renewal before hiring activation. Eligibility dates and stale or missing reviews generate deduplicated follow-ups for active employees as well as completed onboarding reviews, and active-employee follow-ups persist while changes are requested. Employees see the decision, date and explanation, without the private reference. These are reviewed eligibility/enrollment records; carrier enrollment, employee benefit elections, recurring deductions and pretax tax treatment remain separate unfinished work. No plan eligibility or enrollment is inferred from an empty policy.

156. Employees can submit a typed-name enrollment request or decline against the exact published benefits offering, retain a current signed copy, and download it. The initial choice applies to the entire offering described in the published text; per-plan catalogs, coverage tiers and dependent enrollment remain unfinished. Admin enrollment and waiver dispositions require the matching signed current choice. New choices invalidate earlier review, changed terms require a fresh signature, repeated current submissions are idempotent, superseded submissions cannot be replayed, and previous choices remain in the onboarding revision history. Choice submission is restricted to active employees or current hires and is bound to the authenticated employee and hiring cycle. It does not activate or terminate carrier coverage, authorize unspecified deductions, or execute a carrier enrollment.

157. The employer may publish up to 20 plans with 1–10 coverage options each. Each option records monthly employee and employer contributions and the reviewed published tax treatment; employee selection captures those server-side values and the exact catalog. Employees must select an option or decline each plan. Catalog edits require the previously loaded catalog and review source, and are retained in the employer audit history. Prices are monthly plan contributions, not a deduction schedule or permission to silently prorate. Plan-specific carrier fulfillment, dependent records, eligibility calculations, recurring payroll deductions and pretax treatment remain unfinished. Existing bundle-only choices remain available when no structured catalog is published; switching between catalog and bundle offerings requires renewed review when their terms or signed selection evidence change.

158. Positive employee contributions require a separate typed-name wage-deduction authorization after current enrollment review. The statement specifies each plan contribution, employer, monthly total, coverage start and collection rule: full amount once on the first eligible regular payment of each coverage month after signing, with no first-month proration, arrears or second monthly charge under this authorization. This is a proposed collection rule to be implemented in payroll, not a deduction already created. Missing/stale authorization blocks hiring activation and creates a scoped follow-up; amounts, employer or reviewed terms changing require renewed authorization. Current and prior signed copies remain retained, and employees can download the current saved statement. Separate authorization follows the [Maryland Department of Labor deduction guidance](https://www.labor.maryland.gov/labor/wagepay/wpdeductions.shtml); it does not itself prove every deduction is permissible or implement tax treatment, minimum-pay protections, carrier collection or recurring payroll execution.


159. The collection rule in assumption 158 is now implemented for authorized after-tax employee contributions in regular payroll. The payment date determines the coverage month; the full monthly amount is collected once after the signed authorization and coverage start. Approved/finalized payroll snapshots reserve the collection, voids release it, and review fingerprints force stale competing drafts to refresh. Zero-wage workers incur no charge and do not block another worker for missing consent; wages must cover the contribution without reimbursement funds. Current and retained authorization contents, actual posted deduction totals and previous monthly collections are reconciled before reuse. Unsupported pretax deductions, incompatible changed coverage, historical employment collection and ambiguous prior evidence require review. No proration, arrears, carrier remittance, employer contribution accounting or automatic historical coverage reconstruction is assumed. Generic manually entered deductions are not inferred to be linked plan contributions. Employee statements identify the plan, option, month and amount.


160. QuickBooks journals now separate authorized employee benefit contributions by plan, coverage option and payment month within the existing deductions-payable account. Other deductions retain their remaining combined line; employer benefit costs and carrier remittances are not created by this change. Journal construction reconciles retained consent and the run deduction total, and a new sync also checks the posted employee deduction amounts. Plan descriptions contain no employee names or signatures. Saved jobs keep their original payload and request identifier through uncertain-send retries and mapping changes; previously saved or transmitted journals are not rewritten. All external requests in the regression use a synthetic transport.


161. The existing latest-50 QuickBooks job listing now includes each saved journal for admin review and exact JSON download. The view identifies the saved company, environment, payment date, attempts and request ID, so it remains meaningful after account remapping or disconnection. Displayed account IDs and amounts come from the immutable job payload, not current mappings. Access remains facility-scoped under admin authentication. This is an accounting request record; a saved or synced journal is not evidence of carrier remittance or employee funds transfer. Older-job pagination remains separate work.


162. QuickBooks history can now load older jobs in descending-ID pages of 50, with an exclusive validated cursor and facility scoping. This removes assumption 161’s latest-50 access limit. The saved-job retry action is bound to that job ID and verifies the company/environment under the connection lock before creating or sending anything. A different connected destination cannot silently receive a replacement job when the admin intended to retry an older record; the matching company/environment must be reconnected. The existing explicit “Sync selected payroll” action continues to target the current connection. The browser regression covers 51 saved records, terminal pagination, the exact oldest download, invalid cursors and cross-facility denial; synthetic transport checks cover destination changes and matching-job retries.


163. Automatic QuickBooks sync now rechecks auto-sync enablement and the selected company/environment under the connection lock. A payroll with a saved journal exclusively for a different destination raises a deduplicated destination-review alert instead of automatically creating a replacement journal. Those records are excluded from the ten-job sending batch so they cannot starve new payroll; an explicit current-company sync remains available after admin review. Reconnecting the original destination resumes its existing job behavior and clears resolved alerts. Regressions use synthetic transports and cover eleven old-company records ahead of a fresh payroll, repeated sweeps, a changed destination and matching-company recovery.


164. QuickBooks CSV and direct-sync payloads now share the same integer-cent, nonnegative, balanced journal calculation and authorized monthly benefit lines. CSV retains its bookkeeper-verified account names and existing approved/finalized export policy, while direct sync uses numeric account IDs. Both verify posted benefit amounts; failed validation creates no export-log entry. CSV retains its content hash and formula-cell escaping. The parity regression compares every line amount against direct sync, checks the separate plan/month contribution, and rejects altered net pay and employee deduction totals.


165. The benefit-contribution report uses actual finalized payment dates and retained employee names, one row per collected plan/option/month, with payroll and authorization references. The existing date-range controls select the output range. Full affected months are reconciled first so partial ranges cannot hide duplicate or inconsistent collection evidence. Headers-only output means no qualifying finalized collection in the range; approved/unpaid runs, employer contributions, manual unlinked deductions and carrier remittances are excluded. Report generation is authenticated, facility-scoped, audited and uses the existing CSV formula escaping. It is a collection reconciliation report, not proof of carrier payment or coverage.


166. Admins can review benefit contribution totals inside Reports & QuickBooks before downloading. The view groups finalized employee deductions by plan, option and month and expands to retained employee names, payment dates and payroll references. Changing the selected dates clears the previous result; an empty range is explicit. The JSON view uses the same reconciled report calculation as CSV, requires admin authentication and remains facility-scoped. It intentionally omits authorization fingerprints from the screen response; the export still supplies them for record reconciliation. Displayed deductions are not carrier remittance confirmations.


167. Production admin authentication and permission evaluation are extracted unchanged into a shared module used by the server and the permission-aware payroll test harness. Payroll GET requests use payroll.view; other methods use payroll.manage, with the existing canonical-owner behavior. A dedicated real-HTTP test uses signed synthetic JWTs and isolated canonical-view contract rows to verify forged claims, inactive/missing users, view/manage boundaries, allow/deny overrides, expiry and facility isolation. It does not replace verification of the deployed canonical view, real account assignments or production secrets. Ordinary browser fixtures retain their isolated synthetic guard; their results alone do not prove production authorization.


168. Payroll invitation delivery is recorded only when the shared email sender returns sent=true. Disabled, suppressed, missing-result and thrown-error outcomes leave sent_at empty and audit emailed=false while retaining the generated one-time link. The admin sees an Action needed message after the dashboard refresh instead of a success banner. SMTP acceptance does not guarantee inbox delivery. Regression transports are synthetic; the secure-link-only action makes no email call, and a different facility cannot trigger a send for the employee.


169. Employer setup now displays server-configuration checks for secure uploads, invitation email, HTTPS invitation links and scheduled checks. The response projects booleans and fixed explanations only, without sender addresses, credentials, key material or server URLs. Email readiness includes the category-disable policy and basic sender/port configuration. Settings present is not a live probe: it does not verify delivery, a deployed employee portal, historical document decryption/backups or a running scheduler. Admins can refresh the check without sending anything or changing settings.


170. Scheduled payroll sweeps and the admin Run checks action retain execution records with source, start, finish and outcome. Scheduled records cover workforce automation plus compliance alert/source checks; manual records cover the existing workforce action. A facility failure is recorded and does not prevent later facilities from being processed; the scheduler still receives an aggregate failure for logging. The employer-setup view shows the latest ten records for its facility. Missing completion is displayed explicitly and is not inferred to mean a live worker. Raw exception text is excluded from the admin record. Execution history does not establish successful external payment, filing or email delivery. The schema addition runs through the existing payroll initialization migration mechanism and has only been applied in isolated test schemas.


171. Failed scheduled/manual checks now raise separate deduplicated payroll alerts. History completion and alert state are committed together under a short facility-scoped advisory lock. The newest started run that has completed controls its source’s alert: older late success cannot clear a newer failure, and an older late failure cannot reopen an alert resolved by newer success. Manual success does not clear scheduled-check failure. Raw server errors remain private. Mobile alert content now occupies a full row so long titles remain readable beside action controls.


172. Employees use the existing signed benefits-choice workflow to request a changed election. When prior contribution authorization exists, changing to a waiver or another zero-contribution choice requires current admin benefits review before wages can be approved. Zero-wage previews still do not collect or block unrelated wages. A reviewed no-contribution result retains the current decision/election and prior authorization in payroll evidence, which changes the review fingerprint and invalidates older drafts. The payroll view explains the effective decision. This does not refund prior deductions, cancel carrier coverage or implement a separate authorization-withdrawal process.


173. A completed future-dated benefits review does not replace preceding reviewed coverage for payments before its effective date. Payroll uses the newest applicable valid retained review from the same employee, task and onboarding cycle, with its retained catalog/policy and signed deduction authorization. Selected historical evidence is identified in the payroll snapshot and admin view. Known prior funded coverage with missing or inconsistent historical evidence blocks approval for reconciliation. Initial future coverage without known preceding funded coverage creates no earlier deduction. Existing first-regular-payment-per-month collection rules remain in force; changed amounts within an already collected month still require review. This does not prorate, refund, remit to carriers, establish carrier coverage or implement every possible benefit transition.


174. Employees can review their own finalized benefit contributions inside Pay statements by payment year, with automatic loading, refresh, collected total and plan/coverage-month/payment details. The endpoint derives employee and facility identity from the locked authenticated session; caller-supplied identities do not select records. It reuses full-month payroll reconciliation and projects no other employee identity, signature or authorization fingerprint. Year changes clear prior results, and reconciliation errors hide stale totals until resolved. Former employees retain record access while their session remains valid; revoked sessions are denied. The history is a record of wage deductions, not confirmation of carrier coverage or remittance, and does not include employer-funded contributions.


175. Finalized payroll tax reconciliation requires explicit nonnegative integer-cent values for gross and every retained employee/employer tax component. Missing federal or state withholding is no longer treated as zero. Invalid values or totals beyond safe integer precision require payroll reconciliation before a filing receipt can be recorded; the failed operation creates no filing or filing-audit record. Genuine explicit zero amounts remain valid. This validates source evidence and arithmetic precision; it does not calculate new tax methods or produce/submit agency returns.


176. Admin tax reconciliation has an explicit refresh action. Refresh clears prior totals before reloading, and failures display a recovery message instead of an indefinite loading state. Filing entry remains disabled and dependent calendars are hidden until valid reconciliation returns; actual deposit-receipt entry remains available because recording a receipt does not assert matched payroll totals. Selecting the already selected year preserves the current state, and changing years is disabled during an active save/refresh. Refresh remounts calendars from the recovered evidence. The browser regression verifies initial failure, restoration, a second failure without stale totals, and the existing accelerated filing/deposit workflow. Its older synthetic fixture now supplies explicit zero federal withholding.


177. New payroll snapshots retain a versioned FICA wage basis containing the exact gross, prior year-to-date wages, Social Security wage cap, Additional Medicare threshold and taxable wage amounts used by the existing engine. Supplemental bonus/PTO paths inherit the same basis; verified non-wage reimbursements retain explicit zero wage bases. The basis participates in approval fingerprints and is copied into finalized employee statement evidence. Existing drafts without the new evidence must be rebuilt when their approval fingerprint differs; historical finalized records are not rewritten. This does not reverse rounded taxes, add federal/state W-2 box calculations, qualify overtime for year-end reporting or implement new tax rules.


178. Employee payroll summary CSV now appends retained Social Security, Medicare and Additional Medicare taxable wages, the verified record count and wage-basis review details. It checks retained payroll/statement agreement, physical gross/tax amounts, supported calculation references and thresholds, and duplicate evidence. Missing/inconsistent records or imported payments leave all wage-base totals blank instead of presenting partial totals as complete.
