Reconciliation and the ordinary summary use one database query snapshot. Prior finalized records are not backfilled from rounded tax amounts. These are source-control totals, not W-2 box outputs or a filing-ready certification.


179. Reports & QuickBooks includes an internal retained-wage-basis review using the existing date range and CSV reconciliation calculation. It shows employee identity, verified/finalized record counts, supported FICA wage totals and per-run or imported-record issues. Null totals stay unavailable in the view instead of becoming zero. The read-only endpoint requires admin access and facility scoping, returns no private statement or authorization payload, and disables caching. This review supports source reconciliation; it is not year-end issuance or a W-2 readiness certification.


180. Native income-tax calculations retain their federal and Maryland wage inputs before withholding credits/allowances, including the Maryland regular-wage/annual-bonus split. This versioned engine evidence participates in approval fingerprints. Finalized statement evidence includes it only when recorded federal/state withholding is present and matches the native calculation; changed manual amounts leave this basis unavailable rather than assuming a new wage basis. FICA evidence remains separate. Existing drafts with changed fingerprints require regeneration. This is retained calculation input, not a completed W-2 or support for pretax exclusions, additional jurisdictions, unsupported supplemental methods or manually reviewed income-tax wage bases.


181. Employee summary CSV and internal wage review separately reconcile native federal/Maryland wage inputs against retained calculations, statement evidence and posted withholding. These totals are withheld when supporting evidence is missing, manually changed, inconsistent, outside the supported payment year or mixed with imported payments requiring reconciliation. Reimbursement-only records require consistent zero-wage/zero-withholding evidence. FICA and income-tax review results remain distinct. The report retains exact decimal amounts and uses the existing single-query snapshot; it does not create W-2 boxes or establish filing readiness.


182. A separate append-only income-tax wage review can now be recorded through the admin API for finalized 2026 Maryland-resident payroll. It captures reviewed federal/Maryland wages within posted gross, a detailed source reference, reviewer identity and a fingerprint of the exact paid evidence. Finalized wages/statements are preserved. Exact current retries reuse the record; changed payloads, stale evidence and superseded request keys are rejected. History distinguishes current, stale and superseded records. Database guards enforce facility/finalized-payroll ownership and immutable review rows. This schema has only been applied in isolated test databases. The admin form and report consumer remain unfinished, so recording this review does not yet resolve report warnings or establish filing readiness.


183. The employee reconciliation reports consume the latest append-only income-tax wage review for each finalized employee payment when its source fingerprint, retained source snapshot, facility and employee-payment ownership, reference and amount bounds still reconcile. A current review may supply federal/Maryland wage inputs even when native evidence was unavailable. A stale latest review blocks income-tax totals instead of silently reverting to older or native evidence. Reports identify the number of reviewed records and still withhold totals when imported payments or any unresolved record are present. These reviewed wage inputs do not change paid statements or certify W-2/filing readiness. The API and report consumer are implemented; the admin entry form remains pending.


184. Hiring administrators can open an income-tax wage review within each finalized employee payroll card. Inputs start blank and require an explicit reviewed source, confirmation and amounts within posted gross; no wage amount is inferred from withholding. Editing amounts or the reference resets confirmation. Refresh clears prior form data, stale-source conflicts remove the editable source, and unchanged uncertain submissions retain the same request key. Successful saves refresh current/stale/superseded history and direct the admin to refresh report totals. This completes the internal API/form/report review loop for the supported 2026 Maryland scope; it does not expand jurisdiction support or issue year-end forms.


185. Full employer and employee filing identities are stored separately from ordinary payroll records using the existing authenticated encrypted vault. Each correction creates an immutable revision scoped to the facility and employer or employee; a current revision guard serializes competing corrections. Payloads include full nine-digit identifiers, structured legal names, US mailing addresses and a confirmed review reference. Identifier checks establish format only, not agency verification. Ordinary APIs return revision history and last four digits; internal issuance consumers can decrypt an exact facility-scoped revision. Audit metadata excludes identifiers, names, addresses and references. Missing vault configuration blocks writes without creating a revision. Admin entry, employee review, international addresses and actual year-end issuance remain pending. No real filing identities were used in tests.


186. Hiring administrators enter employer filing identity in Employer setup and employee filing identity in People & onboarding. US mailing state starts as MD for the existing employer baseline and remains editable. Full identifiers use masked input; successful saves and refreshes clear entered details. Form state is local to the selected subject and is not persisted in browser storage. All corrections require re-entry and confirmation against the source, using the current immutable revision. Ordinary history shows identifier suffix and reviewer metadata. This completes admin entry only; employee self-review, international addresses and year-end use remain pending.


187. Employees, including former employees with valid sessions, can review only their own current filing name, US address and identifier suffix in the portal. They may confirm displayed details or request correction; no full identifier or administrator source reference is returned. Decisions are immutable, bound to the exact identity revision and attributed to the authenticated employee. Repeating the latest decision reuses it; an admin identity correction requires a fresh review. Hiring admins see decisions in masked revision history. Employee confirmation covers the displayed details, not the unseen full identifier or agency verification. Corrections currently require secure follow-up with the administrator; proactive alerts and issuance integration remain pending.


188. Filing identity correction requests generate a deduplicated internal admin warning immediately. The warning identifies the employee number and identity revision and directs the hiring admin to contact the employee securely. It contains no full identifier, filing name, address or private source reference. Employee reconfirmation or a new identity revision clears the warning. Scheduled/manual workforce automation reopens dismissed requests only while the latest identity revision still has an unresolved correction decision, including former employees. Alert synchronization shares the identity subject lock to avoid stale automation decisions. This is an in-app action queue, not an email or agency notification.


189. Overtime reporting starts with a paid-premium source review rather than treating all overtime wages as qualified compensation. The admin API checks finalized payment year 2026, exact employee calculation/statement agreement, complete workweek payment allocation, posted earnings and matching bonus premium allocations. Duplicate/malformed weeks, mismatched taxable pay items, missing allocations and unsupported correction items suppress the premium total. Imported payments are excluded explicitly. Results remain REVIEW_REQUIRED regardless of amount until FLSA applicability and reporting qualification are established. This API does not produce code TT values; the UI and remaining qualification workflow are pending. The IRS 2026 W-2/W-3 instructions were checked on 2026-09-10: https://www.irs.gov/instructions/iw2w3.


190. Reports & QuickBooks displays the overtime source review for the supported payment year 2026. Each employee payroll shows its paid premium or specific evidence issues. The report explicitly excludes imports and continues to require FLSA qualification review; it does not label paid premiums as code TT amounts. Refresh clears prior results, empty payments are explicit, and no aggregate annual premium is inferred across unresolved records. The existing report date range does not control this separate, explicitly labeled annual review.


191. An admin may record a reviewed FLSA-required premium amount between zero and the reconciled paid premium for a finalized 2026 employee payment. Non-FLSA-required treatment records zero; a reference and explicit confirmation are mandatory. Reviews are append-only, facility-owned and bound to exact retained payroll/statement evidence and payment date. The latest current review supplies the displayed qualified amount; missing or stale reviews leave it unavailable. Exact current retries reuse the record, while changed concurrent reviews require refresh. These are reviewed reporting inputs, not issued tax forms or a blanket legal determination. The API and report consumer are implemented; the admin entry/history UI and broader source support remain pending.


192. Hiring admins record FLSA qualification within each reconciled overtime report record. Treatment and amount start blank; the qualified amount must fit the paid premium, and non-required treatment requires zero. Editing treatment, amount or reference resets confirmation. Conflicts disable the form until the source report is refreshed. Successful saves reload report values and revision history, including treatment, amount, reference and reviewer metadata. The API returns history within the same report query snapshot. This completes the internal qualification entry/report loop for supported source cases; it does not expand unsupported premium coverage or issue tax forms.


193. Native salaried overtime premiums reconcile from retained salary rate, fixed agreement hours and overtime minutes, with exact integer rounding and comparison to the posted payment. The paid premium is the reconciled overtime payment less its calculated straight-time component; it is not inferred by dividing a rounded payment by three. Native exempt salary records require zero overtime minutes/pay to contribute a zero premium. Salary calculation and statement evidence must agree, and existing taxable-pay-item/bonus checks still apply. This extends source support without changing paid wages or automatically establishing FLSA qualification.


194. Newly prepared native hourly correction payments retain before/after workweek payments and their nonnegative premium difference with the authorization and settlement. The report adds only this difference to the processing payroll premium after matching the correction earning, authorized plan and finalized settlement, including employee-payment identity and versions. Duplicate/malformed workweeks, inconsistent wages, negative premium differences and missing legacy evidence remain unresolved. Unsupported correction types are not inferred. The extra evidence participates in existing authorization/payroll fingerprints, so old pending previews may require fresh authorization. This preserves paid statements and still requires FLSA qualification review.


195. Year-end preparation consolidates payment year 2026 into one read-only transaction snapshot. It returns current filing identity revision/name/address with identifier suffix only, employee identity review, annual wage inputs, withholding controls and summed current qualified-overtime reviews. Missing/inconsistent wage evidence or imports suppress affected annual totals. Employee correction requests and missing/unreadable identities appear as reconciliation issues. READY_FOR_REVIEW means these retained inputs reconcile, not that tax forms are approved or issuance is available. Additional compensation, benefits, exclusions, form mapping and delivery remain required. The API does not create or transmit forms, and its admin view is pending.


196. Annual preparation is available in Reports & QuickBooks for payment year 2026. Admins explicitly load current inputs; refresh removes old results before loading. The view displays unavailable values as unavailable rather than zero, preserves exact decimal strings and shows filing identity suffixes only. Employee identity review, imported/finalized counts, run references and per-employee reconciliation issues remain visible alongside totals. Reconciled inputs are labeled for further review, and unfinished tax-form issuance is explicit. This view uses its labeled annual scope rather than the separate custom report date range.


197. Maryland employer reporting uses a separate eight-digit Central Registration Number; it is never derived from the federal EIN. Employer identity can be saved before this number is available, but annual preparation flags its absence for state reporting. Entered values must be eight digits, may retain leading zeroes and cannot be all zeroes. The full value is encrypted with the immutable employer identity revision; annual preparation exposes only the final four digits, ordinary revision history and audits omit it, and successful saves clear the entry field. This validates format and records the admin source attestation, not agency registration status. Existing identity revisions without a state number remain readable. Source: [Maryland employer withholding guidance](https://services.marylandcomptroller.gov/taxes/en/employer-withholding?id=kb_article_view&sysparm_article=KB0010017).


198. The annual W-2 box 6 input combines employee Medicare and Additional Medicare withholding, using exact decimal-to-integer cents with no floating-point addition. Both components must be valid and the existing annual tax/wage reconciliation must be complete; imports, missing evidence or inconsistent posted tax records keep the combined total unavailable. Regular and Additional Medicare controls remain separately visible. The combined number is a preparation input, not an issued tax form or employer Medicare liability. Source: [IRS Additional Medicare reporting guidance](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/questions-and-answers-for-the-additional-medicare-tax).


199. Annual preparation reuses the monthly benefit contribution reconciliation for each paid employee in payment year 2026. It displays retained employee deductions with plan/option, coverage month, tax treatment, payment date and payroll reference; the API retains the authorization fingerprint. Inconsistent evidence makes contributions unavailable and adds a reconciliation issue without hiding other annual controls. An empty list means no retained employee deductions, not proof of no coverage or no reportable benefits. These deductions do not establish employer-paid costs, W-2 benefit codes or other reportable compensation. Employer contributions and classification need separate evidence.


200. Each employee annual preparation now has a versioned source fingerprint scoped to facility and payment year 2026. It binds retained finalized payment rows/calculation snapshots, latest income-tax review evidence, imported payment records, current employer/employee identity revisions, latest employee identity review ID/decision, overtime source/review IDs and the prepared annual values/issues/contributions. Raw payment evidence remains internal; only the digest is returned. Object-key ordering does not change the digest. Revised evidence changes it even when displayed totals remain equal or unavailable. This is a prerequisite for later approval freshness checks; it does not itself save an approval, freeze a form or authorize issuance.


201. Annual input reviews require reconciled 2026 inputs, the current source fingerprint, expected prior review ID, a verification reference and explicit confirmation. A serializable transaction and per-employee/year lock protect concurrent submissions; exact retries reuse the current identical review. Reviews retain an encrypted prepared snapshot and immutable history with current, superseded or stale status recomputed against live inputs. History and audits omit the encrypted snapshot. This records review of retained inputs only; benefit classification, approved tax forms, employee delivery and agency transmission remain separate unfinished steps. The API is implemented; admin form integration is pending.


202. Admin annual preparation includes a review form and immutable history for each employee. Only reconciled inputs expose the save form. Editing the verification reference resets confirmation; saving refreshes preparation and clears the form. A stale-source or concurrent-review response disables saving until preparation is refreshed. History identifies current, superseded and stale reviews. Recording input review is explicitly separate from tax-form classification, approval and issuance. The real-API browser scenario verifies save, edit confirmation reset, stale-source blocking, refresh recovery and superseded history on mobile.


203. Annual-review history can display its encrypted saved input snapshot independently of current payroll. The read endpoint binds facility, employee, review ID, payment year and source fingerprint; invalid ownership is unavailable, and vault errors do not return partial data. The admin view labels the snapshot as historical, displays masked identity and retained annual controls, and clears it before reload, after failed loading or when closed. It does not claim current approval or issued-tax-form status. Backend tests verify unchanged historical values after live payroll changes, cross-facility/employee isolation, authentication and missing-key handling; the browser verifies historic display, close and failure clearing.


204. The 2026 employer health-reporting determination supports REPORT, SMALL_EMPLOYER_RELIEF and UNRESOLVED. Relief requires an explicitly reviewed count of Forms W-2 required for 2025 from zero through 249, plus source reference and confirmation; current app headcount is never used. REPORT and UNRESOLVED can retain a null count. Each correction is append-only with expected revision, actor and audit record; exact retries reuse the current identical determination and competing changes return a conflict. Annual preparation includes the determination separately from annual payment-source fingerprints, because later classification/form approval must bind it independently. This employer determination does not establish any employee reportable coverage cost or authorize tax-form issuance. UI entry and per-employee classification remain pending.


205. Employer setup exposes the 2026 health-reporting determination with an explicit initial load and no preselected disposition. The prior-year count is optional unless small-employer relief is selected. Changes reset confirmation, successful saves refresh and clear inputs, and stale revisions clear the form until history is reloaded. Current and superseded determinations retain evidence, reviewer, date and the reviewed count or its absence. This form does not infer employee coverage costs or issue tax forms.


206. Employee health classifications bind the current 2026 employer determination and reconciled annual payroll fingerprint. REPORT requires a positive verified annual cost in exact cents; RELIEF_USED, NO_APPLICABLE_COVERAGE and UNRESOLVED require a null amount and evidence reference. Relief is only accepted against a current small-employer-relief determination; resolved employee classifications cannot rely on an unresolved employer determination. No coverage cost is inferred from deductions or catalog prices. Serializability, expected revision and immutable history protect corrections; changes to either dependency mark prior classifications stale. Classification history is appended after annual-source hashing so it cannot recursively invalidate payment-input reviews. UI entry and eventual tax-form approval remain pending.


207. Annual preparation exposes employee coverage classification only after an employer determination and reconciled payroll inputs are available. Reported cost entry requires positive exact cents; changing classification clears the amount and resets confirmation. Relief is selectable only for a small-employer-relief determination, and an unresolved employer permits only unresolved employee classification. Saves refresh inputs and history; stale-source responses disable further saves until preparation is refreshed. History distinguishes current and stale classifications and preserves prior verified amounts without presenting them as current. This does not yet constitute approved W-2 mapping or issuance.


208. Compensation applicability review covers retirement, dependent care, taxable fringe benefits, third-party sick pay, tips, equity/deferred compensation, statutory employee treatment and other reportable compensation/exclusions. Every category requires NOT_APPLICABLE, APPLICABLE or UNRESOLVED; none defaults to false or zero. The review requires current reconciled annual inputs, reference and explicit confirmation, with expected revision and immutable history. APPLICABLE identifies further treatment required rather than certifying reporting completion. Applicability history is added after annual-input hashing to avoid recursive invalidation. UI and detailed category treatment are pending.


209. Compensation applicability is entered per employee in annual preparation, using the category catalog returned by the backend. All choices start blank, every category is required, edits reset confirmation and saves refresh the displayed history. Unresolved decisions remain visible rather than becoming zeroes. Stale-source responses require refreshing preparation before another save. Applicable decisions explicitly require additional reporting treatment and do not approve tax forms.


210. W-2 draft mapping requires reconciled annual inputs, current input review, verified identities, resolved/current health classification and current compensation applicability with all additional categories not applicable. Applicable additional categories remain blocked until detailed treatment is implemented. Mapping preserves exact wage/withholding amounts, includes positive DD/TT entries, uses combined Medicare in box 6 and Maryland combined state/local withholding in box 17. Maryland registration is represented by retained employer identity revision and suffix until authorized issuance resolves the full ID. The draft fingerprint binds all review/classification revisions and boxes separately from annual-input fingerprints. No form is issued or approved, and employee deduction limits do not cap TT. Sources: [IRS 2026 W-2 instructions](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/iw2w3), [Maryland 2026 withholding guide](https://www.marylandcomptroller.gov/content/dam/mdcomp/tax/instructions/withholding/2026/withholding-guide.pdf).


211. The admin W-2 draft view shows exact mapped amounts, code entries, reviewed flags and masked Maryland registration only when the backend mapping gate passes. Otherwise it displays missing/stale/unsupported evidence reasons and no draft boxes. The view explicitly distinguishes a draft from an approved or issued form. Refresh removes prior results, so changed payroll cannot leave old mapped amounts visible after the response.


212. W-2 approval requires a current complete supported draft fingerprint, explicit confirmation, reference and expected prior approval revision. Approval freezes mapped boxes and the full employer/employee filing identities selected by immutable revision into an encrypted snapshot. Ordinary history/audits omit full identifiers and form payload. Serializable writes and per-employee/year locking protect concurrent approvals; exact retries reuse the current identical approval. History recomputes current/superseded/stale state from the live draft fingerprint. Approval does not furnish a form, transmit to an agency or execute payroll payments. UI integration and issuance remain pending; migration changes were tested only in isolated databases.


213. Admin annual preparation provides W-2 approval only when a complete supported draft fingerprint is available. Approval evidence edits reset confirmation; successful approval refreshes the view and clears the form. Stale-draft responses require refresh, and missing drafts hide the approval action while preserving history. The interface explicitly states that approval retains form data without delivering or transmitting it.


214. Employee W-2 rendering will use the pinned official 2026 IRS template (SHA-256 in fw2-2026.manifest.json), selecting Copies B, C and 2 and their accompanying instruction pages. The repeated panels on each selected copy will contain the same employee, avoiding unrelated blank employee panels. The canonical field inventory has 94 widgets per employee-copy page and was verified against the PDF field tree. Source template retention does not implement rendering, furnishing or SSA submission. Production runtime support for PDF field filling remains to be connected.

215. W-2 employee copies are generated on demand from a selected retained approval using the checksum-pinned 2026 template and pdf-lib in the backend. Downloads include full filing identifiers, are facility-scoped to authorized admins, use no-store headers and are audited without recording identifier values. Copies B/C/2 and their instruction pages are flattened; Copy A is excluded. Historical approval downloads remain available with stale/superseded labels. Unsupported classifications/codes and text that cannot fit readably fail rather than being silently omitted. Downloading does not itself furnish, issue or file a W-2; a separate delivery/issuance record is still required.

216. The first authorized approval download automatically retains the exact PDF bytes in an encrypted, append-only packet bound to that approval, employee, facility and year. Concurrent first downloads serialize and reuse one artifact. Subsequent downloads verify the stored checksum and return identical bytes, independent of later template or rendering changes. Packet retention is preparation only; it does not claim employee receipt, furnishing or agency filing.

217. Paper furnishing is an admin attestation of an action that already occurred, tied to the exact retained W-2 packet. Mailing requires verification of the recipient/address; hand delivery confirms the employee received their copies. Event time must fall after packet creation, not in the future or before the latest event. Undeliverable returns require a preceding mailing. Records preserve history and do not equate mailing with receipt, send physical mail, establish electronic consent or transmit an agency filing. Historical approval events may be recorded so actual actions are preserved even if current payroll data later changes.

218. W-2 undeliverable follow-up alerts derive from the latest furnishing event for each retained packet. Manual dismissal does not resolve the evidence; scheduled workforce refresh reopens the warning until a subsequent actual mailing or hand delivery is recorded. Alert text identifies employee number, packet and approval without full filing identifiers or evidence references. It asks admins to verify the recipient securely and review stale approvals before reusing copies. Closing this follow-up alert does not certify receipt of a mailing or agency acceptance.

219. A returned W-2 packet may be resolved through a newer same-employee, same-year approval only after its replacement packet has a recorded mailing or hand delivery at or after the return. Admins must explicitly verify the replacement relationship and handle required tax-form corrections separately. Links are append-only, revision-bound and protected by ordered packet locks; changing either furnishing history invalidates the link. Automation reopens the old follow-up alert when a replacement link becomes stale. This is delivery-evidence linkage, not a W-2c generator or agency correction submission.

220. Electronic W-2 consent will cover tax year 2026 only, including its corrections, with paper delivery by default. Disclosures use configured employer name, address and telephone; missing contacts block access checks, and contact/format changes alter the terms fingerprint. The stated portal availability target is at least December 31, 2031, including former employees. Before consent, a session-bound PDF displays a random one-time access code with a 30-minute expiration. Only its hash is stored, and producing or opening the sample does not grant consent. Consent consumption, withdrawal and the promised document availability are still to be implemented before enabling electronic furnishing.

221. Electronic W-2 consent requires an authenticated current session, current disclosure fingerprint, unexpired same-session PDF proof, correct access code, explicit confirmation and signature. Five failed code attempts exhaust a proof; successful consent consumes it once. Exact retries reuse the current record. Signed terms are encrypted and immutable. Withdrawal takes effect when its record is saved, needs no PDF proof or encryption key, and remains available to former employees. Current consent becomes renewal-required when disclosure contacts or format change. The API exposes retained receipts and effective timestamps; employee controls and electronic furnishing remain unfinished.

222. Employees manage 2026 electronic W-2 preferences from the onboarding portal. All disclosure sections are shown before consent; a downloaded sample code, signature and separate confirmation are required. Input edits reset confirmation. Withdrawal has its own explicit confirmation and displays the saved effective time. Both decisions have downloadable text confirmations; signed consent confirmations include the retained disclosure. Reload clears stale records and proof inputs. These controls set a delivery preference and do not imply that a W-2 has been furnished.

223. Publishing a 2026 W-2 requires the current approval, current disclosure-matching electronic consent, explicit confirmation and evidence. It retains the packet/consent relationship immutably and makes the exact encrypted packet available only through employee-authenticated access. Publication is labeled AVAILABLE_NOTICE_PENDING and creates an internal notice-due warning; posting alone is not treated as completed furnishing. Withdrawal blocks new publication but preserves access to existing posted records. Publication takes its serializable snapshot only after acquiring the same consent lock used by employee preference writes; concurrent duplicate publications reuse one record or require refresh. Admin and employee controls and actual notice delivery remain to be connected.

224. Admins review portal publication from the retained approval history. The readiness endpoint withholds the publish action until the approval and signed electronic consent are current and verifiable; publication evidence edits reset confirmation. Published records visibly remain notice-pending. Employees load their own W-2 list under Pay statements and download the retained PDF; failed reloads clear the previously displayed list. Publication controls do not send an availability notice or certify complete furnishing.

225. Each W-2 publication retains the availability notice and recipient in encrypted queue storage with a content digest. The subject is IMPORTANT TAX RETURN DOCUMENT AVAILABLE; the body gives sign-in, document selection, saving, printing and payroll-contact instructions without attaching the W-2 or exposing a private download link. Missing email is NEEDS_CONTACT. Completing email allows a new immutable QUEUED revision; the earlier record remains. Workforce refresh can backfill missing jobs and raises a preparation alert when encryption/configuration prevents it. Queue preparation does not send mail, prove delivery or substitute for a fresh consent/contact check at dispatch.

226. Availability notice dispatch retains an immutable claim before SMTP and an immutable result afterward. Current consent terms, recipient and retained PDF/notice integrity are rechecked under the consent lock. SMTP acceptance is recorded separately from delivery; sender skips are NOT_SENT, and exceptions, duplicate-provider replies or missing results are UNCERTAIN. Neither kind is automatically resent. Workforce automation uses configured transactional mail and maintains alerts when notice work cannot complete. Admin publication history shows attempt status and time without exposing the email body or recipient. Tests inject synthetic senders; no live notices were sent. Retry reconciliation, returned-email handling and fully automated paper fallback remain open.

227. The latest recorded mailing or hand delivery of the exact published W-2 packet resolves pending notice follow-up when its event time is on or after publication. Earlier SMTP outcomes remain visible and immutable. Paper-first furnishing suppresses an unstarted electronic send even if consent has since been withdrawn. A later returned mailing reopens notice follow-up unless an electronic notice was accepted; the separate returned-packet alert remains responsible for paper delivery follow-up. Alerts update with furnishing evidence and automation rechecks them under the packet furnishing lock. Publication exposes AVAILABLE_PAPER_RECORDED separately from mail acceptance. Pre-publication paper evidence and furnishing of a different packet do not silently resolve this task.

228. An explicitly verified replacement-packet furnishing link can resolve the original publication’s notice follow-up. The latest original event must still be the linked return, and the linked replacement event must still be that packet’s latest mailing or handoff, no earlier than the return. A newer packet alone does not resolve the task. The publication panel identifies the replacement packet, verification link and furnishing event. Returning the replacement makes the fallback stale and automation reopens notice work unless an electronic notice was accepted. Existing employee portal documents and SMTP evidence remain retained. This extends assumption 227’s exact-packet fallback through the explicit replacement verification workflow.

229. Workforce automation reevaluates all unattempted publication notices. Changed recipient or prepared notice content creates a new immutable encrypted revision; unchanged content reuses the current job. Missing or invalid email produces NEEDS_CONTACT. Preparation serializes with dispatch and stops revising once any attempt has been retained, so contact correction cannot silently reset attempted, accepted or uncertain delivery evidence. Post-attempt recovery requires the controlled retry/reconciliation workflow rather than an automatic new job.

230. Definite NOT_SENT outcomes may retry automatically up to three total attempts: the second attempt no earlier than one day after the first, and the third no earlier than two days after the second. Each result retains its next eligible time immutably. SMTP acceptance, uncertainty and missing result evidence never authorize an automatic retry. Eligibility is rechecked under the consent lock; a retry revalidates consent, current recipient and retained artifacts. Eligible definite failures may receive a new encrypted notice revision for corrected contact details, extending assumption 229’s post-attempt restriction through this bounded policy. Exhaustion stays actionable and points admins to paper furnishing. The publication panel shows planned timing, attempt count and retained outcome history. Tests use an injected clock and sender; no live notices were sent.

231. Uncertain or missing-result notice attempts can be resolved from retained email_delivery acceptance evidence for the exact facility, dispatch idempotency key, recipient hash, category and template. Source creation must follow the attempt, acceptance must follow source creation, and bounced/complained records do not qualify. No absence or generic failed/sent status proves acceptance or permits another send. Reconciliation retains a separate immutable source snapshot; the original payroll result remains unchanged. Effective status, retry eligibility, alerts and admin history use the reconciled acceptance. The history explicitly labels the reconciliation and original uncertainty. This recovery never calls the sender. Later returned electronic notices still require their own follow-up workflow.

232. Workforce automation retains an immutable returned-notice record when email_delivery has a matching bounced event for the exact facility, dispatch key, recipient hash, category/template and consistent timestamps. Return evidence takes precedence over prior SMTP acceptance or its reconciliation for notice status, preventing automatic resending and reopening unresolved notice follow-up. Existing acceptance and reconciliation records remain retained. The admin panel labels the electronic return and directs staff to paper furnishing; current paper fallback can still resolve the task. This depends on a bounce reaching the existing mail log; asynchronous provider ingestion, manual return entry and deadline tracking remain unfinished.

233. Returned electronic notices receive an internal paper follow-up target 30 calendar days after the earliest retained return date, using the employer timezone. The UI distinguishes open, due within seven days, overdue, and paper completion on time or late. Automation includes the target and current state in unresolved notice alerts. Actual retained paper furnishing resolves the task and preserves its event date; no date is shifted merely because a later notice return is observed. This is a conservative operational target: the regulatory mail/in-person requirement applies when a correct electronic address cannot be obtained. Manual return intake and provider event ingestion remain unfinished.

The return target timezone and date are retained immutably when a return is captured; later employer timezone changes do not shift that target. Legacy return rows without target metadata use the current employer timezone until a dedicated legacy review path is added.

234. Hiring admins can record an electronic return received outside the mail log from a published approval’s notice history. The form requires a selected accepted/uncertain attempt, actual local return time, evidence reference and explicit confirmation; edits and cancellation reset confirmation. The API enforces facility/employee/publication ownership, rejects future or pre-attempt times and definitely unsent attempts, retains actor/source/reference and target metadata immutably, reuses exact retries and rejects conflicting evidence. The notice becomes returned and its target appears in alerts immediately. Existing provider-return evidence cannot be replaced by a manual entry. Correcting retained return records and asynchronous provider intake remain separate unfinished work.

235. Actual direct-deposit execution will use Modern Treasury with the employer's connected bank for USD ACH PPD credits. This assumption does not purchase or configure a service. Instructions retain provider account IDs rather than bank numbers, with separate TEST/LIVE identity and one immutable instruction per employee/run/mode. Stable external IDs supplement API-key-scoped, time-limited idempotency. Account verification is required but does not replace employee authorization. Provider completion, reconciliation, changed dates and later returns are distinct; no adapter result alone marks payroll paid. Check, zero-net, replacement and remittance flows still require their own execution rules. The initial adapter and retention layer are tested but not yet connected to the admin page.

236. Hiring admins may save employer Modern Treasury credentials and funding-account references in Employer setup using the existing payroll encryption key. Every changed configuration creates an immutable revision with an identified admin and encrypted evidence reference; public status and audit metadata omit credentials and provider account identifiers. Exact retries reuse the current revision; conflicting stale edits require refresh. The form defaults to TEST, requires explicit confirmation and clears entered API keys after save attempts. Configuration is labeled unverified and never authorizes or initiates payments. Connection verification, disabling/rotation behavior for in-flight payments, employee destination enrollment and actual dispatch remain implementation work.

237. Funding-account verification uses a read-only Modern Treasury internal-account lookup for the saved configuration revision. Exact account identity, USD currency and test/live mode must match. Credential/access errors and missing accounts are failed checks; network/server errors are unavailable checks. Only sanitized outcomes and admin/timestamp metadata are retained, not provider response bodies. Latest results are displayed explicitly as the last check, and configuration replacement starts unverified. Checks are not proof of sufficient funds, employee authorization or future availability; execution must perform its own current checks. Test harnesses reject external payment transport by default and inject synthetic responses for verification tests.

238. The initial employee destination path links an already verified Modern Treasury individual checking/savings account through an admin-reviewed provider ID. The service requires a counterparty, matching test/live mode and a single usable four-digit account suffix, retaining only selected provider fields and review evidence under authenticated encryption. It does not copy provider bank/routing numbers. Admin linking does not prove employee authorization and does not change direct-deposit status to ACTIVE. Connection changes require a new destination revision, even when the underlying account is unchanged. This is the existing-account path; creating/verifying a new account entirely in the portal, employee authorization/revocation and dispatch remain required to satisfy the full one-stop goal.

239. Employee authorization permits wage credits to the displayed account and expressly does not authorize debits. Employees affirm ownership or permitted use, sign the displayed employer/account terms and may choose check payment. Withdrawal applies to payments not yet submitted and does not reverse an existing payment. Each decision is immutable and bound to the employee session/destination; authorizations retain encrypted terms and signature, and downloadable confirmations are available in the employee portal. Terms fingerprints prevent stale review and employer/account changes from silently carrying authorization forward. Former employees can withdraw but cannot newly authorize. The withdrawal API can record a decision without the encryption key; viewing encrypted account/receipt details still requires it. Dispatch must consume current authorization under the same locks before sending; that integration remains unfinished.

240. Completing pay review for a direct-deposit election requires a current LIVE employer connection, a destination bound to that connection, current employee authorization for the displayed employer/account terms and a latest passed funding-account check. The previous manual ACTIVE flag is insufficient. Check payment retains its existing election/review flow. Connection/destination/authorization identifiers and the current terms fingerprint become part of the retained pay-review basis; withdrawal, new authorization or changed evidence invalidate prior review. This is enrollment readiness, not payment authorization or proof of current provider availability. Dispatch must recheck the provider and lock the current authorization before submitting any funds.

241. An approved run's payment plan separates positive-net check and direct-deposit payments from zero-net employee lines. Positive-net employees require a reviewed payment election, and direct deposits require current enrollment readiness. The plan checks current payroll inputs and net-total reconciliation, returns actionable issues and a deterministic fingerprint, and neither retains executable instructions nor transmits funds. Preview initialization is rolled back. The initial integrated tests cover check payments, missing direct-deposit enrollment, changed employment inputs, tenant isolation and total mismatch; mixed and zero-net execution still need dedicated end-to-end validation. Completing the payment-method review now sets the legacy direct-deposit flag to INVITED, not ACTIVE; current bank readiness remains derived separately.

242. Admin payment authorization retains one batch per approved run, including the exact plan fingerprint, review reference and actor. Exact retries reuse that batch; conflicting decisions are rejected. Direct-deposit instructions bind stable provider account references and amounts to the batch; checks/zero-net lines remain in the retained plan. Active batches block manual finalization and voiding to prevent bypass. Cancellation is permitted only before a dispatch claim, retains immutable evidence and releases that guard; reauthorization of a cancelled batch requires a new run. Dispatch and cancellation share run-row locking and database guards. No provider request is made when authorizing or cancelling. Actual dispatch, reconciliation, completed-batch finalization and in-flight exception handling remain unfinished.

243. A new direct-deposit dispatch must revalidate the exact retained plan and employee authorization, then commit a unique claim before any provider submission. A later invocation with an existing claim only reads the provider by immutable external ID; missing records, lost responses and failed observation writes never authorize another POST. Provider observations are append-only, including returns after initial processing; no observed status automatically marks payroll paid. Recovery uses the retained connection revision and remains possible after employee withdrawal. The session-level connection lock is retained across provider I/O, with settings/run locks released after claiming and never reacquired for observation persistence. The initial coordinator is internal only and requires injected transport/calculation dependencies; user-facing dispatch, scheduling, definite-pre-submission failure release, reconciliation and finalization remain required.

244. A dispatch claim may be released through batch cancellation only when every claimed instruction has affirmative SUBMISSION evidence of BLOCKED_ACCOUNT_LOOKUP or BLOCKED_ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION, no contradictory submission outcome and no provider payment ID in any retained observation. Unclaimed instructions do not prevent cancellation. UNCERTAIN, missing observations and NOT_FOUND alone are insufficient. A later lookup that cannot find a previously observed provider payment never restores cancellation eligibility. The API and database use the same predicate and connection/run locking; eligibility reads fresh evidence after waiting. Claims and observations remain immutable after cancellation, and cancelled instructions cannot dispatch. A replacement authorization still requires voiding/rebuilding the run.


245. Admins explicitly confirm the retained payment amount/date before submitting an individual ACH instruction. Submission is scoped to facility, run, batch and instruction and requires the retained fingerprint. A repeated SUBMIT after claiming performs read-only recovery; the RECOVER action cannot create a claim or payment. Confirmation resets after an action or refreshed data. Submission uses the configured employer provider credentials, while development tests inject synthetic transport. An observed processing/completed status does not by itself finalize payroll. Automatic execution and settlement-backed finalization remain separate unfinished functions.


246. A completed/reconciled ACH order requires independently fetched posted USD debit transactions from the retained employer account and originating line items linked to the exact provider payment order. Matching line-item cents must sum to the employee instruction; bulk transactions may include other employees. Pending entries, duplicates, partial amounts, wrong accounts/modes/currencies and changed effective dates do not qualify. Bank reads are bounded to ten transactions, ten pages of 100 line items per transaction and a 45-second aggregate bank-evidence deadline. Truncated/unavailable evidence requires review; it cannot certify payment. A second order read must still match before BANK_POSTED evidence is retained. Later returns replace current eligibility with EXCEPTION while immutable prior observations remain. Posted bank evidence does not imply irrevocability or automatically finalize the payroll run.


247. Payroll closeout uses bank-posted observations no older than 15 minutes for every direct deposit and records actual check delivery against the approved date and exact employee net amount. Zero-net lines need no transfer. Check references and links to the exact bank observations are immutable. Closeout runs under settings/connection/run locks and the same statement, leave, correction, period and QuickBooks finalization path as recorded external payments. Repeating the same completed closeout returns the retained result without another statement/leave settlement; conflicting retries reject. A finalized authorization cannot be cancelled. Later provider recovery remains available and can expose a return without erasing the finalized history; automated remediation/reissue is still required.


248. A mixed payroll closes as one run: positive-net direct deposits require bank evidence, positive-net checks require exact delivery evidence, and zero-net employees receive a statement without a payment instruction. The integrated fixture uses an active hourly employee with no work for the zero-net case; other causes of zero net retain the calculation engine’s existing validation. All employee statements and one run closeout are retained atomically, including concurrent closeout retries.


249. The server checks existing payment attempts automatically: every five minutes it selects up to 25 due attempts, with ten minutes between checks on approved runs and one day after finalization. Finalized payments remain monitored without an arbitrary age cutoff. A global advisory lock prevents overlapping sweeps. Each scheduled check is retained before work, including failed/crashed attempts, so failures receive a retry delay instead of starving later instructions. Recovery is always read-only and cannot create a dispatch claim. Exceptions create deduplicated internal payroll alerts; no employee communications or replacement payments are sent. PAYROLL_PAYMENT_RECOVERY_ENABLED=false disables the scheduler, and test servers never start its timers. Automatic closeout and payment replacement remain separate unfinished work.


250. Automatic closeout requires a retained admin request for the exact batch, fingerprint, payment date and check records. Check deliveries cannot be confirmed for a future date. The worker waits for current bank evidence and the approved date, then uses the same atomic finalization operation as the admin action. Requests and cancellations are immutable. Authorization is checked again under execution locks, so cancellation after queue selection prevents finalization. Failed eligible requests receive a ten-minute retry delay and an internal alert. Automatic closeout uses the requesting admin’s retained identity and never creates a payment. A cancelled automatic request can be closed manually when ready; it cannot be silently re-enabled.


251. A scheduled payment retains the exact instruction, admin reference and UTC submission instant; the UI accepts device-local time and displays it in that same local convention. This is provider submission timing, not a bank-arrival promise. Submission must be scheduled no later than the approved pay date in the employer timezone. A separate one-minute worker selects up to 25 due instructions, serializes overlapping workers, revalidates current payroll and employee authorization, and rejects new submission after the approved date. Scheduling does not claim or send funds. Cancellation is locked against dispatch; manual submission requires cancellation of an active schedule. A failed pre-claim check gets a ten-minute retry delay and alert; once claimed, recovery handles the instruction without another POST. PAYROLL_PAYMENT_SUBMISSION_ENABLED=false disables this worker, and test environments never start its timer. Cancelled schedules remain immutable and cannot be silently re-enabled.


252. A returned-payment notice is not proof that funds posted back. Recovery requires a completed/reconciled ACH return linked to the original order and full amount, the correct employer account/environment, a posted USD credit and its exact matching return line item. Partial returns, notices of change, pending entries, mismatches and changes during verification do not qualify. Only selected IDs, amount, posted date and a validated return code are retained; raw reasons and bank data are excluded. This evidence does not itself authorize a replacement, alter finalized wages or duplicate payroll taxes. Replacement and accounting remediation remain required.


253. Initial internal bank enrollment supports US individual checking/savings accounts with numeric account numbers of 4–17 digits and checksum-valid nine-digit routing numbers, preserving leading zeros. Provider counterparty and account identities are stable per enrollment. Creation requires a separately retained operation claim; recovery performs lookups without another POST. Micro-deposit verification requires separate consent to its credits and matching recovery debits, distinct from wage-credit authorization. Completion accepts two whole-cent amounts and uses a retained operation ID. The employee workflow must enforce attempt limits and uncertain-operation recovery before these adapters are exposed. No employee bank data or real micro-deposits were submitted in development.

254. Bank enrollment is an employee-owned, encrypted request bound to the employer connection and signed verification terms. US checking/savings account numbers are entered twice in the form and preserved as strings; only the last four digits appear after saving. Routing/account values and verification amounts are not written to audit records. Saving does not change the payment election or authorize wages. The employee explicitly starts verification; the form advances through separately committed counterparty, account and micro-deposit operations while each outcome is affirmative. Recovery never repeats a provider POST. An unresolved outcome requires recovery or payroll review. Each completion attempt has its own retained identity and encrypted amounts; a further attempt requires an affirmative rejected response followed by current pending status, with five attempts maximum. The local completion window is conservatively limited to 56 days after initiation. A verified account can be linked using evidence no older than 15 minutes, with a current-destination revision check. Linking replaces the displayed account and requires separate wage authorization. Employees cannot act for another employee, and former employees can inspect retained enrollment but cannot start or link one. Admins see masked enrollment progress in People & onboarding. These are application assumptions, not a claim that provider testing or employer-specific authorization review has been completed.

255. Bank-accounting reconciliation treats provider-confirmed withdrawals and returned credits as movements of existing net pay, not additional wages or tax calculations. A live retained instruction, matching payment identity, exact complete line-item amounts and valid posted dates are required. Repeated observations of the same movement are collapsed; changed transaction/date/line evidence, different provider identities, missing original withdrawals, duplicate bank lines and later unresolved provider states require review. Evidence is bound to the originating provider account so future mapping can distinguish bank cash from payroll clearing. Bank-movement review is read-only. Separate settlement-journal controls (assumption 257) can post against a retained mapping; employee replacement payments remain a separate required workflow.

256. Bank settlement accounting uses a separate active QuickBooks Bank account and active Other Current Liability clearing account, with a verified USD home currency and no explicitly non-USD selected account. The clearing ID must equal the current payroll journal mapping. The bookkeeper confirms that the chosen bank represents the retained payroll funding account; provider IDs alone cannot establish that cross-system relationship. Each mapping retains account names/types, funding connection, QuickBooks company/environment, disconnect generation and review reference. History is immutable. Changes to the funding revision, company/environment, disconnect generation or payroll-clearing selection make the saved mapping stale. Verification reads provider account/preferences data; saving the mapping creates no journal. Posting must revalidate current account state and reconcile the frozen payroll journal before using a mapping.

257. Settlement journals record only retained bank movements: withdrawals debit payroll clearing and credit bank cash; returned credits reverse those entries. The reviewed current mapping must match the funding source and the original confirmed payroll journal's clearing credit/net amount. Before new posting, QuickBooks account/preferences data and the original journal are read again and compared with retained evidence. Return posting additionally requires confirmed, unchanged withdrawal journals using the same accounts. An admin confirms the movement has not already been entered manually or by a bank rule; that review is retained. One immutable job and committed claim identify each event/company/environment before its possible POST. Stable document numbers and exact payload comparison support read-only recovery; missing, ambiguous, duplicate, changed or unconfirmed provider results never authorize a second POST. Unresolved results open an internal alert, cleared only by confirmation. This does not reissue employee funds or alter wages/taxes. Automatic settlement scheduling, verified preflight-block release, historical-funding mapping remediation, check-clearing entries and employee replacement payments remain required follow-up work.

258. Retained, claimed settlement journals are eligible for automatic read-only recovery after ten minutes without an observation/check; confirmed journals are rechecked after one day. A five-minute worker starts after sixty seconds, is disabled in tests and can be disabled with PAYROLL_SETTLEMENT_RECOVERY_ENABLED=false. A global advisory lock prevents overlapping sweeps; oldest eligible jobs run first, with 25 per sweep (bounded override 1–100). Immutable check rows commit before each lookup, so unavailable credentials and crashed work receive a delay instead of starving newer jobs. The worker uses only the existing RECOVER action and cannot create a new journal. Missing or changed journals remain review items; matching evidence dismisses the journal's alert. Connection errors retain a generic internal alert without credentials. Recovery continues against the original company/environment even when local account mappings change, but a different connected company is blocked. These intervals and limits are operational assumptions. Automatic authorization of new settlement postings and evidence-backed preflight-block release remain separate unfinished work.

259. Employees and payroll-managing admins can inspect paginated masked bank-enrollment history and recover an individual retained operation, including an enrollment superseded by a replacement account. History excludes routing numbers, full account numbers, verification amounts, consent signatures and provider credentials. Recovery uses the enrollment's original encrypted employer connection and provider identities; it never creates an operation, account, verification deposit, completion attempt, payment destination or wage authorization. An expired completion window or exhausted attempts does not disable read-only status checks. Expiry uses the same 56-day cutoff as completion, and verified evidence is not relabeled expired. Current enrollment still governs verification/linking: a recovered previous account cannot replace the current wage destination. Recovery is audited with scoped actor/session and operation identity. Unavailable historical credentials need employer connection remediation; this implementation does not assume a missing provider record permits restarting a previously claimed operation. Explicit unresolved-operation disposition, reuse of refreshed credentials for the same organization and automated enrollment recovery remain unfinished.

260. Same-account verification restart creates a new enrollment cycle linked immutably to its predecessor. It requires fresh employee consent/signature under current terms, the same current employer connection, prior retained evidence that verification reached pending status, fresh matching holder/account lookups and an affirmative provider `unverified` result. Pending, verified, missing, ambiguous or mismatched provider state cannot start a new cycle. Already-linked enrollments use the replacement-account workflow instead. Preparing a cycle performs only provider GETs, retains eligibility evidence and copies confirmed holder/account identities into the new cycle; the employee must separately continue to send new deposits. Each cycle receives its own committed START and up to five COMPLETE claims; old attempts and unresolved responses remain retained. The provider's original external account/holder identity is preserved across cycles. Duplicate preparation reuses the same child, and recovery never replays a provider POST. Successful new verification still requires separate account linking and wage authorization. Unobserved initial creation, missing prior verification evidence, changed employer connections and unavailable credentials remain separate remediation cases.

261. Automatic bank-enrollment recovery is read-only. A five-minute worker starts after sixty seconds, is disabled in tests and can be disabled with PAYROLL_BANK_ENROLLMENT_RECOVERY_ENABLED=false. It selects at most 25 enrollments per sweep (bounded override 1–100), checking unresolved/pending work after ten minutes and current verified accounts after one day. Missing/failed holder or account prerequisites are checked before later operations; operations with no retained response receive priority. Each attempt gets a committed, append-only scheduling record before provider access so failures and crashes receive a delay and do not starve other enrollments. Overlapping sweeps use a global advisory lock. Previously restarted cycles are excluded; unresolved superseded account enrollments can still be recovered. Saved enrollments with no operation are not started, and completed holder-only or unverified account-only setup requires the employee's Continue action. Automatic checks cannot send deposits, complete amounts, restart a cycle, link a destination or authorize wages. Internal alerts identify unknown/failed outcomes, ended verification, expiry and exhausted attempts; affirmative recovery clears resolved alerts. Preparing a valid restart clears the predecessor's resolved expiry/attempt-limit alert, while new unknown/mismatched historical results remain reviewable. No employee message is sent.

The employee form refreshes loaded pending/unresolved enrollment state every thirty seconds while visible and idle. It preserves entered values on background read failures and clears stale confirmations when the enrollment or terms change. Polling reads application state only; it does not call the provider or initiate verification.

262. Returned-payment replacement review is a retained assessment, not payment authorization. It binds the full original net amount, reconciled withdrawal/posted return, current payment election and bank-authorization readiness, proposed replacement date, unpaid-balance reference and a separately reviewed wage/tax-date treatment. An admin must affirm that the amount remains owed and no other replacement has been made. No treatment is preselected; keeping original reporting and requiring correction are distinct retained decisions. Dates cannot precede the original payment or posted return. Conflicting/stale reviews are rejected, history is immutable, and source changes require renewed review. Reviews never mutate wages, withholding, statements, payroll status or payment claims. Annual preparation blocks returned payments without tax-date review, declared correction requirements and changed/unreconciled bank evidence; factual changes invalidate annual review/approval fingerprints, while identical provider rechecks do not. Review evidence is separate from proof that any correction or replacement was actually performed. Replacement dispatch, check issuance, replacement settlement, repeated-return chains, employee-facing resolution receipts and corrected-form execution remain unfinished. This first review path requires finalized payroll and posted returned funds; it does not cover every failed/pending payment or establish permission to delay wages.

263. Replacement payment authorization is separate from both wage review and dispatch. It requires the latest unchanged review to retain original payroll reporting, a future/current proposed date in the employer timezone, current payment-election/readiness checks, an exact full net amount and explicit authorization/return-resolution references. ACH instructions retain current live funding/account identities, wage-authorization revision and masked account details; check instructions contain no ACH destination. Each replacement receives a new identity, while the original payroll instruction remains intact. One active authorization is permitted per original instruction, including under concurrent requests. An exact retry reuses the retained authorization; a changed request requires cancelling the unstarted authorization first. Cancellation and dispatch claims are mutually exclusive under database locks, and all records are append-only. An instruction with any dispatch claim cannot be cancelled through this path. Authorizing or cancelling does not send funds, print a check, dismiss the original returned-payment exception, alter taxes or change statements. Provider submission/recovery, bank-backed completion, definite preflight-block release, check issuance and repeated-return chains remain unfinished.

264. Replacement ACH dispatch uses the separately retained replacement UUID and original full unpaid net amount. Before its first claim, it requires the unchanged latest review, current direct-deposit election and employee authorization, matching current funding/destination revisions and an unexpired employer-local payment date. The provider adapter separately verifies live USD funding and a verified recipient account. A committed unique claim precedes the possible provider POST; concurrent calls and all later calls recover by GET using that same instruction identity, including after a lost response. Recovery never repeats a POST or changes the original finalized payroll. Employer configuration remains locked through the request and retained observation. Check authorizations cannot use the ACH endpoint. Scoped immutable provider observations and internal exception alerts retain unknown outcomes. Any claim disables cancellation, including definite preflight blocks pending a separate evidence-backed release path. The admin explicitly confirms the retained amount/date/destination before initial sending. Automatic replacement recovery, bank-backed completion, employee receipts, check issuance, replacement accounting and repeated-return handling remain unfinished.

265. Submitted replacement ACH instructions receive automatic read-only recovery. The worker starts after sixty seconds, runs every five minutes, is disabled in tests and respects PAYROLL_REPLACEMENT_RECOVERY_ENABLED=false. It checks at most 25 due instructions per sweep (bounded override 1–100), with ten-minute unresolved and daily completed/BANK_POSTED intervals. A global advisory lock prevents overlapping sweeps, and each immutable check is committed before provider access to preserve retry delay and fairness after failure or crash. Unstarted and cancelled authorizations cannot be selected. The shared dispatch coordinator receives recoveryOnly=true and cannot send a payment; automatic observations are audited. Unknown/adverse/date-mismatched results open internal alerts. Fresh completed, live, matching-date BANK_POSTED recovery dismisses only that replacement's alert; later evidence changes reopen it. This does not resolve the original returned-payment case, create a completion receipt, post replacement accounting, issue a check or send employee messages. Original case closure, employee receipt and downstream accounting still require connected completion handling.

266. Completed live replacement ACH recovery with matching payment date and BANK_POSTED evidence automatically retains one immutable bank-evidence receipt per replacement authorization in the same transaction as the observation. The receipt preserves the original pay date, replacement amount/date, masked destination and source bank posting evidence. Its database guard binds the authorization, source recovery and exact snapshot; duplicate recovery cannot create duplicate receipts. Employee Pay statements and admin replacement review display the receipt, without exposing admin references, provider account IDs or credentials. Employees are scoped to their own facility/employee identity. A receipt is evidence of the employer-side bank movement, not an employee account-balance acknowledgment or a second wage/tax statement. Later unknown, returned, mismatched or changed bank evidence marks the retained receipt Needs review; it is never silently replaced. Original returned-payment case closure, downloadable receipt artifacts, check receipts, replacement accounting and repeated-return remediation remain unfinished. No wages, taxes, original statements or employee messages are created by receipt retention.

267. Bank accounting includes claimed replacement ACH movements with their separate instruction/observation identity, original-payment link and existing exact bank-evidence validation. Totals include original withdrawals, returns and replacement withdrawals/returns without changing wage/tax calculations. Duplicate bank line items across any movements block posting. Unresolved replacement evidence blocks that replacement's journal while allowing independently reconciled original movements to be posted. A replacement withdrawal requires confirmed original withdrawal and returned-credit journals in the same QuickBooks destination with matching current mapping; those source journals are fetched and compared again before a new claim. Replacement returns use the existing withdrawal-before-return rule. Immutable settlement jobs/claims, exact document identity, GET-only recovery and scheduled journal recovery apply equally to replacement movements. UI labels distinguish replacement journals. Historical funding/mapping changes, automatic authorization of new journals, original return-case closure, check accounting and repeat replacement issuance remain unfinished. No new wages, taxes or real external postings were made in validation.

268. A returned-payment case closes automatically only when the original payroll remains finalized; original bank-return evidence still matches the authorized unpaid-wage/tax-date review and return code; the current replacement has a bank-confirmed receipt with no unresolved/returned movement; the original payroll journal is synced; and all original/replacement bank movements have matching synced journals in the connected QuickBooks company/environment. Overlapping bank line items prevent closure. Case closure dismisses the original returned-payment alert; later bank, review, journal or connection changes reopen it. Payment and settlement observations refresh the assessment within their transaction, preserving original payroll amounts. Repeated identical evidence does not create duplicate assessment history. A database-only worker starts after sixty seconds, checks up to 25 oldest-due runs every five minutes with a ten-minute per-run delay, and is disabled in tests or with PAYROLL_RETURN_CASE_REVIEW_ENABLED=false. Immutable checks preserve fairness after failure; overlap is locked out; failed sweeps raise an internal review alert. The admin reads current case status and up to twenty retained history entries. Cases use retained provider/accounting evidence; remote changes become known through provider/journal recovery. Closing a case does not authorize another payment, issue a check, amend tax forms or claim the employee acknowledged their account balance. Repeated replacement issuance, historical mapping remediation, automatic authorization of new journals and remaining agency/correction execution stay unfinished.

269. A returned replacement can be followed by a new, explicitly reviewed authorization linked through predecessor_id. The prior executed cycle must have full reconciled withdrawal and returned-credit evidence; uncertain, missing or changed evidence blocks new review/dispatch. The next date cannot precede the latest returned credit. Authorization rechecks current employee consent, method, destination, amount and review; the database binds predecessor, review and instruction and still permits only one active authorization. Concurrent exact retries reuse one successor. Cancelling an unstarted successor preserves the owed amount and allows a fresh authorization against the same returned predecessor. Every sent cycle keeps its distinct provider identity, observations, receipt and accounting history; superseded cycles remain recoverable. Annual preparation requires renewed unpaid-wage/tax-date review when another replacement returns. Each successor withdrawal journal requires the preceding cycle's withdrawal and returned-credit journals, including fresh remote comparison. Case closure reconciles every executed cycle, rather than ignoring earlier returns; a subsequent review of identical paid facts does not force another payment. Prior receipt history remains retained. Check execution, historical mapping remediation, automatic new-journal authorization, receipt-download/history refinements and remaining agency/correction workflows remain unfinished.

270. Internal check execution will use the provider's digital-check payment rail and generated PDF, with separate payee creation, payment claim, document retention and delivery stages. The adapter retains exact payee/funding identities, amount, date, mode and expiration; its default is ninety days and the supported bound is one through 180 days. New creation requires explicit allowCreate after a durable coordinator claim, reviewed digital-check enablement, current employer-local payment date and matching live USD funding/name-only recipient. Recovery defaults to GET and never infers that a missing record permits another POST. PDF retrieval requires one provider-owned rendered_check document for the retained payment, application/pdf content, a PDF header, a five MiB limit, unexpired matching payment evidence and a final payment-state recheck. Download redirects receive no provider credentials and require a server-owned, explicitly trusted HTTPS origin; redirect chains are refused. Generated PDF availability is separate from bank settlement and employee delivery. The current checkpoint is the provider adapter only: saved employer activation, durable check/payee claims, admin/employee UI, encrypted PDF retention, delivery acknowledgment, stop/void/reissue and check accounting remain unfinished. Existing CHECK elections are not assumed to authorize email or require an employee to print a digital check. No provider creation or message was sent outside synthetic tests.


271. Digital-check activation is an employer attestation tied to one retained payment connection, not an inferred provider capability or authorization to issue wages. Admin > Payroll > Employer setup records enablement/disablement, a reference and expiration of 1–180 days (default 90). Enabling a changed setup requires the latest funding-account verification to be VERIFIED and no older than fifteen minutes. That funding check establishes access, account identity, currency and environment, not digital-check activation itself. Changing payment credentials or funding connection requires a fresh check setup for the new revision. Disablement does not cancel previously issued checks. Revisions and audit entries are immutable, employer-scoped and serialized with payment-connection changes; exact duplicate submissions reuse one revision and competing changed submissions conflict. The current form records setup only; durable payee/issuance claims, encrypted PDF retention, employee delivery arrangements/acknowledgment, check settlement/accounting and stop/void/reissue still need to be connected. Existing CHECK elections do not imply consent to email or self-printing.


272. Check recipient setup is an admin-reviewed legal-name record, separate from issuing wages or delivering a check. Each encrypted recipient revision belongs to one employer, employee and retained payment connection. A changed name or connection creates a new revision with its own stable provider identity; the old revision remains recoverable. Current enabled check setup is required to save a recipient or start an unclaimed provider step. Each COUNTERPARTY and ACCOUNT stage has one immutable, committed claim before any possible provider POST. Concurrent requests serialize on the connection lock, and every later request for that stage is GET-only, including when the provider record is absent. ACCOUNT requires a retained successful COUNTERPARTY observation. Read-only recovery uses the original connection and remains possible after setup disablement or a newer recipient revision. The admin UI omits provider IDs, shows stage status, supports earlier-record recovery, and blocks creation while the name field contains an unsaved edit. Recipient creation does not imply employee payment election, delivery consent, check settlement or payment authorization; those are separate checks required at issuance. A missing claimed provider record requires remediation rather than an automatic create retry.
