Automatic recipient recovery, definitive preflight remediation, durable check issuance, encrypted PDF retention, delivery, stop/void/reissue and check accounting remain unfinished.


273. Previously claimed check-recipient operations are automatically recovered using GET-only provider lookups, including historical recipient revisions and disabled current setup. The worker starts after sixty seconds and runs every five minutes, selects at most 25 due operations by default (configurable 1–100), and uses a global overlap lock. Unresolved or alerted operations retry after ten minutes; successfully recorded operations are rechecked daily. An immutable check is written before attempting recovery, preserving bounded retry fairness after failure. Internal per-stage alerts open for uncertain/missing/mismatched observations or worker failure and close only after that stage is recorded successfully. Recovery cannot create an unclaimed recipient step, issue a payment or deliver a check. PAYROLL_CHECK_PAYEE_RECOVERY_ENABLED=false pauses the worker; NODE_ENV=test disables startup timers. The admin component polls local status every thirty seconds while visible and idle, cancels pending state updates when editing begins, and never submits provider mutations from its timer. Automatic creation of later stages, definitive preflight remediation, durable issuance, PDF retention, delivery, stop/void/reissue and check accounting remain unfinished.


274. Digital-check issuance begins with a separate review of one CHECK employee in an active approved payment batch. The current payroll calculation, net wages, payment election and batch fingerprint must still match. The review binds the current live connection, explicit activation revision/expiration, latest encrypted legal-name recipient and matching identity/account evidence. Funding and both recipient stages must have successful evidence within fifteen minutes. The employer-local approved payment date cannot be past. Retained manual check delivery, including any automatic-closeout request even after cancellation, blocks preparation of another check until a separate delivery-remediation process establishes what actually happened. Cancelling closeout does not undo a delivered check. A stable fingerprint includes exact internal identities, amount/date and configuration, while API/UI responses omit provider IDs and credentials. Identical successful evidence recovery preserves the fingerprint; changed setup changes it. The endpoint uses a repeatable-read transaction and rolls back the existing preview initialization work, so reviewing does not persist changes or send a provider request. This checkpoint exposes review only (executionAvailable=false); a durable check claim, duplicate/cancellation/closeout guards, provider submission, encrypted document retention and delivery remain unfinished. An external manual check not recorded in this system will also require an explicit no-prior-payment review before eventual issuance.


275. The backend check-issuance coordinator retains one immutable check claim per employer/run/employee before any provider payment POST. It rechecks the approved review fingerprint under settings, payment-connection and run locks, requires an explicit no-prior-payment attestation and reference, encrypts the exact instruction, and uses a distinct stable check identity. Every request after a claim exists recovers that identity with GET only—even after lost responses, current setup disablement, payment-election changes or a later local date. No missing provider record permits a second creation. Database guards bind claims to the approved CHECK amount/date and scoped live connection/recipient, exclude prior delivery/cancelled authorization, prevent batch cancellation once a check claim exists and prevent manual/automatic closeout from substituting an unverified check reference. Recovery also binds the first observed provider check ID; a different provider record requires review. Known matching provider evidence resolves issuance uncertainty alerts; it does not establish employee delivery or payroll completion. The current backend supports submission/recovery through the authenticated issue endpoint, while the UI still exposes review only until document retention and delivery are connected. Claimed checks intentionally keep the payroll run open. PDF retention/download, actual delivery acknowledgment, automatic check-status recovery, definitive preflight release, stop/void/reissue and check accounting remain unfinished. No live funds or checks were created during implementation tests.


276. Provider-generated check PDFs are retained encrypted under the issued-check identity. Retrieval must match the first observed provider payment ID, one owned provider document, its bounded PDF bytes/hash and a fresh matching SENT check with valid date/expiry. Repeated retention reuses identical evidence; changed documents are rejected instead of replacing the original. Payable admin download is a POST requiring payroll.manage through the existing permission bridge; GET exposes retention metadata only. Every download re-fetches and compares the provider PDF, verifies current payable check state, rejects future payment dates, and decrypts/hash-checks the retained bytes. Completed, stopped, expired, foreign or changed checks cannot be downloaded through this payable-document route. Trusted redirect origins are exact server-configured HTTPS origins; credentials never follow a redirect, and request bodies cannot configure trust. Immutable document checks and safe audit records retain outcomes without raw PDFs, signed URLs or credentials; review alerts open on failed evidence and clear after successful document checks. Retention/download alone is not employee delivery and does not unblock payroll closeout. Internal delivery acknowledgment, historical non-payable copies, automatic document/check recovery, preflight release, stop/void/reissue and check accounting remain unfinished. The UI submission button remains deferred until delivery is connected.


277. Internal check delivery currently means an admin downloads and prints the retained provider PDF and explicitly confirms handing that check to the employee on the approved employer-local payment date. The same admin must have a successful download within fifteen minutes, and delivery revalidates the provider document before retaining immutable source/download links, exact amount/date and handoff reference. It does not assume employee electronic-delivery consent. Concurrent identical handoffs retain one receipt; later exact retries reuse it without repeating provider actions, while different facts conflict. The payroll page now exposes issuance, recovery, retention, protected download and handoff controls. The exact handoff reference fills the closeout form as read-only; unresolved issued checks cannot be replaced with manual references. Recent matching document evidence or fresh confirmed bank settlement is required at closeout, and newer stopped/uncertain/changed issue evidence blocks stale document proof. Downloading another payable copy after handoff is rejected without invalidating the actual delivery receipt. A delivered check can finalize the approved payroll once, generating the existing statements/leave/accounting workflow; bank clearance remains distinct. Late/backdated handoff review, employee acknowledgment/history refinements, automatic check/document recovery, check bank accounting and stop/void/reissue remain unfinished.

278. **Already-issued check recovery is automatic and read-only.** A bounded worker checks existing immutable check claims after ten minutes, or daily after matching live bank-confirmed recovery with no open issue alert. It records an immutable attempt before provider access, selects oldest due work, and prevents overlapping sweeps. It uses the retained connection and payment identity even after setup/election changes; it never issues a new check or retries a provider POST. Failed credential access leaves a payroll alert and waits before retrying. The visible idle check panel reads local progress every thirty seconds and pauses for draft references and confirmations. Admin handoff remains an explicit recorded physical action. Automatic PDF retention, check bank accounting and stop/void/reissue remain separate unfinished work.

279. **Recovered payable checks prepare their PDFs automatically.** The issued-check recovery worker invokes the existing encrypted document-retention path after a SENT result. Fresh provider ownership, identity, expiration and PDF hash checks still apply, and an existing retained document is never replaced. Automatic retention has a null human actor and explicit automatic attribution; printable downloads still require an admin, and handoff remains explicitly confirmed. A document failure opens its own alert and retries on the next due recovery without reissuing the check. This assumption covers internal preparation only; no browser download, physical delivery or wage finalization is inferred.

280. **Check cash accounting follows confirmed bank withdrawals.** A finalized payroll check contributes a separate check-labeled cash movement only from matching recovery evidence covering the entire net amount, check external identity, expiration identity and posted bank line items. Original provider identity must remain consistent. These events use the existing reviewed QuickBooks clearing-to-bank journal process, retained claim and read-only recovery; they do not create additional wages or taxes. Handoff alone does not establish a bank withdrawal. Closed runs retain their issued-check status controls. Stop/return/void/reissue and historical funding changes require further implementation; an unresolved or changed check movement stays in review.

281. **Check delivery history is visible to the employee and payroll admins.** Receipts derive from immutable employer-recorded handoffs and do not assert employee acknowledgment. They show net amount, original pay date, recorded handoff time, last provider-check time and separately evaluated bank-clearance status. Current conflicting, expired or unavailable evidence shows a review message while preserving delivery history. Employee sessions scope receipts to the employee and employer; admins scope them to a run. Internal handoff references, provider identities, encryption fields and negotiable PDF data are omitted. These receipts do not create additional wages, taxes or bank activity.

Check receipt views also refresh local data every thirty seconds while visible and idle; pending loads suppress overlap, and unmounted views discard stale results.

282. **Employee check acknowledgment is optional and separate from pay completion.** The employee may confirm receipt of a handed-over check from Pay statements. This confirms physical receipt only, not wage accuracy, bank clearance or waiver of questions. The active receiving employee session is revalidated under transaction locks; former employees retain this action. The acknowledgment and source session are immutable, concurrent/repeated confirmation records it once, and admins can view but cannot submit it on the employee’s behalf. Payroll closeout and bank accounting do not depend on acknowledgment. Automatic receipt refresh pauses while the employee confirms or saves.

283. **Lost-check stop requests retain one bank action before transmission.** An admin explicitly confirms bank stop-action support and retains a review reference for the original sent check. One immutable stop claim precedes any provider POST; every later attempt queries provider actions only, including missing records. Confirmation requires a matching acknowledged action and matching stopped check. The first action identity cannot change. Any retained stop request blocks further PDF preparation/download, handoff and new closeout; it marks employee receipts for review and keeps an unpaid-wage follow-up alert open. Stop does not void reported wages or authorize replacement. Automatic stop-action recovery, definitive failed-request remediation and replacement issuance remain unfinished.

284. **Retained stop actions recover automatically with the check.** The existing bounded check worker reads a retained stop action before refreshing ordinary check status. It never creates a new stop or check. Unresolved stops retry after ten minutes; a confirmed stop and matching live/date/expiry/provider STOPPED observation recheck daily. Eligibility includes the stop claim and latest stop observation timestamps. PDF preparation is skipped for stopped-request checks, and the unpaid-wage alert stays open even after the stop is confirmed. Automatic observations have explicit automatic attribution and no human actor. The visible admin panel discovers the updated stop/check state through its existing local polling.

285. **A failed/cancelled stop may allow the reviewed original check to continue.** An admin must attest that the original was recovered and no replacement was issued, retain a reference, and obtain fresh matching failed/cancelled stop evidence with the original check still SENT and unexpired. Prior confirmed-stop or paid/stopped/returned/reversed check history blocks initial continuation. One immutable disposition records its source action and observation; retries preserve it. Shared eligibility controls printing, delivery, closeout, receipts and automatic preparation. Later unknown, changed, stopped or conflicting evidence blocks continuation again; a later confirmed stop cannot silently become eligible after another status change. This disposition does not create a new stop, replacement check, wage or journal.

286. **Confirmed stopped checks need an unpaid-wage and reporting review before replacement authorization.** The admin reviews the entire original net amount, current payment choice, proposed date, prior handoff and wage/tax treatment, with separate unpaid-balance and reporting references. Review requires matching original stop/check identities, recent confirmed-stop and STOPPED recovery evidence, and no paid/returned/reversed history. Identical recovery preserves the fingerprint; changed facts invalidate the review. Revisions are immutable and concurrent exact submissions reuse one record. Annual approval for finalized payroll flags unresolved stopped-check cases, missing/changed reviews and required corrections. Retaining a review does not send funds, finalize wages or authorize a replacement; those execution steps remain unfinished.

287. **Stopped-check replacement authorization binds the full unpaid net to the current payment setup.** After the retained original-reporting review, admins authorize a distinct encrypted instruction for CHECK or DIRECT_DEPOSIT using the current check activation/payee or employee bank consent. Matching check recipient/funding evidence must be recent, and the proposed date cannot have passed. One active authorization is allowed for the original check; exact concurrent retries reuse it. Admins can cancel an unstarted authorization with a retained reference, but an immutable dispatch claim prevents cancellation. Cancelled authorizations cannot be claimed. Authorization does not itself dispatch funds or alter original wages. Replacement execution, document/delivery/closeout and accounting integration remain required.

288. **A stopped-check replacement has its own committed dispatch claim and provider identity.** Sending a retained CHECK or DIRECT_DEPOSIT authorization requires the same current review, stop evidence, payment setup and future/current date fingerprint. The claim is committed before provider access that could create a payment; concurrent requests and all later retries recover the retained instruction without another creation attempt. Provider identities bind to the first observed payment, and mismatches require review. Current setup changes block unstarted dispatch but do not prevent recovery of an already-claimed payment through its retained funding connection. Provider results and automatic/human audit attribution are retained, and uncertain/adverse outcomes create follow-up alerts. Replacement dispatch does not itself duplicate wages, close the original payroll, or record delivery. Automatic recovery, replacement check documents/handoff, finalization and accounting integration remain subsequent work.

289. **Submitted stopped-check replacements recover automatically without creating payments.** A bounded, overlap-locked sweep checks only retained dispatch claims, attempts unresolved or alerted payments after ten minutes, and rechecks matching live bank-confirmed payments daily. Check settlement also requires matching expiry evidence. Each attempt is retained before recovery, credential failures open an internal alert and remain on the shorter retry interval, and automated observations omit a human actor. Startup runs after one minute and every five minutes thereafter; PAYROLL_CHECK_REPLACEMENT_RECOVERY_ENABLED=false pauses the worker. The visible idle admin panel refreshes every thirty seconds and protects unfinished references/confirmations. This automation does not submit unstarted authorizations or record check delivery; document, receipt, closeout and accounting integration remain unfinished.

290. **Replacement checks have separate encrypted document evidence and controlled downloads.** Only a claimed, uncancelled CHECK replacement can prepare a negotiable PDF. The original stopped-check evidence must remain consistent, and the replacement must match its first provider identity, authorized amount/date/expiry, current SENT state and immutable retained document/hash. Automatic recovery prepares encrypted PDFs without a human actor; automatic printable downloads are prohibited. Admin downloads revalidate provider bytes and stored integrity, cannot precede the replacement date, and do not make the stopped original printable. Failed document checks retain follow-up evidence without replacing stored bytes. Replacement handoff and downstream receipt/closeout/accounting integration remain unfinished.

291. **Replacement handoff is a distinct immutable delivery event.** An admin confirms the full authorized check amount, replacement date and in-person delivery reference. Handoff requires current original stopped-check evidence, a freshly retained replacement PDF and a successful matching download by the same admin within fifteen minutes. The replacement date must equal employer-local today; late dates require separate remediation. Approved and finalized original payroll can retain replacement delivery without recreating original wages. Exact concurrent retries reuse one handoff; changed references or amounts are rejected. After handoff, printable downloads are blocked and audited while document refresh remains available for recovery. Employee receipts, closeout and accounting integration remain unfinished.

292. **Employees can see and acknowledge delivered replacement checks in the existing receipt history.** Replacement receipts identify the original pay date and replacement date, preserve employer-recorded handoff and employee acknowledgment, and separately assess outstanding, bank-confirmed or review-needed evidence. Current original stop facts and matching replacement identity/date/expiry remain required; bank clearance uses the retained full bank evidence. Responses omit internal delivery references, provider identities, encrypted data and negotiable documents. Acknowledgment uses the receiving employee's locked session and a separate immutable replacement table; concurrent retries reuse one record and admin views cannot impersonate the employee. Existing visible-page refresh carries later status changes into the portal. ACH replacements of stopped checks, receipt downloads, closeout and accounting integration remain unfinished.

293. **Stopped-check replacements reconcile as separate bank movements against original payroll clearing.** Claimed CHECK and DIRECT_DEPOSIT replacements contribute verified withdrawals and, for returned direct deposits, posted credits. Full bank evidence, first provider identity, original stopped-check facts and cross-payment line-item uniqueness gate posting. New authorizations retain an immutable funding-connection identifier in addition to their encrypted instruction; historical rows missing that identifier require funding remediation before accounting. QuickBooks source guards bind the replacement, original check, observation, payment method, funding mapping and company. The existing journal claim/recovery workflow posts replacement movements without adding wages or requiring a withdrawal/return for the unpaid stopped original. Returned credits require the replacement withdrawal journal first. Automatic new-posting authorization, stopped-case closure, historical funding remediation and original-run closeout remain unfinished.

294. A stopped-check case closes only after the original payroll is finalized, a current matching review retains the original wage/tax treatment, the replacement has full confirmed bank payment, any replacement check has a recorded handoff, and the gross/replacement journals agree in the current QuickBooks company. Later conflicting payment, review or accounting evidence reopens the case. Automatic case history records only material state changes and carries no invented human actor. Existing case sweeps review check replacements every ten minutes; no new payment or journal is authorized by case closure.

295. Direct-deposit replacements of stopped checks receive a separate immutable bank receipt automatically after full matching bank recovery. The receipt shows original/replacement dates, net amount, masked destination and retained bank-posted dates; it does not create another wage statement or imply the employee's account balance. Later returned, conflicting or unreadable evidence preserves the receipt while marking it for review. Employee/admin receipt views refresh while visible every thirty seconds, prevent overlapping background requests and discard responses after unmount. Existing recovery sweeps can retain receipts for historical confirmed replacements when they next recover them.

296. Direct-deposit replacement receipts are downloadable as self-contained, printable HTML from employee and admin receipt history. Each download records the current employer name, original/replacement dates, amount, masked account, retained bank dates, receipt identity and status as observed at download time. The original wage statement remains the tax/wage reference. Downloads use the receipt's existing employer/employee/run access scope, escape all dynamic text, include no external assets or executable scripts, and carry no-store attachment headers. A historical download remains a snapshot; the live portal shows later changes.

297. Original and replacement check-delivery receipts are downloadable as printable HTML using the existing employee/admin receipt scope. The record distinguishes employer handoff, optional employee acknowledgment and bank clearance; outstanding or review-needed checks retain those statuses. Replacement receipts also retain the original pay date. These files contain receipt facts rather than a negotiable check image, routing details or payment instructions. They include the current employer name and download timestamp, omit internal handoff/review references, and use the same escaping, offline layout and attachment protections as direct-deposit receipts.

298. Automatic creation of QuickBooks bank-withdrawal and returned-credit journals requires a retained authorization for each finalized payroll. The authorization covers later eligible replacement movements for that payroll and binds the reviewed mapping, gross payroll journal, company and environment. Admins confirm that competing manual/bank-rule postings are not active. Current bank/source checks and remote account/gross-journal verification still apply before every new claim. Disabling or changing the authorization stops new automated claims; saved journals continue through existing recovery. Automatic journal/claim records have no human executor and link their authorizing review separately. A bounded worker checks due authorizations after ten minutes, processes up to ten new eligible movements per run per sweep, and records failures as internal alerts. No live authorization is enabled by this code change.

299. Automatic QuickBooks posting keeps immutable worker-attempt outcomes and links each new journal claim to its exact attempt. Worker completion is distinct from QuickBooks confirmation; missing completion evidence stays unconfirmed, and an attempt that fails after claiming still exposes its saved journal. History shows the retained company/environment plus each linked journal's current recovery status. The visible admin panel refreshes every thirty seconds only while idle, avoids overlapping polls and ignores stale responses; unfinished references or confirmations pause background refresh. Older attempts without an outcome are displayed as unconfirmed rather than assumed successful or running.

300. SendGrid is an optional asynchronous W-2 notice provider for employers using smtp.sendgrid.net; existing Gmail/other SMTP paths are preserved. SendGrid unique arguments carry only an opaque retained dispatch key, and the delivery log must exist before transmission. Raw provider bytes are authenticated before JSON parsing. Older signed timestamps are not rejected solely for age because durable provider-event deduplication will handle retries; future timestamps and invalid signatures are rejected. Signed-event verification alone is not payroll ownership proof. Webhook routing, exact event matching, durable intake, return reconciliation and provider readiness remain unfinished. Primary sources and integration boundaries are recorded in docs/PAYROLL_NOTICE_PROVIDER.md.

301. Verified SendGrid bounce callbacks are retained automatically without an admin session, using the configured public signing key plus exact retained dispatch, recipient hash, provider and notice metadata. Duplicate event IDs are idempotent only when their evidence matches; conflicting message identities are rejected. Batches commit atomically. Padded provider event IDs are supported. Raw recipient/reason/payload data is not copied into event evidence. Provider timestamps remain retained, while effective return time respects exact database source creation timestamps to handle second precision safely. Late SMTP-result updates cannot clear a bounce. A bounded worker reconciles mail-log returns and paper-follow-up targets, retries temporary failures after ten minutes and alerts on unresolved evidence conflicts. Manual or conflicting immutable returns require a future reviewed correction workflow. The intake worker flag pauses processing only; valid callbacks continue to be retained. Provider configuration/readiness and real delivery verification remain rollout work.

302. W-2 service readiness is shown in Employer setup alongside existing onboarding services. Notice email policy is evaluated separately from invitation policy. Signed-return readiness requires SendGrid SMTP and the same valid P-256 public key used by intake. Worker enablement is independent so already-retained events remain actionable when sending settings change. Counts and latest received/check times are scoped to the employer; missing checks remain explicitly unrecorded, and zero returns do not prove successful notice delivery. No credentials, addresses or key material are returned. A failed refresh clears previous evidence, and disposed requests cannot restore it. These are configuration and retained-activity checks, not live provider verification.

303. Electronic W-2 return time/source corrections are append-only, reviewed in the publication panel and protected by the current correction revision. Original evidence and all correction references/timestamps remain visible. If signed provider evidence exists, the earliest retained event supplies the corrected time; an administrator cannot substitute a later manual date. Without provider evidence, the actual corrected timestamp must follow the attempt and cannot be future-dated. Corrections preserve the original follow-up timezone and recompute its 30-day target, including existing paper-furnishing assessment. Matching pending provider events reconcile through the existing worker. A correction never retracts the returned status or proves delivery; retraction and other uncertainty dispositions remain separate unfinished work.

304. A manually entered W-2 return can be retracted once when an admin verifies it was entered in error, retains an evidence reference and reviews its current correction revision. Provider/mail-log returns and currently bounced deliveries cannot be retracted this way. Retraction preserves original/correction history, removes that mistaken return from target calculation and restores the earlier retained send outcome; uncertain sends remain uncertain. A later verified provider return takes precedence, automatically reopens follow-up from its earliest timestamp and retained timezone, and reconciles through the existing worker. Retraction does not resend a notice or prove delivery. Repeated manual return/retraction cycles and other uncertainty dispositions remain unfinished.

305. An approved payroll with an originally handed-off check may close after a later replacement check or ACH payment is fully confirmed by current bank evidence, when the retained tax review explicitly preserves the original wage reporting. The original handoff date/reference remain the wage-date evidence, and the replacement date, method, amount and bank movements are retained separately in immutable closeout proof. No new wages or second finalization are created. Original stop, replacement, current payment choice, funding connection and review changes invalidate eligibility; recovery evidence must be current within fifteen minutes. Closeout waits until the actual replacement date. Originally undelivered checks and reviews requiring wage-date/tax correction remain blocked pending the separate recalculation path. A refreshed tax review can retain a past replacement date only when it matches an already-dispatched replacement; it does not authorize another payment. This policy relies on a reviewed valid original check handoff, not merely check creation; IRS constructive-receipt guidance and the implementation boundary are recorded in docs/PAYROLL_PAYMENT_EXECUTION.md.

306. Replaying the original manual W-2 return request after its evidence was corrected, retracted or reinstated by a provider is a stale request requiring refreshed publication history. It must not report success against obsolete evidence or reactivate a retracted return. Exact retries of an unchanged active original record remain idempotent. A new manual return cycle requires its own explicit reviewed workflow.

307. After retracting a mistaken manual W-2 notice return, an admin may record newly reviewed return evidence for the same notice attempt and retract that later review if it was also mistaken. Every transition is append-only and requires the current correction and cycle revisions, actual return time and an evidence reference. New return times may describe previously discovered evidence, so they must follow the original send attempt and cannot be in the future; they need not follow the administrative retraction time. The original return and first retraction remain visible, alongside all corrections and later transitions. Follow-up uses the originally retained timezone and the reviewed return date. Retraction restores retained send evidence, including uncertainty; it does not establish delivery. Verified provider returns and bounced mail evidence cannot be replaced by manual cycles, and a late NOT_SENT result blocks another return review. These reviews change follow-up evidence only and do not send notices or alter W-2 wage amounts.

308. A retained check attempt may be cancelled only when its immutable submission evidence proves the adapter stopped before making a provider create request, no observation or document/handoff/stop/replacement evidence indicates an issued check, and the latest GET-only recovery confirms NOT_FOUND within fifteen minutes. A lookup failure during the original existence check, an unknown submission outcome, a failed create request or NOT_FOUND by itself does not prove non-submission. Cancellation retains the exact blocking and recovery observations, dismisses that resolved check alert and stops scheduled recovery for the cancelled authorization. Admins then void and rebuild the run; the cancelled attempt never gains permission to create a check. Existing ACH cancellation rules still apply independently to mixed payrolls. This workflow does not cancel an already-created provider payment or release uncertain funds.

309. A provider-created check may be reviewed for cancellation only while its current matching provider record is awaiting approval, approved or already cancelled, with no retained bank reconciliation, processing, sent, paid, printed, delivered, stop or replacement history. A unique cancellation claim is committed before the first possible provider PATCH. Retries recover by GET only; a missing, pending, changed or uncertain result is not cancellation proof. Fresh matching cancellation and original-check recovery are required before releasing the payment authorization. Release retains both observation links, resolves the cancellation alert and permits void/rebuild without reusing the old check claim. Already-cancelled provider checks can be reviewed without another PATCH. A race detected before any PATCH retains that fact; other uncertain cancellation attempts block printing pending follow-up. This flow does not change posted wages, stop a sent check or retry an uncertain provider update automatically. Additional reviewed retry/disposition paths for unsuccessful cancellation requests remain separate work.

310. A cancellation update may be retried only after every retained SUBMISSION explicitly proves `requestSent: false`, including a result for every durable retry claim. GET-only recovery results never substitute for missing submission evidence. The admin must review fresh matching unprocessed-check evidence and submit its current observation revisions, a reference and confirmation. Each retry is committed before transport, retains its source observations and receives its own immutable submission result; simultaneous or stale reviews cannot create a second update. A claimed attempt with no result remains recovery-only even if its process crashed before transmission. Any possible earlier PATCH permanently disables this retry path. Automation only recovers existing requests. Failed or superseded UI reads clear actionable readiness. Confirmed cancellation still requires fresh matching recovery before authorization release; retry history remains available to hiring/payroll admins. Additional evidence-backed dispositions for an uncertain transmitted update remain separate work.

311. When an uncertain cancellation is followed by fresh matching evidence that the original check is sent and uncashed, an admin may retain a reviewed original-check continuation if the original is available and no replacement was issued. This disposition keeps the wage/payment authorization intact; it does not authorize another check or release wages. Initial eligibility excludes prior paid, cancelled, stopped, returned, reversed, held or conflicting-identity evidence, existing printing/handoff, stops and replacements, and expired checks. The retained review binds both current observation revisions and is immutable. Printing/handoff still perform their independent date, document and provider checks. Later uncertain, stale, expired or contrary evidence makes continuation unavailable until valid recovery; conflicting provider/cancellation history cannot be erased by a newer matching response. A subsequent valid bank-confirmed payment remains the original payment. Recovery refreshes current evidence and the associated alert automatically. An unavailable original may enter the existing bank-stop workflow; originally undelivered replacement wage-date treatment remains unfinished.

312. A failed or cancelled bank-stop action may be followed by a newly reviewed stop attempt while the original check remains sent and uncashed, the original is unavailable, the bank supports stop actions, and no earlier paid/stopped or conflicting original-check evidence, release or replacement authorization exists. Each attempt consumes the current failed-action observation and commits its own immutable claim before provider transport. The complete paginated provider action list must contain all retained prior actions in failed/cancelled states and at most one new candidate; missing, conflicting, reactivated or ambiguous actions stop processing. Lost responses and unanswered claims recover by GET only. Each attempt has its own first action identity; replacement review and closeout bind the current attempt rather than the first historical stop. Repeated failed attempts retain their references and source links. Automation only recovers existing attempts, including unavailable-credential observations, and never creates a new stop without review. This does not retry an uncertain transmission, remove prior evidence, release wages or create a replacement automatically; replacement retains its existing separate review, bank, delivery and closeout requirements. A claimed retry that never yields identifiable provider evidence still requires separate remediation.

313. A bank-stop attempt may be retried after a missing-action recovery only when that same durable attempt has a completed submission explicitly recording `requestSent: false`. Missing submission results, any possible transmission, an observed action identity or an ambiguous action list exclude this path. Earlier no-send attempts and GET-only recovery never substitute for the current submission. Recovery must freshly confirm the original sent, uncashed check, exact identity, dates and live mode; retained paid, reconciled, stopped or conflicting check evidence remains blocking. Each admin-reviewed retry consumes the current observation and commits a separate immutable claim before transport. Repeated no-send failures retain null prior-action links; later known failed-action retries retain their actual provider identities. The employee wage reservation remains intact, and replacement/closeout still require their existing evidence. Unknown transmitted or crashed attempts need separate evidence-backed remediation; they are never resubmitted on a missing-record response alone.

314. If the current durable bank-stop attempt affirmatively proves no transmission and fresh recovery finds no new action, an admin who recovered the original check may retain continuation of that same check. The review binds the current stop observation and requires current matching sent, uncashed, unexpired original-check evidence, no conflicting payment history and no replacement authorization. The retained disposition has no invented provider action ID and never releases wages or creates another check. Subsequent stale, unavailable, expired, paid-to-sent reversal, conflicting-identity or stopped/returned evidence blocks continued use; fresh matching recovery may clear temporary uncertainty. Later matching completed payment can remain the original payroll payment. Immutable history, repeated-call idempotency and facility/admin scope are retained. Unanswered claims, possible transmissions and ambiguous action lists cannot use this path. Reviewed renewed stops after a retained original-check continuation remain separate work.

315. An admin may request a renewed bank stop when a previously continued original becomes unavailable again. Renewal requires fresh eligible failed-action or proven no-send recovery, a currently effective original-check continuation, its exact retained review ID, the current observation ID, bank-support/unavailable-original confirmation and a new reference. The unique durable renewal claim links the superseded continuation before transport; the older review cannot unblock the new attempt. Each attempt may retain one immutable continuation, allowing repeated found/lost cycles without replacing history. Unanswered claims remain recovery-only, and later failed or proven unsent attempts may receive their own reviewed continuation. Existing paid, stopped, conflicting identity, replacement and uncertain-transmission exclusions remain in effect. Automation recovers the current attempt but never starts a renewed stop without admin review. Repeated cycles preserve one original wage/payment identity and the existing separate replacement/closeout requirements.

316. Retained paid, reconciled, stopped, cancelled, returned, reversed, held or conflicting-identity observations cannot be erased by a later sent response. First-stop preflight now retains its original-check recovery facts and audit event even when no stop is allowed. First-stop admission and every continuation use shared original/check-stop/cancellation history rules plus current matching evidence. Paid evidence observed before a failed or contradictory final provider read remains retained without being treated as settled-bank proof. Stop recovery carries paid/conflict observations across its own multiple reads. A rejected continuation saves new recovery evidence before returning its error, so retrying cannot discard the reason for rejection. Current continuation remains gated by current matching original/stop evidence, freshness, expiry and history; legitimate later completed payment still uses normal bank/accounting checks. The UI explains history-based ineligibility. Resolving truly contradictory provider evidence remains a separate reviewed remediation task.

317. Hiring/payroll admins may inspect retained original-check, stop and cancellation observations directly within the check workflow. This read-only history shows result/check states, attempt numbers, timestamps with timezone, payment/reconciliation facts and identity/date conflicts using a fixed safe projection; provider IDs, raw payloads, credentials and account details are omitted. It does not obtain a new provider result or authorize any payment. Pages contain at most twenty observations and use an issue-bound cursor with full timestamp precision and a deterministic tie-break, so newer observations do not duplicate or displace older pages. Opening the panel or refreshing starts a new view; older pages append to the retained view. A failed refresh labels previously loaded observations and leaves payment controls unchanged. Current eligibility remains governed by the existing shared evidence checks and recovery workflow.

318. Federal remittance preparation uses the February 2026 EFTPS Financial Institution Handbook for 2026 obligations: Form 941 deposit code 94105 and quarterly return-period ending month; FUTA code 09405 and annual December return period, including quarterly deposits. The TXP date uses day 01. Total-only instructions repeat the tax code as the amount type and use integer cents, avoiding invented component allocations after partial deposits. The employer EIN remains encrypted and only its last four digits reach the review UI. Reviews require a positive outstanding obligation, a future eligible settlement date, verified calendar inputs and an explicit admin reference; changes to source facts invalidate the retained review. A review is not bank authorization, payment scheduling, agency acceptance or a tax-deposit receipt. EFTPS enrollment and a verified bank/provider mapping for the required CCD+ fields—including the entry-detail taxpayer identification—are still prerequisites to transmission. The generic provider remittance text field alone is insufficient evidence that those fields are populated correctly.

Remittance specification sources: [EFTPS Financial Institution Handbook, February 2026](https://download.eftps.gov/Financial_Institution_Handbook.pdf), [Treasury EFTPS resources](https://fiscal.treasury.gov/payments-to-government/electronic-federal-tax-payment-system-eftps/resources), and [Modern Treasury payment-order API](https://docs.moderntreasury.com/platform/reference/create-payment-order).

319. A bank-generated ACH sample can be compared internally against a current retained federal remittance review to diagnose the bank's tax-field mapping. This deliberately checks the actual entry-detail taxpayer identification separately from the TXP addenda. The current diagnostic accepts a single credit tax entry with its immediately preceding CCD batch header and following addenda; it supports fixed-width records with no separators, LF or CRLF and rejects malformed/non-ASCII/oversized samples. It returns field names and match results, not uploaded content or taxpayer/account values. The file is not retained, sent to a provider or used as a payment authorization. A matching diagnostic does not establish full NACHA validity, bank enrollment, cutoff compliance, acceptance, settlement or agency credit. Changed source facts require a refreshed retained review before comparison. Required field positions are based on the Treasury handbook and [Nacha's ACH file details](https://achdevguide.nacha.org/ach-file-details).

320. An admin may retain an employer-only active retirement participation determination for box 13 when referenced plan records establish participation and there are no employee deferrals, Roth or after-tax contributions, distributions, make-up contributions, or other retirement amounts requiring W-2 reporting. The determination covers qualifying employer-funded participation or defined-benefit eligibility; mere eligibility to elect contributions is insufficient. A dedicated confirmation is required, the selection is available only for the retirement category, and the existing immutable source-bound applicability history applies. A current determination checks the retirement flag in the draft and approved employee copies without adding deferral amounts or changing wages. Other retirement arrangements remain subject to detailed treatment and cannot use this selection to bypass their reporting. Sources: [IRS retirement plan W-2 reporting guidance](https://www.irs.gov/retirement-plans/common-errors-on-form-w-2-codes-for-retirement-plans) and [2026 W-2/W-3 instructions](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/iw2w3).

321. An employee can withdraw the currently displayed benefit deduction authorization with explicit confirmation. Withdrawal is bound to that signed request and onboarding cycle, retained in immutable task revisions, and reported to the hiring admin. It blocks further collection and invalidates an approved calculation before finalization; it does not itself cancel insurance coverage, reverse completed deductions, or recall payments already transmitted. Old signature retries remain rejected. Deductions can resume only after a new explicit signature, or payroll can resume without deductions after the admin completes the applicable coverage/funding review. Existing historical contribution evidence remains unchanged. The current conservative review gate can pause payroll even when a previous payment already collected that month's contribution; automatic handling of that case and employer-funded continuation after withdrawal remain follow-on work. Retirement plan-specific limits, tax treatment and remittance workflows must be implemented separately from generic benefit costs.

322. Withdrawal need not pause later wages in a month whose matching contribution was already finalized before withdrawal. Current reviewed coverage, matching signed amounts and intact prior collection evidence remain required. The prior run must still be finalized and its database finalization timestamp must be no later than the retained withdrawal time; an approved or later-finalized source cannot stand in for this proof. The later run carries the existing collection and withdrawal as evidence with no new deduction. The original contribution remains in reports exactly once. A following month's new collection still requires renewed authorization or an applicable reviewed funding change. Zero-wage previews collect nothing and do not become blocked merely because authorization was withdrawn. This resolves the already-collected-month limitation recorded in assumption 321.

323. A hiring admin may keep signed, catalog-backed group-health enrollment active while the employer assumes all published employee contributions from a reviewed effective date. This path is restricted by explicit confirmation to excluded group medical, dental or vision premiums for an eligible employee, with no taxable shareholder, individual-policy reimbursement or other taxable-benefit treatment. It preserves the employee's enrollment and the published total monthly premium; payroll records the reviewed employer-funded amounts and deducts nothing from the employee. Existing completed deductions are not refunded or prorated automatically, and the review does not prove a carrier payment or create an employer-premium accounting entry. A future funding date preserves applicable earlier coverage; withdrawn earlier authorizations remain blocked. Funding supersedes the prior signature for any later restoration of employee contributions, requiring a fresh signature even if the original terms are reused. Admin confirmation is renewed when review fields change. Sources: [2026 IRS fringe-benefit guidance](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15b) and [IRS employee-benefit guidance](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/employee-benefits).

324. Employer-funded continuation evidence is reported from finalized regular payroll, grouped once per employee, payment month and retained funding decision. A selected payment range includes matching decisions and their supporting payrolls throughout those months so repeated paychecks do not multiply a monthly premium. Different decisions in a month remain separate and cannot be added as liabilities. The report validates retained enrollment, dates and published funding amounts and reconciles any employee deductions from the whole month, including payments outside a narrower selected range. Employee collected totals are employee/month amounts, repeated for context and not additive across plans or funding versions. The report is evidence for carrier-invoice reconciliation, not an accrued expense, amount owed, automatic proration, refund or proof of carrier payment. Employees without finalized payroll evidence are outside this report; a full carrier coverage ledger remains necessary.

325. Carrier invoice reconciliation records the actual positive invoice total supplied by an admin, not a total inferred from published payroll premiums. A review covers one coverage month and binds the month’s finalized employer-funded continuation evidence, including employee collections and differing funding decisions. Admins explicitly reconcile other covered employees, no-pay coverage, credits and adjustments against supporting carrier records. Carrier name and invoice number, trimmed and compared without case, identify a revision chain within the facility; changing its coverage month is rejected. Invoice and due dates must be valid and the due date cannot precede the invoice date. Reviews and their source snapshots are append-only; exact repeated submissions reuse the latest matching revision, and replacement requires its current ID. Later source changes mark a review stale without erasing it. Current means matching retained payroll evidence, not independent verification of carrier records, an expense journal, payment or full carrier roster completeness. Document references are retained; source-document upload and accounting/payment execution remain outstanding.

326. Carrier supporting files are retained per immutable invoice revision, with PDF, PNG or JPEG signatures and a 5 MB per-file limit using the existing payroll document validator. Each revision permits 20 distinct file hashes; uploading identical bytes reuses the original attachment even at the limit. Files are encrypted with the configured payroll document key and authenticated context including facility, invoice revision and document ID. Downloads require matching facility and invoice scope, verify the retained SHA-256 hash and use attachment/no-store/nosniff headers. Upload dates remain visible, including files added to older revisions; an attachment does not retrospectively prove that it was present at the original review. Files are not automatically copied to a later invoice revision. Missing vault configuration blocks uploads and is displayed in the admin UI; no production key was created or changed. File signatures and encryption do not independently verify carrier authenticity or accounting/payment status.

327. An invoice accounting allocation is an explicitly reviewed split between employer premium expense and employee contributions applied to the actual positive invoice total. Both fields must be nonnegative integer cents and sum exactly to the invoice amount; zero is explicit. Supporting allocation evidence and separate confirmation are required. Gathering an invoice without an allocation remains possible, but its allocation status is incomplete and no expense is inferred automatically. A revised invoice retains a new split only after fresh confirmation, preserving earlier versions. This records an admin review; automated matching/reservation of underlying employee deductions across invoices, verified accounting mappings, journal posting/recovery and carrier remittance are not yet established by the allocation.

328. Employee amounts applied to carrier invoices must reference specific retained finalized monthly benefit contributions from the invoice coverage month, rather than an unlinked total. Partial assignments are supported, sum to the reviewed employee allocation and cannot exceed each source deduction after other current invoice revisions are counted. All saves serialize on employer payroll settings; revising the same invoice replaces its current reservation while retaining the earlier history. Stale other invoices continue reserving their deductions until explicitly revised, preventing silent reuse. Legacy positive allocations without source links must be reconciled before further assignments in that month. The admin selects the carrier-appropriate employee/plan sources and confirms supporting records; the system validates retained amounts and prevents duplicate assignment but does not infer carrier identity from plan names. These are accounting reservations, not a remittance or journal. Contributions outside the selected coverage month and unsupported/manual deductions still need a separate implemented reconciliation path. Adding deduction evidence to the source fingerprint may require refreshing earlier invoice reviews.

329. Before using matched employee deductions in invoice accounting, Vortex verifies the connected QuickBooks company and the original payroll journals. Positive employee allocations require the current active USD Other Current Liability deduction account, USD company preferences, finalized reconciled payroll evidence, a retained synced job for the same company/environment and an actual fetched journal matching both the saved payload and current payroll mapping. The invoice must be the latest revision with unchanged monthly source evidence and valid reservations. The UI reports the checked time, company, liability account and source journal IDs. This is a point-in-time check, not a retained premium posting authorization: future premium dispatch must repeat necessary source/mapping checks. No employee contribution implies no source payroll journals to verify; a connection is still required. Employer premium expense/payable mapping, premium journal authorization/submission/recovery and carrier payment remain unfinished. Synthetic tests did not perform production QuickBooks writes.

330. The premium journal preview uses the reviewed invoice date and actual invoice amount: employer premium expense and applied employee deduction liability are debited, and a separate carrier premium Other Current Liability account is credited. The active expense and carrier accounts must be USD and distinct; a used deduction liability account must also differ. Company home currency is verified as USD, and matched source payroll journals are rechecked before preview. Zero-value lines are omitted. This convention is an internal proposed journal, not a vendor Bill, payment, tax adjustment, prepaid-amortization calculation or posted transaction. Admins supply the selected account IDs and see verified account names before further review. A deterministic document reference and fingerprint bind the previewed invoice/source/company/accounts; posting authorization, accounting-period review, connection-generation binding, durable submission and recovery remain to be implemented. Intuit reference: [JournalEntry line AccountRef and PostingType](https://static.developer.intuit.com/sdkdocs/qbv3doc/ippdotnetdevkitv3/html/62627c63-90a3-c87a-ef9b-8b4b06daee08.htm).

331. Premium preview dates must fall after any verified QuickBooks book closing date. The invoice date is retained as the proposed journal date; Vortex does not silently move it into another accounting period. Missing or malformed company accounting preferences block preview. An omitted or null BookCloseDate within a valid preferences object means no closing date is configured, following Intuit’s documented optional field. The reviewed period facts and payroll QuickBooks connection generation are included in the preview fingerprint, so changing either requires a fresh review before future authorization. This does not establish accountant approval, tax treatment or posted accounting. Sources: [Intuit company accounting preferences](https://static.developer.intuit.com/sdkdocs/qbv3doc/ippphpdevkitv3/entities/files/IPPCompanyAccountingPrefs.html) and [QuickBooks advanced accounting settings](https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/customer-company-settings/set-advanced-account-settings/L4Dw2ATRQ_US_en_US).

332. Premium authorization retains the exact revalidated journal preview and company/account/period evidence with a separate admin confirmation and review reference. It is append-only and bound to a request key; retries of an active identical request reuse it, while cancelled keys cannot create another authorization. At most one active authorization may hold an invoice chain. An active authorization blocks invoice revision through API and database guards, preserving its contribution reservations until cancellation. Cancellation requires a recorded reason and retains all authorized journal evidence; a new request may authorize again afterward. Authorization is not posting or payment. The present cancellation path is valid before any premium dispatch exists; future dispatch implementation must add an atomic claim/cancellation exclusion and source revalidation before sending. No production provider write occurred.

333. Premium journal dispatch is permitted only for an uncancelled retained authorization after fresh invoice, deduction reservation, source journal, account, period and connection checks. A unique immutable claim with initiating admin is committed before any create request; first dispatch rechecks necessary facts after that claim. Lookup uses the retained deterministic journal document identity and accepts only one exact matching journal. Once claimed, all retries are query-only recovery, including missing or uncertain outcomes; a missing lookup never authorizes another create. The claim/cancellation boundary is enforced in the API and database. Claimed invoice allocations remain held, so posted-journal corrections require a future explicit accounting correction workflow. Provider observations are immutable and the UI distinguishes confirmed journals from outcomes requiring recovery. No carrier payment is inferred from a posted premium liability journal. Scheduled recovery and proven-no-send claim remediation remain outstanding. All tested provider traffic was synthetic.

334. Automatic premium recovery operates only on existing dispatch claims and never creates a journal. The dedicated scheduler runs every five minutes (unless test mode or PAYROLL_CARRIER_PREMIUM_RECOVERY_ENABLED=false); each sweep considers up to ten oldest due claims across employers. Unresolved claims retry after five minutes, and confirmed journals are rechecked after 24 hours so missing or changed provider evidence can reopen review. Workers recheck eligibility under the employer lock, retain observations and safe audit entries, and advance retry timing even when the authorized company connection is unavailable. Manual workforce automation also invokes recovery when QuickBooks sync work is enabled. Unresolved outcomes open scoped payroll alerts; successful automatic or manual recovery dismisses them. The admin invoice page polls retained status every 30 seconds for claimed journals, preserving edits and displaying a refresh failure without erasing saved evidence. Scheduling was verified in code and worker/browser tests; production scheduler/provider configuration remains a rollout prerequisite.


335. **Proven unsent premium cancellation.** A completed first posting attempt may retain immutable no-send proof only when it made no journal create request and did not encounter an existing/mismatched journal. A changed second preflight or unavailable initial lookup can produce that proof; a crash with no retained proof, an attempted create, or legacy ambiguous history cannot. Admin cancellation still requires a fresh query in the originally authorized QuickBooks company/environment, a definite absent result and no retained synced/conflicting journal evidence. Cancellation preserves the claim and observations, releases the invoice authorization, clears its alert and excludes it from scheduled recovery. Fresh authorization is required for another posting attempt. Query-only recovery never grants no-send proof merely because a journal is absent. Carrier payment and correction of a posted journal are separate unfinished paths.


336. **Premium reversal preparation.** Premium corrections begin with a separate full reversal, retaining the original journal instead of editing or deleting it. The proposed journal offsets each original account and amount with the opposite posting direction. Its explicitly reviewed date cannot precede the original date or fall in closed books. Preparation requires the latest retained synced original, a fresh exact-match original journal in the same company/environment, active original accounts with matching types, USD home currency and current connection-generation facts. It does not require today's invoice payroll basis to remain unchanged, because it corrects historical accounting. The fingerprint binds the original authorization and journal identity, destination, accounts, period, generation and reversal payload. Preview does not post, release invoice allocations, undo carrier payments or approve a correction; retained reversal authorization, posting/recovery and subsequent invoice revision remain unfinished. Sources: [Intuit reversal guidance](https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/journal-entries/reverse-delete-journal-entry-quickbooks-online/L2prlrnkh_US_en_US), [Intuit journal posting date](https://static.developer.intuit.com/sdkdocs/qbv3doc/ippdotnetdevkitv3/html/0b5f8961-f32e-e396-3a39-7b3e241434e8.htm), and [Intuit posting direction](https://static.developer.intuit.com/sdkdocs/qbv3doc/ippdotnetdevkitv3/html/eb8e35b5-ebe9-ffdd-d0ec-024f9e287d26.htm).


337. **Retained premium reversal authorization.** A hiring/payroll admin explicitly confirms the reviewed full reversal and provides a 12–2000 character evidence reference. Authorization refreshes the original journal, account, period and connection facts and rejects a stale preview fingerprint. One active reversal is allowed per original premium authorization, with immutable preview/reference/actor history and exact-request retry reuse. A cancelled request key cannot reauthorize; a fresh review/request can. Pre-posting cancellation is an internal retained action and remains possible after the QuickBooks connection changes. Database guards bind the original authorization, original journal evidence and preview fingerprint and prevent competing active reviews. Authorizing or cancelling a reversal does not change the original premium journal, release invoice contribution reservations, create another invoice revision or send a carrier payment. Dispatch claims, atomic dispatch/cancellation exclusion, posting/recovery and verified reversal-based allocation release still require implementation before reversal execution can be offered.


338. **Premium reversal dispatch and recovery.** A retained reversal requires an explicit posting action. First dispatch revalidates the original journal, accounts, period and preview fingerprint, commits a unique claim with its initiating admin, then rechecks before creating the journal. API and database guards exclude cancellation once claimed and exclude dispatch of a cancelled reversal. Retries and background recovery query the retained VTXR document identity in the authorized company/environment and never create a second journal. Exact-match observations are immutable; unresolved outcomes open scoped alerts and confirmed results clear them. A five-minute scheduler checks up to ten due reversals, with five-minute unresolved eligibility and daily confirmed-journal rechecks; shared manual workforce automation uses the same recovery path. The scheduler can be disabled with PAYROLL_CARRIER_REVERSAL_RECOVERY_ENABLED=false. Invoice history refreshes the observed reversal status. Posting a reversal does not release employee contribution allocations or automatically revise the invoice; verified correction reconciliation remains required. Crash/preflight claims without a send outcome, accounting correction/revision release and carrier remittance remain unfinished. Provider evidence used for validation is synthetic.


339. **Reversal reconciliation and corrected invoices.** An admin confirms the original and reversal offset and provides a retained correction reference. Reconciliation requires current confirmed observations, fresh exact-match original/reversal journal identities in the same company, and an exact inversion of original amounts/accounts. The immutable record unlocks a new invoice revision; it does not cancel the original journal or immediately free employee contribution reservations. The latest invoice allocation stays reserved until a replacement revision changes it. Reposting requires a new invoice revision and new authorization/document identity. Revision saves and new accounting preparation revalidate every prior reconciled journal pair in that invoice history. Missing/changed prior journals block progress. A separate optional premium accounting date defaults to the supplier invoice date; correction editing defaults to at least the latest reconciled reversal date and cannot post before it. The supplier's document date remains unchanged. Revised allocations can leave a verified unapplied contribution remainder available for other reviewed invoices; no employee refund or carrier payment is inferred. Production provider reconciliation, claimed-but-unposted remediation, no-pay coverage reconciliation and carrier payment remain separate unfinished work.


340. Carrier payments use a separate USD business ACH CCD provider contract with immutable carrier payment identity and retained invoice, payee and employer funding revisions. The provider layer requires a verified business checking or savings account, one masked account detail, one explicit valid ACH ABA route, and a provider update timestamp. A fingerprint binds counterparty, holder, account/detail identities, routing and update time; changed facts block first dispatch pending a new review. Only masked account data and the fingerprint are returned from the account reader. First dispatch rechecks funding and destination; conflicts query the same external identity, and uncertain recovery never creates another order. Provider completion does not establish settlement: exact posted bank line items and a stable fresh order observation are required. Returns currently surface as exceptions without inferring a refund. This provider layer is not yet connected to a durable carrier payee/authorization ledger, admin UI or scheduler, and cannot yet pay a carrier through Admin > Payroll. Reviewed carrier association, encrypted destination history, remittance details, allocation/concurrency rules, settlement accounting, returns and production verification remain required. Twelve carrier/employee provider tests passed with synthetic evidence; no live transaction was performed.

Admins select an existing verified business account in the configured provider, preview masked owner/type/last-four/environment details, and independently confirm the carrier or authorized collection agent using a retained reference. Saving rechecks the live funding and destination and requires the unchanged preview and latest revision. Each UUID payee revision retains an encrypted account snapshot tied to facility and revision, a numeric employer funding revision, a masked summary and immutable verification history. Concurrent reviews serialize with payment-connection changes; database guards reject cross-employer or superseded funding references. Rechecks distinguish changed account/funding details, unavailable providers and replaced employer connections without changing the saved history. The admin UI exposes review, save, current/superseded history and recheck controls. No payment is authorized by setup. Provider business-account creation/verification enrollment, automatic payee rechecks, invoice payment authorization/reservations, dispatch, remittance and bank accounting still require implementation. A carrier name or matching provider account is not independent evidence of carrier authorization.

365. Authorized carrier remittance notices now have internal dispatch/recovery and bounded scheduled processing. A notice-scoped session lock serializes manual and automatic processing; employer and payment-connection locks revalidate bank evidence/current recipient before each eligible send. The initial claim and individual attempt commit before external I/O. A missing result or legacy claim without an attempt remains uncertain and cannot trigger another send. Definite sender non-sends can retry after five minutes, with at most three attempts; accepted or uncertain attempts cannot be automatically resent. Recovered affirmative SMTP acceptance must match the exact facility, recipient hash, category, template, dispatch key and attempt-time window, with no retained bounce/complaint. Acceptance is retained separately from the original result. It does not establish carrier delivery, acknowledgment or application of funds.

The SMTP adapter now recognizes a transactional financial carrier-remittance category and requires a retained delivery row before transport. If that row cannot be retained, it reports a definite non-send for bounded retry; actual sender exceptions remain uncertain. The sender receives allowlisted authorized text/recipient and escaped HTML, with no bank-account or employee details. Sender responses retain sanitized status/message identity; failures do not expose exception secrets. Attempts, results, recovered acceptance and scheduled checks are immutable. A failed result write leaves the committed attempt recoverable without resending. Claimed notices remain protected from cancellation, including known non-sends; reviewed release/replacement after exhausted or otherwise blocked attempts remains separate unfinished remediation.

A minute scheduler selects up to ten eligible notices, oldest unchecked first, using a schema-scoped overlap lock. Unresolved notices are due after five minutes; accepted notices are checked after twenty-four hours. It isolates recoverable per-notice failures, retains sanitized check history, and raises scoped carrier/invoice/month alerts; acceptance or cancellation clears the corresponding alert. Complete database failure that prevents recording the check still requires runtime recovery. Shared workforce automation invokes the same sweep. PAYROLL_CARRIER_REMITTANCE_ENABLED=false disables default new sending and scheduler startup; configured SMTP is required. Manual recovery can still inspect retained evidence. The scheduler is disabled under NODE_ENV=test; tests call it explicitly with synthetic senders.

The admin delivery panel provides process/recover controls, attempt history, bounded retry time, recovered acceptance and thirty-second automatic refresh after history is requested. Failed refreshes retain displayed evidence with a warning and retry automatically. SMTP acceptance is explicitly distinguished from carrier receipt. Initial authorization remains separate from carrier contact review. Signed provider return intake, bounce/complaint reconciliation and resulting re-delivery/disposition workflows are not yet connected for this category, and production SMTP delivery is unverified.

366. Signed carrier remittance return intake reuses the existing SendGrid raw-byte ECDSA verifier and endpoint, with a separate opaque vortex_carrier_dispatch argument. Only smtp.sendgrid.net uses this metadata. No recipient, employee, bank or invoice details enter provider unique arguments. The shared verification public key remains PAYROLL_SENDGRID_WEBHOOK_PUBLIC_KEY. The intake accepts matched bounce, spamreport and dropped events; delayed returns may lack a provider message ID, but must still match the exact retained dispatch, encrypted recipient hash, employer, template and attempt timestamp. Events without correlation are ignored rather than guessed. Event IDs are durable and immutable; identical retries reuse evidence while conflicting content or message identity rejects the complete batch. Raw signature tampering is rejected before retention. Employer locks precede delivery locks in stable order for mixed carrier/W-2 batches.

Returned notices retain their original SMTP outcome and separate provider event history. The effective state is RETURNED; both application and database guards prevent another attempt. Preview and first-send readiness also refuse the same returned address across new contact revisions. This is deliberately unresolved until a reviewed disposition exists; simply re-reviewing the address does not establish deliverability or authorize a resend. Complaint status takes precedence over bounce, then dropped failure; late SMTP status updates cannot erase those outcomes. The worker detects newly retained event counts immediately, serializes the final check against intake and cannot clear a newly returned alert using an earlier accepted result. The admin panel refreshes return kind, attempt, timestamp and event identity without another manual read. Provider return evidence does not prove carrier payment application, nor does lack of a return establish delivery.

Carrier remittance signed returns are connected to the existing raw-body SendGrid endpoint. Exact dispatch, recipient hash, employer, category/template and attempt-time matching retain immutable bounce, complaint and dropped events. Duplicate callbacks reuse evidence; conflicting events and signatures fail atomically. Returned state overrides prior acceptance, prevents new sends, reopens scoped alerts immediately and appears through the admin panel's automatic refresh. Late SMTP completion preserves returned mail status. 367. Returned carrier remittance notices can now be retired through an internal replacement review. The admin first saves a distinct current carrier-contact revision, then previews the original notice return IDs, all retained return IDs for the proposed address, current contact and prior review identity. A confirmed investigation reference and explicit carrier request to resume delivery are required, including after a complaint. Review snapshots and the request attestation are immutable; exact retries reuse one record, concurrent differing reviews require a fresh preview, and scope/recipient/event/history guards serialize with signed intake. The review closes the original delivery alert, never deletes the return or original SMTP result, and never sends a notice itself.

A separate notice preview and authorization govern the replacement. The new notice retains its address-clearance review identity alongside the encrypted content. ### Assumption 392 — unused PTO cashout terms are separate plan evidence

Paid leave included in plan compensation does not imply that unused-leave cashouts are included. Each treatment may explicitly require further review. Existing revisions without these terms preserve their fingerprints and remain unreviewed for cashouts; no default inclusion or exclusion is inferred. New terms are canonicalized into the immutable plan fingerprint, so the existing source revision checks require fresh dependent reviews after a plan change.

The [IRS final section 415 regulations](https://www.irs.gov/irb/2007-18_IRB) and [Revenue Ruling 2009-32](https://www.irs.gov/irb/2009-39_IRB) distinguish post-severance unused accrued bona fide leave from other severance payments. Applicable plan provisions, the employee's ability to use leave if employment continued, and payment by the later of 2.5 months after severance or the end of the limitation year must be established. Recording the plan terms alone does not establish these employee/payment facts, authorize contributions or enable the currently blocked PTO retirement path. Non-calendar limitation years remain explicitly visible rather than being treated as calendar years.

### Assumption 398 — recordkeeper participant mapping

Hiring admins can now retain a recordkeeper plan identifier and participant identifier for the selected employee and internal retirement plan. This is independently reviewed recordkeeper roster evidence, not automatic enrollment or a provider API verification. Identifiers retain their exact trimmed case and are encrypted with a participant-specific context; the UI/API expose only masks. Short identifiers are fully masked. Keyed, domain-separated fingerprints support exact-request retries and duplicate detection without exposing raw identifiers in database lookup hashes.

The mapping binds current plan revision, provider name, employee name/number, hire date and onboarding cycle. Changed source facts require review. Immutable revisions record VERIFIED or SUSPENDED disposition, with references, actor and history; suspension removes the mapping from remittance use without deleting earlier evidence. The same recordkeeper plan/participant pair cannot be current for two employees within this employer's internal plan. A suspended previous association may be replaced after a new independent review; this does not move previously transmitted contributions or certify a provider transfer.

Concurrent exact requests retain one review; a lost response retries the original request. Differing contents, changed sources and competing revisions are rejected. Database guards enforce employer/employee/plan scope, append-only retention and duplicate exclusions. The admin panel preserves drafts when current evidence changes, supports retry and suspension, and refreshes current status automatically.

Finalized contribution reconciliation now attaches participant mapping status to each positive allocation. A verified mapping exposes only its retained ID, source fingerprint and masks, never the decrypted identifiers. Zero-contribution allocations do not require a participant payment mapping. A changed employee record or suspended mapping requires review while preserving the underlying payroll deductions. Participant matching is separate from contribution delivery.

This initial mapping is for the current reviewed 2026 standard-plan workflow. Actual recordkeeper API connectivity, provider enrollment, broader rehire/history reconciliation, provider-specific identifier namespaces across internal plans, allocation-file submission, timing and funds/provider reconciliation remain unfinished. No provider message, enrollment or payment is sent by these controls.
